## Архивный источник: `docs/decisions/0002-candidate-excluded-ensemble-convergence.md`

# ADR 0002: Исключать accepted candidates из ensemble reference set итеративно

Статус: принято.

Дата: 2026-07-31.

## Проблема

Переменный объект в reference ensemble может частично переносить свой сигнал в калибровку. После первого исключения candidates могут проявиться новые объекты, поэтому одного дополнительного прохода недостаточно.

## Решение

Сохранены два режима:

- fixed mode — предсказуемое заданное число ensemble stages;
- until-converged mode — продолжение до отсутствия новых accepted candidate IDs с отдельным safety cap.

Requested exclusions и actual exclusions разделены: не каждый candidate входил в исходный reference candidate pool.

## Критерий сходимости

После текущего field QC вычисляется:

```text
new_ids = accepted_candidate_ids - cumulative_requested_exclusion_ids
```

При пустом `new_ids` новая calibration не запускается, в history записывается terminal entry с `executed=false`, а stop reason становится `converged`.

## Последствия

Manifest обязан различать terminal convergence check и последнюю реально выполненную calibration. Поэтому actual exclusions верхнего уровня берутся из последней history-записи с `executed=true`.

---

## Архивный источник: `docs/decisions/0003-science-calibration-role.md`

# ADR 0003: отделить internal ensemble от science calibration

Дата: 2026-08-01.

## Контекст

До 0.5.34.0 конечные продукты не имели единого контракта выбора calibration version. Ensemble calibration использовалась одновременно как внутреннее относительное решение и как экспортируемая научная шкала, хотя для фильтров RoboPhot/MASTER она была предварительно привязана к Gaia G.

Отдельная `apply-color-calibration` существовала, но не входила в стандартный pipeline, применялась только к объектам с внешним цветом и могла сформировать неполную по кадрам derived version.

## Решение

- `ensemble` обозначает внутреннюю относительную calibration version.
- `science` обозначает единственную calibration version для конечных QC, light curves и exports.
- При успешной reference/color calibration `science = color`.
- При отсутствии reference coverage, frame ZP или внешнего сервиса `science = ensemble`.
- Color version создаётся только при frame ZP для всех source frames.
- Source measurements без индивидуального reference color сохраняются с fitted pivot color и явными flags; строки без пригодного `mag_inst` также сохраняются с `mag_cal = NULL`.
- Автоматически загруженная reference photometry получает namespace, связанный с identity catalog, чтобы повторный импорт не изменял соответствия, использованные другим полем/версией каталога.
- Выбор reference catalog/band/color задаётся instrument profile.

## Последствия

Конечные продукты больше не должны самостоятельно выбирать «последнюю» calibration version. Manifest явно показывает внутреннюю и научную версии. Pivot-color points пригодны для относительной переменности, но требуют осторожности при интерпретации абсолютного блеска и межсистемных сравнений.

---

## Архивный источник: `docs/decisions/0004-physical-random-error-budget.md`

# ADR 0004: physically decomposed per-epoch random-error budget

Status: accepted and real-data verified in 0.5.37.0.

## Context

The legacy forced-photometry formula treated ADU as electrons and omitted the uncertainty of the annulus-median background estimate. It also had no explicit gain/read-noise, flat/intrapixel or scintillation provenance. Candidate thresholds depend directly on `mag_err_random`, so hidden assumptions made boundary decisions difficult to audit.

## Decision

Grandgousier evaluates a physical variance budget in ADU² and stores every component in measurement flags. Source Poisson noise uses detector gain. Pixel background variance is the maximum of the robust annulus variance and the detector sky-plus-read prediction. The uncertainty of the median background estimator is propagated separately. Optional fractional and scintillation terms are flux-proportional.

The legacy formula is always evaluated in parallel. The selected physical branch receives distinct calibration names. Final internal ensemble reference residuals provide diagnostic A/B validation, but the software does not automatically rescale errors in the same release that introduces the model.

## Consequences

- `mag_err_random` becomes physically interpretable and auditable.
- Candidate membership may change and must be compared explicitly.
- Frame-common absolute calibration uncertainty remains separate in `mag_err_systematic`.
- Unknown detector or telescope metadata produce explicit fallback provenance rather than guessed values.
- A later release may calibrate an error scale or fractional floor only after multiple real datasets are evaluated.

---

## Архивный источник: `docs/decisions/0005-residual-floor-diagnostic-only.md`

# Decision 0005: residual floor remains diagnostic in 0.5.37.1

Status: accepted for multi-series verification.

## Context

The real 0.5.37.0 run shows a magnitude-dependent mismatch: the physical detector/background model is close to normalized scatter unity at the faint end, while bright references retain an approximately additive residual scatter. A global multiplicative rescale would therefore distort the faint-end uncertainties.

## Decision

0.5.37.1 estimates a lower-envelope additive floor and frame-common residual but does not modify `mag_err_random`, ensemble weights, candidate thresholds or accepted-candidate semantics.

The hypothetical effective error is persisted only as provenance:

```text
mag_err_effective = hypot(mag_err_detector, mag_err_epoch_floor)
residual_noise_floor_applied = false
```

Near-threshold objects with two failed criteria are preserved under a diagnostic-only status and never trigger reference exclusion.

## Consequences

- real-data A/B is possible without silently changing science products;
- a later release can choose independent-floor, covariance or instrument-dependent semantics using evidence from several series;
- candidate disappearance at a hard boundary no longer prevents inspection of the underlying light curve.

---

## Архивный источник: `docs/decisions/0006-frame-common-support-and-effective-error-semantics.md`

# Decision 0006: require evidence for frame-common decomposition

## Status

Accepted for 0.5.37.2.

## Decision

A frame-common component is considered supported only when subtracting it improves both the lower-envelope residual floor and the median absolute pairwise residual correlation. A measured after-common floor is not labelled independent when this gate fails.

Hypothetical residual-floor errors are split into:

```text
mag_err_effective_detector_only = hypot(mag_err_detector, floor)
mag_err_effective_total         = hypot(mag_err_random, floor)
```

Candidate A/B uses the total form. Neither form replaces `mag_err_random` in 0.5.37.2.

## Rationale

The real BK Lyn run produced a nonzero frame-common estimate, but its subtraction increased both the lower-envelope floor and pairwise absolute correlation. A nonzero fitted term alone is therefore insufficient evidence for a common physical covariance component.

## Архивный источник: `docs/decisions/0007-candidate-evidence-and-exclusion-growth.md`

# ADR 0007: Межсерийные evidence и ограничение роста candidate exclusions

Статус: принято.
Дата: 2026-08-03.

## Контекст

Три серии BK Lyn подтвердили additive residual floor около 0.024 mag. Одновременно single-series candidate membership оказался нестабилен: в серии `r` 2026-04-02 iterative candidate exclusion потребовал четыре дополнительных ensemble passes и расширил requested exclusions до 31 объектов. Значительная часть новых кандидатов появлялась только после изменения reference set.

Прямое применение residual floor к старым thresholds почти полностью подавляет weak-variable channel. Поэтому residual floor нельзя просто включить в science weights или заменить им candidate significance без новой калибровки порогов.

## Решение

1. Не менять science errors и thresholds в 0.5.38.0.
2. Добавить отдельный cross-series evidence layer по экспортированным light curves, с explicit target-source override для старых exports.
3. Считать положительную синхронную корреляцию независимых фильтров отдельным видом доказательства, не эквивалентным single-band RMS excess.
4. По умолчанию фиксировать candidate-exclusion set после первого accepted snapshot (`initial_only`).
5. Сохранять новые accepted candidates как suppressed diagnostics, а не автоматически удалять их из reference ensemble.
6. Сохранить legacy policy `all` как явную opt-in настройку.
7. Требовать явный target source/object ID для воспроизводимого target provenance; отключённое auto-resolution должно быть заметно в manifest.

## Последствия

- Pipeline становится устойчивее к exclusion cascades.
- Межсерийная evidence доступна без миграции БД и без пересчёта photometry.
- Candidate evidence report зависит от экспортированных per-object CSV; будущая версия может перенести тот же алгоритм в DB-native multi-series product.
- Порог correlations является диагностическим и требует проверки на большем числе полей.

# Grandgousier 0.5.34.0

Дата: 2026-08-01.

## Назначение

Первый этап стабилизации фотометрического продукта: существующая PS1/reference-band color calibration встроена в стандартный field pipeline и становится финальной `science_calibration` для конечных QC-отчётов и кривых блеска.

## Изменения

- Добавлена profile-driven политика `photometric_calibration` для MASTER и RoboPhot.
- Для RoboPhot поддерживаются `g -> PS1 g, g-r`, `r -> PS1 r, g-r`, `i -> PS1 i, r-i`.
- Для MASTER консервативно поддерживаются `R -> PS1 r, g-r` и `I -> PS1 i, r-i`; B/V/unfiltered режимы не получают выдуманного преобразования.
- Цветовая calibration сохраняет все source measurements: при отсутствии внешнего цвета используется fitted pivot color с явными provenance-флагами, а строки без `mag_inst` копируются с `mag_cal = NULL`, а не исчезают.
- Цветовая версия создаётся только при наличии frame ZP для всех source frames; неполная версия не становится science product.
- `run-field-pipeline` может выполнить `apply_color_calibration` после финальной internal ensemble calibration.
- Candidate-excluded ensemble остаётся на внутренней относительной шкале; color term применяется только к финальному science product.
- Добавлена роль `science_calibration`. Все конечные field reports, target/candidate exports и archive light-curve summary используют её.
- `process-archive-path --enable-color-calibration` проверяет существующее reference coverage и при необходимости автоматически получает и импортирует Pan-STARRS DR2.
- Автоматический импорт использует identity-scoped namespace reference catalog, поэтому повторная обработка другого автоматически созданного Gaia-каталога не перезаписывает прежнюю привязку PS1↔Gaia.
- Автоматический запрос можно запретить через `--no-auto-reference-photometry`.
- Ошибка или недостаточное покрытие внешнего каталога не уничтожают прогон: science calibration остаётся последней ensemble version, а manifest сохраняет причину fallback.
- Manifest содержит `reference_photometry_results` и color/science provenance.
- После PS1 calibration object QC не сравнивает итоговую PS1 magnitude с identity Gaia-G, что исключает ложные `LARGE_CATALOG_MAG_RESIDUAL`.

## Совместимость

Миграция БД не требуется. Новые функции выключены по умолчанию и активируются флагом `--enable-color-calibration`.

## Проверки при сборке

```text
python -m compileall -q grandgousier tests scripts = OK
python -m pytest -q = 55 passed, 6 skipped
```

Шесть модулей пропущены в среде сборки из-за отсутствия Astropy и PostgreSQL end-to-end окружения. Реальная проверка automatic PS1 acquisition и final science calibration выполняется на серии BK Lyn в пользовательском окружении.

# Grandgousier 0.5.34.2

Photometric stabilization release: ensemble-preserving absolute color calibration.

## Science model

- replaces final per-frame PS1 ZP recalibration with an object-level transform of the final ensemble calibration;
- fits `reference_mag - median(ensemble_mag) = A + C * (color - color0)` with robust object clipping;
- applies one constant correction per object to all epochs;
- verifies that RMS, MAD and robust peak-to-peak are preserved before writing the target calibration;
- retains the old frame-ZP/color model as diagnostics only.

## Quality gates

A color calibration is activated only when calibrator count, color span, transform residual MAD, pivot-color fraction and shape-preservation thresholds pass. On failure, no target measurements are written and the final ensemble remains the science calibration.

## Errors and QC

- adds `measurements.mag_err_random` and `measurements.mag_err_systematic`;
- keeps `mag_err` as the backward-compatible random per-epoch uncertainty;
- propagates transform coefficient/color/scatter uncertainty as a correlated systematic component;
- light-curve plots and variability metrics use random errors;
- exported products expose random, systematic and backward-compatible total errors;
- same-band PS1 reference magnitude is used for `mag_ref_delta` after color calibration;

# Grandgousier 0.5.34.3

Photometric stabilization hotfix after the real BK Lyn 0.5.34.2 run.

## Candidate selection and products

- missing same-band PS1 reference magnitude is informational and no longer produces `NO_REF_MAG_DELTA` rejection;
- candidate rows expose `reference_residual_status` (`AVAILABLE`, `MISSING_OBJECT_REFERENCE`, `NOT_CONFIGURED`);
- variability candidates are selected on the final internal ensemble calibration;
- accepted candidate light curves are exported from the final science calibration;
- candidate products are built in a staging directory and replace the previous directory as one tree, preventing stale object CSV/JSON/PNG files.

## Absolute transform model selection

The pipeline compares:

```text
reference - ensemble = A
reference - ensemble = A + C * (color - color0)
```

The color model is selected only when all configured criteria pass:

- minimum `|C| / sigma(C)`;
- minimum BIC improvement over offset-only;
- minimum robust residual-MAD improvement.

Otherwise the science calibration applies a shape-preserving offset-only transform. The fitted but rejected color coefficient remains in diagnostics and provenance.

## BK Lyn expectation

The 0.5.34.2 diagnostics give `C = 0.0192 +/- 0.0322`, significance about `0.60`, and BIC improvement about `-3.66`. With RoboPhot defaults, 0.5.34.3 should therefore select `offset_only` while preserving all ensemble shape metrics.

## Database

No new migration is introduced. Databases upgrading from versions before 0.5.34.2 still require:

```text
scripts/migrate_mvp5_34_2_measurement_error_components.sql
```

# Grandgousier 0.5.35.0

Spatial aperture-correction stage between raw forced photometry and the frame zero-point calibration.

## Algorithm

For each frame, bright unsaturated sources measured with the working aperture are remeasured with a larger reference aperture. The stage fits

```text
m_large - m_small = A
m_large - m_small = A + Bx*x_norm + By*y_norm
```

on robustly clipped calibrators. The spatial plane is selected only when it has sufficient calibrators, improves BIC, does not worsen residual MAD, has a meaningful detector-wide amplitude, and remains within the configured correction range. Otherwise the frame uses a robust constant. Frames failing the per-frame quality checks use an identity fallback.

The next frame-ZP stage uses the aperture-corrected calibration only when the global quality gate passes; otherwise the pipeline automatically falls back to the original raw forced-photometry calibration.

## Errors and provenance

The correction-model uncertainty is propagated into `mag_err_random`. Existing `mag_err_systematic` is preserved separately. Raw, aperture-ZP, preliminary and ensemble writers now consistently upsert/copy both error components.

Each corrected measurement records model type, correction, calibrator count, residual scatter, spatial amplitude and fallback reason in `flags`. CalibrationVersion parameters and exported JSON/CSV diagnostics record aggregate and per-frame statistics.

## Products

With the default 3-pixel working aperture and 5-pixel reference aperture, generated calibration names include:

```text
*_apcorr_r3_to_r5_spatial_v1
*_apcorr_r3_to_r5_aperture_g_zp_v1
*_apcorr_r3_to_r5_ensemble_g_*
```

Diagnostics are written to:

```text
<series export>/aperture_correction/aperture_correction_summary.json
<series export>/aperture_correction/aperture_correction_frames.csv
```

## Database

No new migration. The measurement-error columns introduced in 0.5.34.2 remain required.

## Verification

```text
python -m compileall -q grandgousier tests scripts: OK
python -m pytest -q: 73 passed, 6 skipped
```

Skipped modules require Astropy, unavailable in the packaging environment. The real PostgreSQL/Astropy check is the BK Lyn 2026-03-28 i-band series.

# Grandgousier 0.5.35.1

Hotfix for generated calibration-name overflow discovered by the first real 0.5.35.0 BK Lyn aperture-correction run.

## Failure reproduced

Aperture correction completed and passed its quality gate, but the first candidate-excluded ensemble name was 133 characters long while `calibration_versions.name` is `VARCHAR(128)`. PostgreSQL raised `StringDataRightTruncation`; subsequent error logging saw a failed SQLAlchemy transaction and reported `PendingRollbackError`.

## Naming policy

- generated names of 128 characters or fewer remain byte-for-byte unchanged;
- an overlong candidate-excluded suffix first changes from `candidate_excluded` to readable `candx`;
- exceptionally long generated names retain their semantic suffix and receive a deterministic ten-hex SHA-256 token;
- BK Lyn names through candidate iteration 10 fit in 120--127 characters.

## Transaction recovery

The runner calls `Session.rollback()` before persisting failed-step and failed-run diagnostics. Earlier successful steps are already committed independently, so only the failed step transaction is discarded. The manifest/log now retains the original database exception.

## Database

No migration. The existing 128-character constraint remains authoritative.

## Verification

```text
compileall: OK
pytest: 78 passed, 6 skipped
```

# Grandgousier 0.5.35.2

Hotfix for aperture-correction random-error semantics discovered by the completed 0.5.35.1 BK Lyn run.

## Real-run finding

The aperture stage passed its gate (`51 constant`, `9 plane`, `10 identity`; good-frame fraction `0.8571`; median residual MAD `0.02029` mag), and the full pipeline completed. However, the candidate set fell from 16 to 10 and BK Lyn (`object_id=6751`) disappeared even though common-candidate RMS/MAD changed only slightly. The cause was propagation of the full aperture-model prediction uncertainty into every epoch's independent random error.

A constant aperture offset, the plane intercept, and the frame-common model floor are absorbed by the later frame zero point and ensemble offset. They are diagnostics, not independent per-object epoch noise.

## Corrected propagation

- accepted `constant` models add zero aperture uncertainty to `mag_err_random`;
- `identity` fallbacks add zero aperture uncertainty;
- accepted `plane` models propagate only slope covariance relative to the mean normalized position of the aperture calibrators;
- intercept covariance and the residual/sqrt(N) floor remain in the total diagnostic prediction error;
- measurement flags store both `aperture_correction_model_error_total` and `aperture_correction_differential_error`;
- the legacy `aperture_correction_model_error` flag remains as a total-error alias for compatibility;
- calibration parameters record `error_propagation = differential_spatial_only_v1`.

## Diagnostics

Added `median_plane_spatial_peak_to_peak`, which excludes constant models and therefore reports the actual median detector-wide spatial amplitude for selected planes.

## Database

No migration. Existing aperture-corrected and downstream calibration versions are regenerated/reused by name on rerun.

## Verification

```text
compileall: OK
pytest: 81 passed, 6 skipped
```

# 0.5.36.0 — aperture detector/PSF context diagnostics

## Назначение

Версия добавляет диагностический слой для проверки, почему отдельные кадры требуют spatial-plane aperture correction. Численные поправки, критерии выбора plane/constant, propagation `mag_err_random`, candidate thresholds и science photometry не изменяются.

## Новые измерения

Для каждой яркой aperture-калибровочной звезды непосредственно по FITS оцениваются вторые моменты PSF в локальном cutout:

- circularized, major и minor FWHM в пикселях;
- ellipticity `1 - sigma_minor / sigma_major`;
- позиционный угол большой оси в координатах детектора.

Покадрово сохраняются медианные PSF-метрики, header FWHM при наличии, pixel scale, background median/scale, число локальных максимумов, astrometric RMS, detection-ZP MAD, airmass, CCD temperature и время.

## Detector-plane diagnostics

Для выбранной plane и для любой рассчитанной, но отклонённой plane-candidate сохраняются:

- коэффициенты и модуль градиента;
- направление градиента в координатах `+x right, +y increasing detector row`;
- predicted center/corner corrections;
- detector-wide peak-to-peak;
- угол между градиентом и большой осью PSF;
- BIC improvement и residual metrics.

Это позволяет анализировать threshold-edge cases, где plane была рассчитана, но не опубликована.

## Series-level analysis

Строятся:

- circular mean и resultant length направлений выбранных plane;
- quadrant/sign consistency;
- медианное alignment с PSF major axis;
- временной диапазон plane-кадров;
- model-group medians;
- exploratory Spearman associations с FWHM, ellipticity, background, time, airmass, temperature и astrometric diagnostics.

Корреляции маркируются как описательные; автоматический causal вывод запрещён.

## Новые продукты

В каталоге `aperture_correction`:

- `aperture_correction_context_summary.json`;
- `aperture_correction_context_frames.csv`;
- `aperture_correction_context.png` при доступном Matplotlib.

Existing `aperture_correction_summary.json` также содержит `context_analysis` и полный список `frame_contexts`.

## База данных

Новой миграции нет. Краткий summary сохраняется в parameters aperture-correction calibration и в итоговом pipeline `quality_policy`.

## Предварительный сигнал из 0.5.35.3

Ручной post-processing существующего frame CSV (до появления PSF columns) дал для девяти selected plane circular mean направления около `239.8°`, resultant length `0.946`, sign consistency `1.0` и временной диапазон около `95.3` мин. Это мотивирует context diagnostics, но не является доказательством причины spatial term.

# 0.5.36.1 — separated aperture-plane safety semantics

## Purpose

0.5.36.0 showed that the previous plane safety gate mixed the frame-common aperture intercept with detector-dependent spatial variation. For BK Lyn, eight statistically supported plane candidates were rejected only because the total corner correction marginally exceeded 0.5 mag while the differential spatial component remained modest.

## Changes

- Plane safety is evaluated with two independent quantities:
  - maximum absolute spatial deviation from the calibrator pivot, default `0.15 mag`;
  - emergency maximum absolute total correction at detector corners, default `0.75 mag`.
- The historical `0.5 mag` combined edge gate is retained as a shadow decision for A/B provenance.
- Per-frame diagnostics store current and legacy model decisions, pivot correction, total edge amplitude, spatial deviation, and whether the model changed versus legacy semantics.
- Context diagnostics report coherence across all plane candidates, not only selected planes.
- New calibration names use `spatial_v2` and downstream `sv2` tags, preserving 0.5.36.0 calibration rows for comparison.
- Measurement flags record the v2 model-selection semantics and legacy decision.

## Expected BK Lyn effect

From the confirmed 0.5.36.0 diagnostics, frames `193, 204, 210, 216, 221, 226, 232, 234` satisfy the statistical plane criteria and have derived maximum spatial deviations of approximately `0.048–0.089 mag`, but were rejected by the old total-edge threshold. They are expected to be promoted, increasing selected plane frames from 9 to about 17. Frame 249 remains constant because the plane fails BIC/residual criteria independently of the safety gate.

## Compatibility

No database migration is required. Photometry will change on frames whose selected aperture model changes; therefore the 0.5.36.1 rerun must be compared against the accepted 0.5.36.0 products before publication.

# 0.5.37.0 — physical random-error budget

## Added

- physically decomposed aperture-photometry random errors with source Poisson, empirical/detector background, annulus-median estimator, optional fractional floor and optional scintillation terms;
- exact parallel evaluation of the pre-0.5.37 legacy formula;
- `random_error_*` measurement provenance propagated through all calibration branches;
- per-frame and series-level random-error diagnostics;
- normalized-residual validation on final internal ensemble references;
- distinct `errphys_v1` and `errlegacy_v1` calibration branches;
- instrument-profile policy for RoboPhot and explicit fallback policy for MASTER.

## Semantics

The empirical annulus variance is used as a floor over the sky-plus-read detector prediction, not added to it. The annulus-median background-estimation variance is propagated separately with a default factor `pi/2`.

The validation scale recommendation is diagnostic only. 0.5.37.0 does not tune a global error multiplier, fractional floor, candidate threshold or membership policy automatically.

## Compatibility

No new database migration. Candidate membership can change because the selected random error is intentionally different from the legacy approximation.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.37.1.md`

# 0.5.37.1 — residual noise-floor diagnostics

## Added

- lower-envelope estimate of an additive residual floor in magnitude bins;
- frame-common residual estimate from quiet lower-envelope reference stars;
- raw and frame-common-subtracted pairwise residual-correlation diagnostics;
- diagnostic `mag_err_detector`, `mag_err_epoch_floor` and `mag_err_effective` provenance;
- object/frame CSV products and association diagnostics against magnitude, detector position, time, background, astrometry and PSF context;
- hypothetical candidate A/B metrics under the suggested floor;
- `DIAGNOSTIC / NEAR_THRESHOLD_LOW_AMPLITUDE` preservation for objects that miss up to two low-amplitude criteria while remaining within the configured threshold-ratio boundary.

## Semantics

The suggested residual floor is diagnostic only. It is not written into `mag_err_random`, is not used as an ensemble weight and does not change accepted candidate or reference-exclusion semantics. The effective error is stored only as a hypothetical quantity:

```text
mag_err_effective = hypot(mag_err_detector, mag_err_epoch_floor)
residual_noise_floor_applied = false
```

`BORDERLINE` retains its existing one-failed-criterion semantics. The new `DIAGNOSTIC` status preserves near-threshold objects with up to two failed criteria but never creates a candidate origin and never triggers ensemble exclusion.

## Compatibility

No database migration. The selected photometry and physical `mag_err_random` model remain those of 0.5.37.0; only diagnostic flags, products and near-threshold exports are added.

# 0.5.37.2 — residual-floor semantics hotfix

## Fixed

- frame-common subtraction now receives an explicit support status instead of being implicitly treated as an independent-noise decomposition;
- the after-common floor is called independent only if both lower-envelope floor and pairwise absolute-correlation diagnostics improve;
- hypothetical effective uncertainty is split into detector-only and total-random forms;
- candidate residual-floor A/B uses `hypot(mag_err_random, floor)`, preserving differential aperture-correction uncertainty;
- `mag_err_effective` remains as a compatibility alias of the total quantity.

## Support criteria

```text
minimum relative floor reduction:       0.05
minimum absolute-correlation reduction: 0.01
```

The real 0.5.37.1 BK Lyn series is expected to report `NOT_SUPPORTED`, because both metrics worsened after common-mode subtraction.

## Compatibility

No database migration. The residual floor is still diagnostic only and does not modify `mag_err_random`, ensemble weights, candidate thresholds or automatic candidate membership.

# Grandgousier 0.5.38.0

Дата: 2026-08-03.

## Candidate evidence across series

Добавлена команда `candidate-evidence-report`, которая объединяет уже экспортированные candidate products нескольких серий по `source_id` и создаёт:

- `<prefix>.json` — полный отчёт;
- `<prefix>_candidates.csv` — сводка доказательств по объектам;
- `<prefix>_pairs.csv` — попарные межсерийные корреляции.

Для одновременно наблюдавшихся кривых точки сопоставляются one-to-one по ближайшему MJD в заданном временном окне. После вычитания медианы вычисляются Pearson и Spearman correlations. Evidence classes:

- `COHERENT_MULTI_FILTER`;
- `REPEATED_ACCEPTED`;
- `EFFECTIVE_ERROR_PASS`;
- `WEAK_SINGLE_SERIES_ACCEPTED`;
- `DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY`.

Target-объекты получают префикс `TARGET_`; для старых экспортов target можно явно задать повторяемым `--target-source-id`.

## Защита candidate-excluded ensemble от каскада

Добавлена политика `candidate_ensemble_growth_policy`:

- `initial_only` — новый default: первый candidate-excluded pass использует исходный accepted set и target; новые кандидаты последующих пересчётов фиксируются как suppressed diagnostics, но автоматически не расширяют exclusion set;
- `all` — прежнее поведение до 0.5.37.3, при котором новые accepted candidates добавляются на каждой итерации.

Recipe version повышена до `field_pipeline_v4`. Manifest и pipeline provenance сохраняют policy, suppressed IDs, `growth_suppressed` и причину остановки. Это предотвращает самоподдерживающееся разрастание reference exclusions, наблюдавшееся в RoboPhot BK Lyn `r` 2026-04-02.

## Target provenance

`quality_policy.target_provenance_status` различает:

- `EXPLICIT_SOURCE_ID`;
- `EXPLICIT_OBJECT_ID`;
- `AUTO_NEAREST_TO_FIELD_CENTER`;
- `DISABLED_UNRESOLVED`.

`process-archive-path` выдаёт явное предупреждение, если target resolution отключён отрицательным `--target-max-sep-arcsec`, но source/object ID не указан.

## Совместимость

- Миграция БД не требуется.
- Science `mag_err_random`, residual floor, photometric values и candidate thresholds не изменяются.
- Для воспроизведения старого iterative-growth поведения используйте `--candidate-ensemble-growth-policy all`.

- `python -m compileall grandgousier tests scripts`: OK;
- full available test suite: `109 passed, 7 skipped`;
- real export evidence: 3 series, 47 candidate sources, 38 pair rows, 2 multi-filter coherent sources;
- BK Lyn: `TARGET_COHERENT_MULTI_FILTER`, 70 paired epochs, Pearson `0.282834`, Spearman `0.293780`.

- Перед candidate-excluded pass requested exclusions пересекаются с текущим ensemble reference set.

- No-op фиксируется как `stop_status=NO_USABLE_REFERENCE_EXCLUSIONS`, `stop_reason=no_usable_reference_exclusions`, `iterations_executed=0`.
- Initial ensemble остаётся активной calibration; последующая color calibration использует её без изменения.

## Основание

В реальном 0.5.38.3 control run для 66 кадров candidate branch запросила два исключения, но фактически не исключила ни одного reference object и потратила около 63 s на повторную запись и QC.

## Совместимость

Photometric formulas, reference selection thresholds, candidate criteria и database schema не меняются. Миграция БД не требуется.

## Проверка

- `python -m compileall grandgousier`: OK.
- `python -m pytest -q`: 125 passed, 8 skipped в среде упаковки.
- Пользовательский полный набор 0.5.38.3 до patch: 161 passed, 1 skipped.

# Grandgousier 0.5.39.3

Hotfix for the managed PostgreSQL migration runner introduced in 0.5.39.1.

## Fixed

`migrate-db` used SQLAlchemy `Connection.exec_driver_sql()` with raw migration text. Psycopg's `pyformat` placeholder parser treats a literal `%` in ordinary PostgreSQL SQL (for example `LIKE 'forced_aperture_%'`) as the start of a DBAPI placeholder and rejected the 0.5.39.2 migration before PostgreSQL could execute it.

The runner now escapes literal percent characters at the DBAPI boundary for `format` and `pyformat` drivers. Migration files remain normal PostgreSQL SQL and their checksums are unchanged.

The failed 0.5.39.2 attempt is transaction-safe: PostgreSQL rolls back the migration DDL and the ledger row is not inserted. Rerun `python -m grandgousier.cli migrate-db` after installing this hotfix.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.39.6.md`

# MVP5.39.6 — immutable artifact registry and run-addressed export snapshots

Patch over Grandgousier 0.5.39.5.

This patch implements Phase B2 of the data-model refactor. It does not change
photometric formulas or measurement materialization.

## Database model

Two additive tables are introduced:

- `artifacts` — one immutable file artifact with pipeline/calibration/series
  provenance, type/role/format, URI, optional compatibility publication URI,
  size and SHA-256;
- `artifact_publications` — mutable publication/head pointer from a stable
  compatibility path to the current immutable artifact.

The current ORM schema contract therefore contains 29 tables.

## Run-addressed exports

The existing per-series export directory remains the compatibility publication.
Files created or refreshed by a recorded field-pipeline run are copied after the
run into a sibling run-addressed tree:

```text
exports/
  <calibration-prefix>/        # compatibility publication
  runs/
    <pipeline_run_id>_<run_uid>/
      ... immutable snapshot files ...
```

Only files changed relative to the pre-run publication snapshot are copied, so
stale files from an older compatibility publication are not attributed to the
new run. Candidate directories are handled recursively.

Pipeline logs are already run-addressed under `logs/pipeline_runs/...` and are
registered in place after the final run log event, so the stored checksum covers
the completed log.

The archive orchestrator also snapshots newly fetched reference-photometry CSV,
per-series light-curve summary JSON, and a single-run `process-archive-path`
manifest into the corresponding immutable run tree. Multi-run manifests are
left for the DB-native batch ownership introduced in Phase B3.

## Registry semantics

For one `(pipeline_run_id, uri)` the content is immutable. Re-registering the
same checksum is idempotent. Different content at the same run URI is rejected
rather than rewriting provenance.

A compatibility publication path may move to a newer artifact through
`artifact_publications`; the older artifact row and checksum remain unchanged.

## CLI

```powershell
python -m grandgousier.cli show-artifacts --pipeline-run-id <ID>
python -m grandgousier.cli verify-artifacts --pipeline-run-id <ID>
```

`verify-artifacts` recomputes size/SHA-256 and returns a non-zero exit status for
missing or changed files.

## Migration

```powershell
python -m grandgousier.cli migrate-db
python -m grandgousier.cli schema-status
```

Expected newest migration:

`mvp5_39_6_artifact_registry`

No existing files are backfilled automatically. The registry becomes populated
by subsequent recorded runs.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.12

Performance patch for repeated calibration-analysis snapshots used by Object QC and field diagnostics.

## Changes

- Added incremental color-calibration analysis snapshots. When the color calibration is a direct child of an ensemble calibration already cached by the field pipeline, the color QC snapshot is derived from the cached parent plus normalized `calibration_iteration_objects` color terms.
- The derived snapshot reuses immutable frame/object metadata and measurement geometry, while rebuilding only color-dependent measurement/scatter state.
- Added `analysis_snapshot_derived` and `analysis_snapshot_materialization_source` telemetry to Object QC results.
- Converted legacy/science photometry readers from full ORM hydration to scalar/mapping queries.
- Converted base/science reconstruction row loading from full ORM hydration to scalar/mapping queries. This reduces the remaining normalized ensemble snapshot load cost as well as verification/read-path overhead.
- No database migration is required.

## Expected effect

For the standard MASTER control pipeline, the second color-calibrated Object QC pass should report an incremental snapshot (`calibration_analysis_snapshot_v3_incremental_color`) with `analysis_snapshot_db_load = 0`. The first ensemble QC still constructs its own snapshot, but its base-photometry read now uses the scalar loader.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.13

## Science measurement index cleanup

This release reduces PostgreSQL write amplification for the retained final
`science_measurements` product.

The table previously maintained six btree structures per inserted science row:
its surrogate primary key, the natural science UNIQUE constraint, an exact
duplicate of that UNIQUE index, and stand-alone indexes on `object_id`,
`frame_id`, and `base_measurement_id`.

The steady-state archive workload is immutable and calibration-scoped.  The
schema now keeps three write-time index structures:

1. primary key on `science_measurement_id`;
2. UNIQUE `(calibration_version_id, object_id, frame_id)` for object/light-curve
   access and idempotency;
3. `(calibration_version_id, frame_id, object_id)` for frame-scoped reads.

The migration is data-preserving and does not rewrite science rows.  It trades
fast stand-alone parent deletion (`objects`, `frames`, base `measurements`) for
lower steady-state materialization cost.  Such deletes are not part of normal
archive processing.

No photometric equations or reconstruction logic changed.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.14

## Compact science flags

This release removes duplicated immutable BASE JSONB provenance from newly
materialized `science_measurements` rows.

The PostgreSQL server reconstruction path now writes only science-specific flag
content to `science_measurements.flags`:

- normalized science provenance identifiers;
- reference/color-calibration summary fields;
- residual-noise/effective-error annotations.

Detector/catalog/per-epoch flags remain only on the immutable BASE
`measurements` row addressed by `base_measurement_id`.

Science readers reconstruct the historical public flag view transparently as
`BASE || SCIENCE`, with science keys taking precedence. This is implemented in:

- calibration photometry views;
- calibration reconstruction reads of an already materialized science layer;
- light-curve SQL readers, including catalog/source filters and Object QC joins.

The server reconstruction CTE also stops carrying the full BASE JSONB object
through each calibration stage. It extracts only the two BASE flag values needed
by reconstruction (`catalog_name` and `random_error_physical_mag_err`) and keeps
those as scalar columns.

New telemetry for the fast path reports:

- `science_flags_strategy = COMPACT_NORMALIZED_SUMMARY_V2`;
- `materialization_source = POSTGRESQL_SERVER_RECONSTRUCTION_V2_COMPACT_FLAGS`.

Existing science rows remain readable because the effective flag merge is
backward-compatible with rows that already contain a full accumulated flag
payload.

No database migration is required. Photometric scalar equations and normalized
calibration terms are unchanged.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.40.15.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.15

## Compact science materialization source hotfix

This release fixes the PostgreSQL server reconstruction failure introduced by
0.5.40.14.

`science_measurements.materialization_source` is defined as `VARCHAR(48)`, while
0.5.40.14 wrote the 49-character marker
`POSTGRESQL_SERVER_RECONSTRUCTION_V2_COMPACT_FLAGS`. PostgreSQL therefore aborted
the final science `INSERT .. SELECT` with `StringDataRightTruncation` before any
science rows could be committed.

The marker is shortened to the semantically equivalent 43-character value:

`POSTGRESQL_SERVER_RECONSTRUCTION_V2_COMPACT`

The compact-flags implementation, science-row contents, flag reconstruction,
photometric equations, and database schema are otherwise unchanged.

A regression assertion keeps the server materialization marker within the ORM
`String(48)` contract.

No database migration is required.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.16

## PostgreSQL science materialization profiler

This release adds an opt-in diagnostic mode for the normalized PostgreSQL
science materialization path. It is intended to separate the remaining cost of
server-side reconstruction from heap/index/FK/WAL insertion cost.

Enable it with `--diagnose-science-materialization` on `run-field-pipeline` or
`process-archive-path`, or with `-DiagnoseScienceMaterialization` in the TESS
batch PowerShell controller.

For the server `INSERT .. SELECT` path the diagnostic run records:

- `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, WAL, VERBOSE, SETTINGS, FORMAT JSON)` for the
  actual INSERT. The INSERT is profiled in place and is not executed twice.
- The same EXPLAIN instrumentation for the reconstruction SELECT with the INSERT
  removed. This is intentionally executed after the INSERT so it cannot warm the
  cache before the primary insertion measurement.
- Condensed top-node, buffer, WAL and trigger summaries plus the full JSON plans.
- Science-row count, average/min/max physical row size, compact flags size, and
  total heap/index relation sizes.

The data is stored in the `materialize_science_measurements` pipeline step
`result_json.diagnostics`. Normal runs are unchanged and incur no profiling
overhead. Diagnostic runs are expected to be slower because they additionally
execute the reconstruction SELECT and row-size scan.

No photometric equations, science-row semantics, or database schema are changed.
No database migration is required.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.40.17.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.17

## PostgreSQL reconstruction plan stabilization

This release targets the pathological PostgreSQL plan observed by the
`--diagnose-science-materialization` run on the MASTER control dataset.

The diagnostic run showed that server-side science reconstruction was dominated
by planner-induced nested loops rather than heap/index/FK/WAL insertion cost:

- approximately 3.58 million scans of one `calibration_frame_terms` iteration;
- approximately 71.6 million shared-buffer hits in that node;
- approximately 232.8 million rows rejected by its join filter;
- FK trigger time remained below one second for the full 50,565-row product.

### Changes

- Every server reconstruction boundary (`s0`, aperture correction, aperture ZP,
  ensemble, and color calibration) is now declared `AS MATERIALIZED`.
- Per-frame term joins now include the exact normalized `term_kind`:
  - `APERTURE_CORRECTION`
  - `APERTURE_ZP`
  - `ENSEMBLE_OFFSET`
- The complete unique key
  `(calibration_iteration_id, frame_id, term_kind)` is therefore visible to the
  planner at each frame-term lookup.
- Telemetry reports
  `reconstruction_strategy=POSTGRESQL_CTE_MATERIALIZED_V2`.

The photometric equations, normalized calibration terms, compact science flags,
and science schema are unchanged. No database migration is required.

---

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.18

## Forced-aperture photometry performance diagnostics

This release adds opt-in internal phase profiling for `run_forced_photometry` so
that the next optimization is based on measured costs rather than aggregate step
wall time.

Enable profiling with:

- `--diagnose-forced-photometry` for `run-field-pipeline` and `process-archive-path`;
- `--diagnose-performance` for the direct `run-forced-photometry` command;
- `-DiagnoseForcedPhotometry` for the TESS PowerShell batch controller.

The profiler records aggregate timing for frame/link selection, FITS loading,
object identity resolution, aperture measurement, diagnostic/row construction,
COPY staging/merge/finalization, final statistics and commit.  The aperture
kernel is further split into geometry/mask construction, background+flux
estimation, random-error model calculation and magnitude finalization.

Per-frame timing distributions (sum/mean/median/p90/max) and throughput metrics
are persisted in the `run_forced_photometry` pipeline step result JSON.  The
high-frequency per-source timers are active only when diagnostics are requested,
so normal production runs retain the previous hot path.

Photometric equations, persistence semantics and database schema are unchanged.
No database migration is required.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.19

## BASE photometry link prefetch and direct COPY fast path

This release removes two measured overheads from fresh immutable BASE photometry.

`frame_catalog_links` are now prefetched for the complete selected-frame scope
instead of executing one ORM join query per frame.  The new reader uses two
compact scalar queries: one for link geometry and one for the unique catalog
sources, then groups the rows by frame in memory while preserving per-frame
ordering and `limit_links` semantics.

Fresh immutable BASE generations with zero pre-existing measurements now bypass
the temporary staging table and `INSERT .. SELECT` publication step.  Buffered
rows are streamed directly into `measurements` with PostgreSQL COPY.  Existing,
partial, reusable and legacy targets retain the previous staging + UPSERT path.
Transaction rollback continues to provide atomic failure handling.

New result telemetry includes:

- `link_read_strategy=BULK_SCALAR_2QUERY_V1`;
- `prefetched_link_rows`;
- `measurement_write_strategy`;
- `direct_copy_rows`, `direct_copy_batches`, `direct_copy_sec`;
- `timings_sec.postgres_direct_copy` when forced-photometry diagnostics are enabled.

Photometric equations and database schema are unchanged. No database migration
is required.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.21

Hotfix for calibration-performance diagnostics in `process-archive-path`.

`0.5.40.20` exposed `--diagnose-calibration-performance` in the CLI and passed it from `cmd_process_archive_path`, but `grandgousier.archive.auto_process.process_archive_path()` did not yet accept the corresponding keyword. Archive processing therefore failed before creating a new pipeline run with:

```text
TypeError: process_archive_path() got an unexpected keyword argument 'calibration_performance_diagnostics'
```

This release:

- adds `calibration_performance_diagnostics: bool = False` to `process_archive_path()`;
- forwards it to `FieldPipelineConfig`;
- records the switch in the per-series command provenance;
- adds a regression test covering the archive-path forwarding contract;
- clears the mutable manifest before a fresh EXECUTION attempt, after recovery handling, so an early process failure cannot inherit status/points/pipeline_run_id from the previous successful manifest.

No database migration is required. Photometry and calibration algorithms are unchanged.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.40.22.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.22

## Calibration row-reuse fast paths

Real MASTER profiling in 0.5.40.20/21 showed that database/reconstruction row
loading, not calibration mathematics, dominated both remaining calibration
stages.  On the 66-frame control field, `apply_aperture_correction` spent about
7.15 s loading 54,268 source measurements, while `apply_color_calibration`
spent about 4.96 s loading diagnostic rows and another 4.72 s loading the same
50,565 ENSEMBLE rows again for application.

This release removes both avoidable costs without changing photometric formulas.

### Color calibration

`apply_color_calibration` now loads one ordered superset of source rows,
reference photometry, frame metadata and ObjectQc support.  Diagnostics derive
their reference-qualified subset from that snapshot in memory, and application
reuses the same rows instead of reconstructing the ENSEMBLE calibration a
second time.  `limit` semantics remain equivalent to the old independent
queries: filtering occurs before the limit for each derived view.

Telemetry exposes:

- `measurement_row_read_strategy = SHARED_SUPERSET_SINGLE_LOAD_V1`;
- `shared_measurement_rows`;
- `timings_sec.load_shared_color_rows`;
- zero DB time in `diagnostics_load_rows` and `load_application_rows` on the
  shared path, with the small in-memory filtering costs reported separately.

Direct `compute_color_calibration_diagnostics` calls keep the original loader
path and behavior.

### Aperture correction

The old `select(Measurement, Frame)` source load hydrated full ORM entities and
repeated all frame columns for every source measurement.  It is replaced by a
scalar measurement query containing only fields used by the correction and a
second compact lookup that fetches each selected frame once.  SQLAlchemy Row
objects preserve the attribute-based numerical code, so model selection,
remeasurement and output semantics are unchanged.

Telemetry exposes
`source_read_strategy = SCALAR_MEASUREMENTS_PLUS_FRAME_LOOKUP_V1`.

No database migration is required.

---

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.40.23.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.23

## Detection and detection↔catalog throughput fast paths

Real MASTER run 99 left two adjacent stages as the next clear target:

- `detect_sources`: 11.56 s for 66 frames / 27,225 detections;
- `match_detections_to_catalog`: 7.87 s for 27,225 detections against 54,268 frame-catalog links, producing 20,018 matches.

The old implementation still performed database work per frame and hydrated full
ORM objects in the cross-match reader. This release removes that overhead while
keeping the detection thresholding, centroiding, aperture measurement, sky
cross-match radius, and greedy one-to-one acceptance semantics unchanged.

### Source detection

For PostgreSQL/psycopg runs, detection rows are streamed into a transaction-local
COPY staging table while FITS frames are processed. After all successful frames
are known, `replace_existing` uses one set-based DELETE over those frame IDs and
one server-side `INSERT .. SELECT` publishes the staged detections. This replaces
66 per-frame DELETEs and 66 parameter-heavy INSERT batches on the run-99 control
series with one DELETE, buffered COPY, and one publication statement.

The greedy minimum-separation selector no longer scans every previously accepted
source with Python `any(...)`. A uniform spatial hash inspects only neighboring
cells while preserving candidate order and the exact legacy strict
`distance < min_separation` rejection rule. A regression test compares the new
selector with the historical brute-force algorithm over 5,000 synthetic
candidates and boundary cases.

Result telemetry now exposes the write strategy, COPY batch counts, delete batch
count, and phase timings for FITS reads, detection kernel, row construction,
staging, publication, and finalization.

### Detection↔catalog matching

Detections and frame-catalog inputs are prefetched once for the complete selected
frame scope using two compact scalar queries. The old path issued one
`SourceDetection` ORM SELECT and one `CatalogSource + FrameCatalogLink` ORM SELECT
for every frame. The catalog source objects used by the numerical matcher are
also reused in memory across frames.

On PostgreSQL, match rows use a transaction-local COPY staging table followed by
one `INSERT .. SELECT .. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`. `replace_existing` can therefore
use one set-based DELETE over successful frames. Per-frame `FrameQc` writes are
collected and emitted in PostgreSQL-safe multi-row UPSERT batches instead of one
UPSERT per frame. Frame quality-flag merge semantics are unchanged.

New match telemetry includes `read_strategy=BULK_SCALAR_2QUERY_V1`, prefetched
row counts, COPY/write strategy, DB phase timings, matching/QC CPU timings, and
batch counts.

No database migration is required.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.28

## Color calibration hybrid reconstruction fast path

The 0.5.40.27 all-in-one PostgreSQL reader was scientifically correct but slower on the MASTER control series (`apply_color_calibration` 6.947 s -> 9.330 s). The profile showed 7.234 s in `load_shared_color_rows`, of which 6.954 s was the server query.

0.5.40.28 keeps normalized scalar photometry reconstruction in PostgreSQL, but moves low-cardinality decoration back to one-time bulk Python joins:

- the server query no longer performs the per-epoch `ObjectQc` lateral lookup;
- the server query no longer joins the wide reference-photometry relation;
- only the BASE flag keys required by color semantics are transferred (`catalog_name`, `source_id`, saturation flags);
- the server query no longer sorts the fully decorated ~50k-row payload; ordering is restored after decoration in Python;
- reference photometry and ObjectQc are loaded once for the unique source/object IDs and cached during row decoration.

The fast path remains restricted to normalized-only color products. Legacy/materialized color calibration keeps the authoritative full-row path.

No database migration is required.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.29

Object-QC analysis snapshot fast path for normalized ENSEMBLE calibrations.

The field runner can now build its reusable calibration analysis snapshot with PostgreSQL server-side normalized reconstruction instead of reconstructing the complete ~50k-row calibration chain in Python. The PostgreSQL wire payload is intentionally narrow: scalar photometry required by QC, selected BASE rejection/error flags, and ENSEMBLE object membership state. Public snapshot callers retain the previous storage-independent path unless they explicitly opt in.

The fast path is conservative: PostgreSQL only, normalized-only ENSEMBLE targets, and only chains supported by the existing science-materialization server reconstruction engine. Legacy materialized ENSEMBLE rows and unsupported chains fall back unchanged.

New Object-QC timings expose `analysis_snapshot_server_plan`, `analysis_snapshot_server_query`, and `analysis_snapshot_server_decode`. Successful runs report `analysis_snapshot_materialization_source=RECONSTRUCTED_NORMALIZED_POSTGRES_COMPACT`.

No database migration is required. Photometric formulas, QC thresholds, candidate semantics, color calibration, and science materialization are unchanged.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.3

D3 compact intermediate-calibration cutover.

- The recorded field pipeline now defaults to `NORMALIZED_ONLY` intermediate calibration storage.
- `APERTURE_CORRECTION`, `APERTURE_ZP`, `ENSEMBLE`, candidate-excluded ensemble passes, and `COLOR_CALIBRATION` no longer write full `measurements` layers by default.
- Immutable `BASE_PHOTOMETRY` remains fully materialized in `measurements`.
- Final science photometry remains fully materialized in `science_measurements`.
- Adds `--materialize-intermediate-calibrations` as an explicit compatibility/debug switch restoring the former full-layer behavior.
- Adds a storage-independent calibration photometry view used by downstream calibration, object QC, field QC, target resolution, color calibration, light-curve readers, aperture-stability lookup, and random-error validation.
- Compact intermediate stages are reconstructed from base photometry plus `calibration_iterations`, `calibration_frame_terms`, and `calibration_iteration_objects`.
- `verify-calibration-terms` treats normalized-only calibrations as a valid compact representation instead of requiring legacy target rows.
- `verify-calibration-reconstruction` can compare a compact final calibration against `science_measurements` when the legacy final `measurements` layer is absent.
- Residual-noise-floor provenance is stored once in normalized iteration metrics and projected onto reconstructed row flags; compatibility mode still annotates legacy measurement flags.
- Science materialization no longer requires a legacy shadow layer in compact mode; compatibility/debug mode retains shadow comparison.
- No database migration is required: 0.5.40.3 changes storage policy and readers on top of the 0.5.40.2 schema.

The intended steady-state heavy-row count for the main science chain is therefore approximately `BASE + SCIENCE` rather than `BASE + APERTURE_CORRECTION + APERTURE_ZP + ENSEMBLE(+iterations) + COLOR`. Existing historical measurement generations are not deleted by this release.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.30

Performance patch for the detection branch, with rollback of the unsuccessful
0.5.40.29 Object-QC snapshot experiment.

## Detection fast path

- `pre_photometry_frame_qc` can keep its exact local-maxima coordinates,
  background median, and MAD sigma as a transient in-process detection seed.
- The seed is never written to `frames.quality_flags`; persistent QC remains
  compact and unchanged.
- The handoff is accepted only when threshold sigma, path, file size, and
  nanosecond mtime still match. Otherwise source detection falls back to the
  normal image-statistics path.
- `detect_sources` therefore avoids recomputing the same robust background and
  local-maxima pass that immediately preceded it in the standard field runner.
- Pixel-to-sky conversion for accepted detections is vectorized into one WCS
  call per frame, with automatic fallback to the historical per-source calls
  if a WCS implementation rejects vector input.
- Detection result telemetry now includes transient seed counters and a
  `kernel_timings_sec` phase breakdown (`background_stats`/seed decode,
  `local_maxima`, `score_sort`, `min_separation`, `centroid`, `wcs_transform`,
  and `aperture_measure_and_finalize`).

## Object-QC rollback

The 0.5.40.29 PostgreSQL compact Object-QC snapshot path is removed from the
field runner. Real MASTER benchmarking showed 5.266 s -> 5.407 s, while the
server query itself still cost about 3.48 s. The storage-independent Python
normalized reconstruction remains the default and authoritative path.

## Compatibility

No database migration is required. Detection selection, thresholding,
min-separation semantics, centroiding, aperture photometry, and saved source
rows are unchanged; only already-computed transient pre-QC data and batched WCS
execution are reused.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.4

D4a PostgreSQL-native final science materialization.

- Final `science_measurements` writes now use PostgreSQL `COPY` into a temporary, unindexed staging table followed by one server-side `INSERT ... SELECT`.

Hotfix for the runner wiring regression in 0.5.40.39.

The snapshot-reuse argument intended for `apply_color_calibration()` was accidentally attached to the preceding `apply_aperture_correction()` call. # Grandgousier 0.5.40.43

Performance patch for the normalized BASE -> APERTURE_CORRECTION -> APERTURE_ZP -> ENSEMBLE -> Object-QC path.

## Shared downstream seed after APERTURE_ZP

In 0.5.40.42 the ENSEMBLE step widened its BASE query so that Object-QC could reuse those rows. This removed the Object-QC query, but moved a substantial read cost into ENSEMBLE.

0.5.40.43 moves the handoff one stage earlier. When the standard normalized pipeline is active, APERTURE_ZP reads the rich compact BASE scalar subset once and keeps two transient products in memory:

- the rich BASE scalar rows required by `CalibrationAnalysisSnapshot` / Object-QC;
- the already APERTURE_ZP-calibrated compact `(object_id, frame_id, mag_inst, mag_cal, catalog_name)` rows required by ENSEMBLE.

ENSEMBLE consumes the compact APERTURE_ZP rows without another BASE query or APERTURE/APERTURE_ZP reconstruction. It then forwards the same rich BASE seed to Object-QC using the existing 0.5.40.42 transient seed cache.

Candidate-excluded ENSEMBLE iterations reuse the same APERTURE_ZP seeds as well.

All seed payloads are transient Python attributes and are not persisted to calibration products, manifests, or `pipeline_run_steps.result_json`.

Fallback behavior is unchanged for materialized intermediates, unsupported storage/chains, dry runs, and standalone calibration calls.

No database migration is required.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.40.44.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.44

Performance patch for PostgreSQL final science materialization.

## Compact frame-term maps for server reconstruction

The V5 science materializer kept the immutable BASE rows and each normalized
frame stage as separate MATERIALIZED CTEs.  This protected the query from the
old pathological frame-term nested loops, but the production MASTER diagnostic
still showed several thousand temp blocks written while ~50k-wide state was
materialized repeatedly through APERTURE_CORRECTION, APERTURE_ZP and ENSEMBLE.

0.5.40.44 keeps only the BASE state materialized.  Each normalized frame-term
set is small (normally one row per frame), so it is aggregated once into a
JSONB `frame_id -> term` map.  The APERTURE_CORRECTION, APERTURE_ZP and ENSEMBLE
stages decode the appropriate map entry with `jsonb_to_record` and remain
`NOT MATERIALIZED`.  COLOR_CALIBRATION retains the proven V5 object-map lookup.

The scalar reconstruction formulas, catalog eligibility, accepted-term gates,
color payload, residual-noise annotations and final science row schema are
unchanged.  Unsupported/non-PostgreSQL paths retain the existing fallbacks.

The production strategy marker is now:

`POSTGRESQL_CTE_FRAME_MAP_COLOR_MAP_INLINE_V7`

and the per-row provenance marker is:

`POSTGRESQL_SERVER_RECONSTRUCTION_V7_MAP`.

No database migration is required.

A dedicated XeLaTeX project is introduced under `docs/user_manual_ru/`.
The manual is user-facing and separate from developer context/release history.  Its structure starts with a quick start and then expands into installation, workflow concepts, single-series photometry, CLI workflows, products/QC, batch processing, and chapters marking the planned multi-series and raw-reduction stages.

The LaTeX sources compile with XeLaTeX; generated PDF/build files are not part of the patch and are not authoritative source files.

## Documentation maintenance contract

Future Grandgousier patches must explicitly evaluate documentation impact.  If a patch changes CLI, parameters, workflow, migrations, user-visible products, or scientific interpretation exposed to the user, the affected `docs/user_manual_ru/` sources must be updated in the same patch-only archive.  Internal optimizations with no user-contract change do not require substantive manual edits.

This rule is recorded in `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/README.md`, `context/project_state.yaml`, and `docs/user_manual_ru/README.md`.  `scripts/build_context_bundle.py` now includes the manual README so the rule is carried into future-chat context bundles.

## Current project direction

Developer current-state/next-task documents are refreshed to reflect the current architecture: Stage 2 single-series photometry is the mature/verified component; Stage 3 inter-series calibration/object history is the next development priority; Stage 1 raw-to-processed FITS reduction remains open.

No database migration and no scientific algorithm change are included.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.5

D4b PostgreSQL-native BASE_PHOTOMETRY write path.

- Forced-aperture `measurements` are buffered in moderate Python chunks and streamed with psycopg3 `COPY FROM STDIN` into one transaction-local, unindexed temporary staging table.
- One server-side `INSERT ... SELECT` publishes the complete staged BASE layer. Fresh immutable generations use a direct insert; compatibility/partial targets with pre-existing rows retain `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` behavior.
- The PostgreSQL path no longer executes one large parameterized measurement UPSERT per frame.
- Catalog-source → archive-object IDs are cached for the full forced-photometry run instead of being resolved again on every frame.
- Fresh BASE generations skip the redundant post-write full measurement/JSONB readback used only to rebuild diagnostics that were already accumulated while measuring. Existing/partial targets keep the persisted-diagnostics reload.
- Adds BASE write telemetry: `write_strategy`, `staging_rows`, `staging_copy_batches`, `staging_copy_sec`, `insert_select_sec`, `write_finalize_sec`, object-identity cache hits/misses, pre-existing row count, and whether persisted diagnostics were reloaded.
- Non-PostgreSQL/test backends retain the previous bounded SQLAlchemy UPSERT fallback.
- No database migration and no photometric formula change.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.6

D4c catalog-to-frame matching hot-path optimization.

- Projects the full working catalog through each frame WCS in one vectorized Astropy call instead of one Python/Astropy WCS call per source. A scalar compatibility fallback remains for unusual WCS implementations.
- Reuses the indexed `frames.header_json` WCS/header metadata when complete, avoiding repeated FITS header opens; older/incomplete cached headers fall back to the FITS file.
- Computes the working reference magnitude once per catalog source instead of repeatedly decoding `ref_mags` during filtering, sorting, and row construction.
- PostgreSQL writes now buffer several projected frames at a time, stream frame-catalog links through psycopg `COPY FROM STDIN` into one transaction-local staging table, and publish them with one `INSERT ... SELECT`. `replace_existing` performs one bulk delete for successfully projected frames before a conflict-free direct insert.
- Non-PostgreSQL/test backends retain bounded SQLAlchemy UPSERT behavior.
- Adds stage telemetry for source loading, header/WCS construction, vectorized/scalar projection, row construction, delete, COPY, merge, and finalization.
- No database migration and no catalog-selection/footprint formula change.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.7

Performance patch for the retained final science materialization.

## PostgreSQL server-side science reconstruction

When the main pipeline runs in normalized-only mode (`--materialize-intermediate-calibrations` is not enabled), PostgreSQL now materializes `science_measurements` directly from immutable BASE photometry plus normalized calibration terms using one `WITH ... INSERT ... SELECT` statement.

The standard normalized chain supports:

- `APERTURE_CORRECTION`;
- `APERTURE_ZP`;
- `ENSEMBLE`;
- `COLOR_CALIBRATION`.

The previous Python reconstruction + streaming COPY path remains the compatibility fallback for shadow/legacy runs, non-PostgreSQL backends, and unsupported future/custom calibration stages.

## Compact final flags

`science_measurements.flags` no longer accumulates duplicated frame-level provenance from every intermediate stage on the server fast path. It retains the immutable BASE measurement flags and adds only compact final science information needed by current readers:

- normalized science/base product identity;
- color-system summary and per-object reference/color application values when color calibration is present;
- residual-noise-floor/effective-error fields when available.

Full calibration provenance remains authoritative in `calibration_iterations`, `calibration_frame_terms`, `calibration_iteration_objects`, and `calibration_versions`.

No database migration is required.

## Telemetry

`materialize_science_measurements` now reports:

- `write_strategy=POSTGRESQL_SERVER_INSERT_SELECT` on the fast path;
- `reconstruction_strategy=POSTGRESQL_CTE_NORMALIZED_V1`;
- `science_flags_strategy=BASE_PLUS_NORMALIZED_SUMMARY_V1`;
- `insert_select_sec` for the combined server reconstruction/write;
- existing `total_sec` / `finalize_sec` fields.

`verify-calibration-reconstruction` and `verify-science-materialization` remain the numerical parity gates after the run.

# Grandgousier 0.5.40.8

Hotfix for the PostgreSQL server-side science reconstruction introduced in 0.5.40.7.

## Python 3.11 compatibility

The SQL builder used an f-string expression containing a backslash escape in `",\n        ".join(ctes)`. Python 3.11 rejects this syntax during module import with `SyntaxError: f-string expression part cannot include a backslash`.

The joined CTE fragment is now computed before the f-string and interpolated through a simple variable. This is syntax-compatible with Python 3.11 and does not change the generated SQL, reconstruction mathematics, materialization strategy, or database schema.

No database migration is required.

Existing `test_postgres_server_reconstruction_builds_direct_insert_select` exercises the affected builder after import and serves as the regression gate.

# Grandgousier 0.5.41.1

Stage 3 clean-rebuild foundation before M1/M2.

## Added

- `reset-derived-data --scope stage2 --all-series`:
  - dry-run audit by default;
  - destructive execution requires `--execute --yes`;
  - explicit transactional PostgreSQL `TRUNCATE` boundary without `CASCADE`;
  - preserves archive/field/series/catalog/reference/object identity and migration ledger;
  - resets series/field runtime status and Stage-2 frame QC/runtime state;
  - identity sequences deliberately continue.
- `audit-field-catalog-identity`:
  - reports catalog namespace coverage for every series in a field;
  - groups repeated series by `field + instrument_unit + filter`;
  - identifies `READY_SHARED_NAMESPACE`, missing links, extra namespaces, or reconciliation requirement.
- PowerShell batch runner `-FreshStart` mode:
  - does not import legacy `state.csv` into a newly rebuilt batch;
  - does not recover old successful manifests;
  - intended for a full archive rebuild after `reset-derived-data`.

## Reset boundary

Derived/operational tables are removed, including measurements, science measurements, normalized calibration terms/generations, detections/matches, frame/object QC, pipeline/batch history, artifact registry rows, event coverage tied to derived measurements/detections, and early inter-series offsets.

Preserved tables include `frames`, `fields`, `field_series`, `field_series_frames`, `instrument_units`, `catalog_sources`, reference photometry, `objects`, event identity/object links and `schema_migrations`.

The reset does not delete FITS files, manifests, reports, exports or logs from the filesystem.

## Stage 3 workflow

The immediate real-data sequence is now:

1. backup database;
2. dry-run reset audit;
3. transactional derived-data reset;
4. full current-pipeline archive rebuild with a new batch name and `-FreshStart`;
5. `audit-field-catalog-identity`;
6. `plan-interseries-calibration`;
7. only then implement/run M1/M2 pairwise calibration.

## Database

No schema migration is required.

# 0.5.41.5 — MASTER remote archive Stage 1A

Первый рабочий сетевой слой Stage 1 для архива MASTER. Фотометрия Stage 2 и межсерийные вычисления Stage 3 не изменены.

Добавлены две read/download команды:

- `master-archive-search` подключается к удалённой БД MASTER `imdata`, ищет строки `processed_frames` в sky-box вокруг заданных ICRS координат, сохраняет CSV inventory и выводит сводку по наблюдательным ночам и фильтрам;
- `master-archive-fetch` читает inventory, дедуплицирует общие dark/flat, преобразует внутренние пути `/master/...` в подтверждённые HTTPS пути `https://master.kourovka.ru/data/master/...` и скачивает raw/header/dark/flat в локальный зеркальный cache.

Downloader использует HTTP Basic Auth, `.part` + atomic rename, продолжение частично скачанного файла через Range, retry/backoff для временных HTTP ошибок, пропуск существующих файлов и SHA-256 provenance. По умолчанию fetch работает plan-only; реальная передача требует `--execute`. Пароль не принимается CLI-аргументом: используется `GRANDGOUSIER_MASTER_HTTP_PASSWORD` или скрытый интерактивный prompt.

Новые environment variables:

- `GRANDGOUSIER_MASTER_DATABASE_URL`;
- `GRANDGOUSIER_MASTER_HTTP_USER`;
- `GRANDGOUSIER_MASTER_HTTP_PASSWORD`;
- optional `GRANDGOUSIER_MASTER_HTTP_BASE_URL`.

Локальный default cache root для текущего GPX workflow: `C:\master\gpx`.

Миграций БД нет. Raw calibration/reduction ещё не реализована: 0.5.41.5 только discovery + transfer/provenance foundation.

# Grandgousier 0.5.41.6 — MASTER archive HTTPS discovery fallback

Дата: 2026-08-25.

## Причина

Реальный smoke `master-archive-search` с рабочей станции `192.168.241.6` показал, что MASTER PostgreSQL `192.168.240.17:5432` отклоняет соединение через `pg_hba.conf`. При этом HTTPS MASTER и прямое скачивание `/data/master/...` доступны по HTTP Basic Auth.

## Изменения

- `master-archive-search --search-transport auto|postgres|http`; default `auto`;
- `auto` пробует PostgreSQL и при отказе выполняет authenticated HTTPS fallback;
- `http` позволяет сразу обойти закрытый PostgreSQL;
- добавлены `--http-user` и `--http-page-size` для discovery; пароль по-прежнему может вводиться скрытым `getpass`;
- HTTPS discovery читает `master2/processing.php`, извлекает `processed_frame_id`, science raw path, astrometric header path и calibration raw IDs;
- уникальные dark/flat IDs разрешаются через `master2/index.php`, после чего строятся те же `/data/master/...` URL, что использует downloader;
- формат inventory CSV не изменён, поэтому `master-archive-fetch` совместим без изменений.

Миграций БД, изменений Stage 2 photometry и Stage 3 calibration нет.

---

# Grandgousier 0.5.41.7 — MASTER HTTPS coordinate-search hotfix

Дата: 2026-08-25.

## Причина

Реальный smoke 0.5.41.6 успешно прошёл HTTP Basic Auth, но `master-archive-search --search-transport http` вернул `rows=0` для координат GPX-поля, где штатный MASTER web-interface показывает множество processed frames. Причина локализована в способе spatial query: production `processing.php` не воспроизвёл ожидаемую выборку при передаче pgSphere-предиката через `where_long`.

## Изменения

- HTTPS discovery использует штатное поле `coord2000` формы `master2/processing.php`;
- server-side web search выполняет свой стандартный box (пример production HTML показывает ±0.95 deg по Dec с cos(dec)-коррекцией RA);
- Grandgousier локально применяет запрошенный box, фильтры и datetime bounds, поэтому API semantics `--radius-deg 0.8` сохраняются;
- HTTPS transport временно ограничен `--radius-deg <= 0.95`; более широкие области требуют PostgreSQL transport;
- pagination использует официальный `order_by` и распознаёт ссылку на следующую страницу;
- если HTML содержит MASTER raw paths, но parser не смог получить строки, команда теперь завершается явной parser/layout ошибкой вместо ложного `rows=0`;
- dark/flat resolver и downloader не изменены.

Миграций БД и изменений Stage 2/Stage 3 photometric semantics нет.

# Grandgousier 0.5.41.8 — MASTER HTTPS result-row parser hotfix

Дата: 2026-08-25.

## Причина

Реальный GPX smoke 0.5.41.7 успешно прошёл HTTP Basic Auth и spatial search через штатный `coord2000`, но завершился guard-ошибкой:

`MASTER processing.php returned frame paths but no rows could be parsed; the HTML layout may have changed`.

То есть сервер вернул заполненный HTML с `/master/imdata/rawdata/...`, но parser не признал ни одной result row. В 0.5.41.7 parser был привязан к presentation markup: требовал `tr class="n"` и ожидал Raw строго в колонке 10.

## Изменения

- parser больше не использует CSS class как data contract;
- table rows/cells собираются стековым parser-ом, устойчивым к вложенным таблицам search-form;
- science result row определяется по canonical `/master/imdata/rawdata/...` signature;
- позиция Raw определяется динамически, поэтому optional/presentation columns не обязаны иметь прежний индекс;
- если Raw cell содержит только basename, canonical raw path может быть восстановлен из trailing `|RAW` download link;
- header path поддерживает как `Show_Header.php?header=...`, так и прямой `/data/master/imdata/procdata/..._header.fits` link;
- dark/flat IDs по-прежнему извлекаются из двух колонок после найденного Raw;
- добавлены regression tests для classless/alternate-class rows, nested table markup и action-link path fallback.

Inventory schema, downloader, database schema и Stage 2/Stage 3 photometric semantics не изменены. Миграция БД не требуется.

# Grandgousier 0.5.41.9 — MASTER canonical header-path fallback

Дата: 2026-08-25.

## Причина

Реальный Stage 1A smoke на 0.5.41.8 успешно нашёл 5 science frames и скачал 9 unique files (5 raw, 2 dark, 2 flat), однако `header_path` оказался пустым во всех inventory rows. Authenticated HEAD на ожидаемый файл `/master/imdata/procdata/2018/09/07/375506_header.fits` вернул HTTP 200, `Content-Type: image/fits`, `Content-Length: 11520`. Значит header существует, но production `processing.php` не всегда выводит отдельную Header-ссылку.

## Изменения

- явная Header-ссылка из HTML остаётся authoritative;
- если она отсутствует, parser строго выводит header path только из canonical raw path `/master/imdata/rawdata/YYYY/MM/DD/ID.*`;
- fallback: `/master/imdata/procdata/YYYY/MM/DD/ID_header.fits`;
- noncanonical paths не переписываются;
- per-frame HEAD probing не добавляется, поэтому discovery не получает O(N) дополнительных сетевых запросов;
- добавлены regression tests для missing-header-link production shape и rejection noncanonical paths.

CLI, inventory columns, downloader protocol, database schema и Stage 2/Stage 3 photometric semantics не изменены. Миграция БД не требуется. Для текущего 5-frame smoke ожидаемый fetch plan после повторного search: 14 unique files = 5 raw + 5 header + 2 dark + 2 flat.

# Grandgousier 0.5.42.1 — MASTER Stage 1B FITS-card warning hotfix

Дата: 2026-08-26.

## Основание

Первый реальный `master-archive-reduce --limit 1 --execute` для GPX_TF17 `raw_id=375506` завершился `REDUCED`, `failed=0`, median `73.743 ADU`, `invalid_flat=0`, `saturated=359`. Проверка выходного FITS подтвердила float32 primary, корректный TAN-SIP WCS, 359 `RAW_SATURATED` pixels в DQ и отсутствие NaN/Inf. Единственный дефект — `astropy.io.fits.card.VerifyWarning: Card is too long, comment will be truncated`.

Причина: длинные remote paths вместе с описательными FITS comments превышали 80 символов в cards `DARK`, `FLAT`, `GGHDR`; `GGMSMETA` также был длиннее 80 символов. Значения путей при этом сохранялись полностью, урезались только комментарии.

## Изменения

- `DARK`, `FLAT`, `GGRAW`, `GGHDR` теперь записываются как path-valued cards без комментария;
- comment `GGMSMETA` сокращён до `MASTER metadata copied`;
- научная формула `(raw-SDARK)/SFLAT`, DQ semantics, WCS transfer, checksums и validation не изменены;
- end-to-end regression test при наличии Astropy требует отсутствия warning `Card is too long` и проверяет комментарии provenance cards;
- manual/context обновлены.

The real 0.5.42.1 five-frame GPX_TF17 reduction smoke passed with zero failures and the existing Stage 2 detector recognized all outputs, but `SKIPPED_EXISTING` rows in `master_reduction_report.csv` had blank reduction metrics.

No change to `MASTER_DARK_FLAT_V1`, DQ flags, WCS transfer, calibration validation, or database schema.
