# Grandgousier 0.5.44.0

Первый диагностический патч новой подсистемы PSF/оптических систематик.

## Что добавлено

- Новый read-only-in-science шаг `psf_field_diagnostics` в field pipeline.
- Новый standalone CLI `psf-field-diagnostics` для анализа уже существующих `source_detections` по `series_id`, `frame_id` или `instrument_unit_id` без повторной фотометрии.
- Для каждой отобранной изолированной high-S/N detection измеряются:
  - centroid по положительным background-subtracted весам;
  - `FWHM_major`, `FWHM_minor`, geometric FWHM;
  - ellipticity;
  - ориентация главной оси и circular orientation components;
  - simple curve-of-growth diagnostic между внутренним и внешним радиусом.
- Detector coordinates нормируются в диапазон примерно `[-1,+1]`.
- Для FWHM/ellipticity/growth по каждому кадру строятся robust constant, plane и quadratic models с iterative MAD clipping, BIC, residual MAD и detector-wide peak-to-peak amplitude.
- Диагностика экспортирует:
  - `psf_sources.csv` — source-level shape measurements;
  - `psf_frames.csv` — компактные frame-level spatial coefficients и summary metrics;
  - `psf_summary.json`;
  - `psf_field_maps.png`;
  - `psf_time_series.png`.
- `process-archive-path` и `run-field-pipeline` получили `--enable-psf-field-diagnostics` и параметры отбора/fit. В `process-archive-path` включение PSF diagnostics автоматически включает source detection, даже если полный detection-catalog branch не запрошен.

## Научная семантика

0.5.44.0 не меняет forced-aperture flux, aperture correction, ensemble calibration, science measurements, object QC или candidate thresholds. PSF measurements являются диагностическими artifacts; новая DB migration не требуется.

Сравнить MASTER GPX_TF17 2018-09-07:

- EAST/V, series_id=76;
- WEST/R, series_id=77.

Нужно проверить spatial dependence `FWHM`, ellipticity, orientation/growth и их временную эволюцию. Особый интерес — связь WEST/R PSF gradient по detector Y с ранее обнаруженными candidate light-curve slope/MAD gradients.

# Grandgousier 0.5.44.1

## Adaptive elliptical / elongated aperture A/B diagnostics

Реальный PSF field test 0.5.44.0 на MASTER GPX_TF17 показал, что WEST/R имеет сильную нелинейную пространственную PSF-структуру, особенно в нижней части CCD, где ранее концентрировались ложные intrinsic-variability candidates. Поэтому 0.5.44.1 добавляет первый shape-aware flux estimator, но оставляет его диагностическим: circular aperture остаётся production science path и схема БД не меняется.

Новая команда `adaptive-aperture-diagnostics`:

- выбирает уже существующую `field_series`;
- использует сохранённые source detections для ярких изолированных PSF reference stars;
- интерполирует локальную covariance matrix по ближайшим reference stars;
- строит adaptive ellipse с ориентацией и axis ratio локальной PSF;
- увеличивает equivalent aperture radius при локальном уширении PSF;
- динамически отодвигает background annulus за большую полуось для elongated/trailing profiles;
- применяет safety clamps по axis ratio и максимальному radius scale;
- на тех же catalog-frame links параллельно вычисляет baseline circular и adaptive flux;
- экспортирует per-measurement, per-frame и per-object A/B diagnostics.

Object-level diagnostic удаляет constant object median и robust frame common mode отдельно для circular/adaptive instrumental magnitudes, затем сравнивает RMS, MAD и robust peak-to-peak. Это не является заменой полной ensemble calibration, а служит gate перед постоянным multi-estimator storage и PSF-fitting photometry.

Новые artifacts:

- `adaptive_aperture_measurements.csv`;
- `adaptive_aperture_frames.csv`;
- `adaptive_aperture_objects.csv`;
- `adaptive_aperture_summary.json`;
- `adaptive_aperture_field_maps.png`;
- `adaptive_aperture_time_series.png`.

Первый real gate: series 76 EAST/V и series 77 WEST/R от 2018-09-07. Проверяется, уменьшаются ли у WEST/R differential RMS/MAD и их сильная зависимость от detector Y.

DB migration: none. Science calibration semantics: unchanged.

# Grandgousier 0.5.44.10

Spatial-ensemble immutable-generation restart hotfix.

The first Windows rerun of the 0.5.44.9 MASTER GPX_TF17 spatial-v3 A/B failed for both series immediately after conventional ensemble calibration with:

```text
ValueError: Spatial-ensemble calibration name ..._spatial_v3 already exists with different parameters.
```

The spatial materializer still used its pre-MVP5.39 mutable-name helper. A previous/interrupted spatial-v3 row therefore collided with a rerun whose newly materialized ordinary-ensemble source had a different `source_calibration_version_id`.

0.5.44.10 routes pipeline spatial targets through the shared immutable-generation writer used by the other calibration stages:

- an unfinished legacy/materializing logical row may be safely reused and rewritten before finalization;
- a finalized immutable spatial head receives a new pending generation and is atomically republished under the same stable logical name;
- runner passes immutable-generation mode only for persisted pipeline runs; direct/library calls keep the previous compatibility behavior;
- `process-archive-path` summary now prints `pipeline:N error_message`, so a pipeline exception is visible without manually inspecting the JSON manifest.

No scientific spatial fitting/model-selection logic changed. The 0.5.44.9 robust non-degradation gate, `robust_zero_mean_spatial_residual_v3`, `spatial_v3` suffix, random-error semantics and CLI defaults are unchanged. No DB migration.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.44.11.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.44.11

Spatial-ensemble normalized-reconstruction hotfix.

The first Windows rerun after 0.5.44.10 no longer hit the immutable-name collision: both MASTER series completed conventional spatial ensemble, Object QC, candidate-excluded ensemble and the second Object QC. The run then failed downstream with `ReconstructionStateError`.

Root cause: the spatial product was intentionally materialized as `FULL_MEASUREMENTS`, but unlike aperture/ensemble/color stages it did not dual-write a `CalibrationIteration`. The immutable reconstruction path therefore encountered an ENSEMBLE-labelled spatial calibration with no normalized iteration.

0.5.44.11 adds a compact normalized spatial representation without changing the scientific correction:

- every spatial generation writes `iteration_kind=SPATIAL_ENSEMBLE`;
- per-frame constant/linear coefficients use existing generic frame-term columns; quadratic coefficients and detector bounds are stored in existing JSON details/parameters;
- reconstruction dispatches the spatial iteration before generic ENSEMBLE semantics and applies exactly `mag_out = mag_source - spatial_correction`;
- `local_zp_correction` uses the same sign; random/systematic magnitude errors are unchanged;
- FULL_MEASUREMENTS materialization remains enabled for the current controlled A/B.
- `process-archive-path` now prints a separate untruncated `Pipeline failures:` block in addition to the compact summary table.

No schema migration. No spatial model-selection, robust non-degradation gate, CLI default, candidate policy or error model changed. Existing incomplete/older generations do not need to be deleted; the immutable writer will create a new generation on rerun.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.44.12.md`

# 0.5.44.12 — conservative post-ensemble photometric frame QC

## Purpose

The MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B experiments showed that per-frame spatial ensemble correction can reduce median RMS/MAD while increasing the final variable-candidate population, especially in EAST/V. The production problem is therefore reframed from "fit and subtract every instrumental spatial pattern" to "detect unreliable photometry automatically, reduce its statistical weight, and reject only clearly bad frames".

## Changes

- Adds opt-in `--enable-photometric-frame-qc` to `run-field-pipeline` and `process-archive-path`.
- The new stage runs immediately after each conventional ensemble pass and is recomputed during candidate-excluded ensemble iterations.
- It uses the actual ensemble reference objects and computes per-frame residual robust scatter
  `R_j = 1.4826 MAD(r_ij)`.
- The within-series baseline is `R_0 = median(R_j)`. Relative robust thresholds are combined with broad absolute safety limits.
- Frames are classified as `GOOD`, `SUSPECT`, or `BAD`; the series summary is `GOOD`, `DEGRADED`, or `BAD`:
  - `GOOD`: science action `KEEP`;
  - `SUSPECT`: retained; if excess scatter is measurable, the additional systematic term is
    `sigma_sys,j = sqrt(max(R_j^2 - R_0^2, 0))`;
  - `BAD`: raw/source measurements remain in the database, while the derived QC calibration exposes `mag_cal=NULL`, excluding the frame from downstream science/object scatter.
- The existing spatial polynomial fitter is reused only as a diagnostic detector. Its surface is not subtracted from magnitudes.
- Existing aperture/PSF context is reused without rereading FITS. Compact `frame_psf_summary_v1` and `frame_photometric_qc_v1` payloads are persisted in `frames.quality_flags`.
- A normalized `CalibrationIteration(iteration_kind="PHOTOMETRIC_FRAME_QC")` is written, so immutable reconstruction remains authoritative and no new schema migration is required.
- `PHOTOMETRIC_FRAME_BAD` is added to the science reject policy when the new stage is enabled.
- The old `--enable-spatial-ensemble` correction remains experimental and is mutually exclusive with the new conservative QC path.

## Initial defaults

The first controlled A/B keeps the policy intentionally small and fixed in code:

- minimum reference stars per frame: 20;
- relative SUSPECT/BAD robust thresholds: 3/6 robust frame-scatter scales with ratio floors 1.5/2.5;
- absolute residual robust-sigma safety limits: 0.05/0.10 mag;
- spatial diagnostic peak-to-peak warning limits: 0.03/0.10 mag.

These are first validation defaults, not final instrument-specific tuning.

## Compatibility and rollout

- No DB migration.
- `--enable-photometric-frame-qc` is opt-in in 0.5.44.12 pending real MASTER A/B validation.
- Magnitudes are never spatially corrected by this stage.
- Existing source calibration generations and raw measurements are preserved.

---

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.44.13.md`

# 0.5.44.13 — hard-reject-only photometric frame QC v2

## Why this patch exists

The first real `0.5.44.12` MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B showed that the architecture was useful but the initial rejection policy was too aggressive. EAST/V classified 17 GOOD + 8 BAD frames and produced 22452 accepted science points / 12 final candidates versus the adaptive-only baseline 30995 / 7. WEST/R classified 14 GOOD + 3 SUSPECT + 8 BAD and produced 22554 / 45 versus 29312 / 30. Removing roughly one third of the epochs therefore reduced time-series support and increased, rather than decreased, candidate contamination.

## Policy changes

- Relative residual outliers are now `SUSPECT`, never `BAD` by themselves.
- Spatial residual structure is diagnostic-only and can raise a frame only to `SUSPECT`, including the former severe spatial threshold.
- `BAD` is reserved for hard failures:
  - residual scatter cannot be measured;
  - absolute robust residual scatter reaches the emergency limit (default 0.10 mag);
  - critically few usable references remain (hard floor 5; the ordinary 20-star warning remains SUSPECT-only).
- The derived `BAD` QC calibration still exposes `mag_cal=NULL`; source/base measurements are never deleted.
- The new immutable product suffix is `photqc_v2`, so 0.5.44.12 `photqc_v1` products remain available for A/B comparison.

## Frame-specific uncertainty semantics

For a frame with robust residual scatter `R_j` and series median `R_0`, the measured excess term remains

`σ_frame,j = sqrt(max(R_j^2 - R_0^2, 0))`.

In 0.5.44.13 this term is explicitly treated as epoch-dependent uncertainty. It is folded in quadrature into the effective `mag_err_random` / backward-compatible `mag_err` used by object variability and candidate statistics. The pre-QC detector/random term is preserved in flags as `mag_err_random_before_frame_qc`; the added term is stored as `mag_err_frame_systematic`. Correlated absolute/color `mag_err_systematic` is left unchanged.

This corrects the 0.5.44.12 semantic mismatch where the frame term was accumulated into the correlated systematic component and therefore did not reliably reduce the statistical weight of a suspicious epoch in variability metrics.

## PSF provenance hardening

Photometric frame QC now merges the existing aperture/PSF context with the dedicated `psf_frames.csv` product when PSF field diagnostics are enabled. The canonical `frame_psf_summary_v1` can therefore preserve median geometric/major/minor FWHM, FWHM in arcsec when available, ellipticity, position angle, and available FWHM/ellipticity spatial peak-to-peak without rereading FITS.

PSF morphology remains diagnostic-only: it does not directly reject a frame.

## Reconstruction / immutable-calibration contract

- Algorithm provenance: `post_ensemble_photometric_frame_qc_v2`.
- Normalized iteration kind remains `PHOTOMETRIC_FRAME_QC`.
- The reconstruction branch applies the frame-specific uncertainty consistently without changing magnitude for GOOD/SUSPECT frames.
- Candidate-excluded ensemble iterations recompute the same QC policy and use distinct `photqc_v2` generations.
- Spatial ensemble correction remains experimental and mutually exclusive with photometric frame QC.

## Compatibility

- No database migration.
- No new permanent error column is introduced in this patch.
- Existing `frame_photometric_qc_v1` and `frame_psf_summary_v1` JSON containers are retained for compatibility; their algorithm/provenance identifies the v2 policy.
- `--enable-photometric-frame-qc` remains opt-in until the controlled MASTER v2 A/B passes.

---

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.44.14.md`

# 0.5.44.14 — diagnostic-only photometric frame QC v3 and GOOD-frame candidate confirmation

## Motivation

The real 0.5.44.13 MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B recovered most science epochs, but frame-level error inflation did not improve candidate purity. EAST/V produced 17 GOOD, 6 SUSPECT and 2 BAD frames with 29964 accepted points and 39 final candidates; WEST/R produced 13/10/2 with 29589 points and 49 candidates. The validated adaptive-only baselines remain 30995/7 and 29312/30 respectively. The inferred frame excess terms were of order 0.05–0.06 mag (and reached about 0.16 mag), so they are not justified as a common per-star random uncertainty.

## Error semantics

`--enable-photometric-frame-qc` no longer modifies `mag_err`, `mag_err_random` or `mag_err_systematic` for GOOD or SUSPECT frames.

The diagnostic quantity

```text
sigma_frame = sqrt(max(R_j^2 - R_0^2, 0))
```

is still measured and stored in QC/provenance, but it is diagnostic only. BAD remains the only automatic science rejection and is reserved for hard failures.

The normalized algorithm is now `post_ensemble_photometric_frame_qc_v3`; the immutable calibration suffix is `photqc_v3`, so previous `photqc_v1/v2` products remain distinct.

## GOOD-frame candidate confirmation

The ordinary field-QC/candidate evaluator is reused on the GOOD-frame subset. An automatic candidate accepted on all usable epochs remains accepted only when it is also accepted on GOOD epochs.

- `GOOD_FRAME_CONFIRMED`: accepted on both scopes;
- `SYSTEMATICS_SENSITIVE`: accepted only when SUSPECT epochs participate, demoted to `BORDERLINE`;
- `INSUFFICIENT_GOOD_FRAME_SUPPORT`: too few GOOD epochs for the ordinary evaluator, demoted to `BORDERLINE`;
- explicit target candidates are preserved and labelled `TARGET_PRESERVED`.

Confirmation is applied before candidate-reference exclusion as well as before final candidate export. Therefore a source whose variability evidence depends on SUSPECT epochs cannot remove itself from the ensemble reference set and create a feedback loop.

The exported field-QC tables use the confirmed candidate rows. The raw all-usable candidate triage and GOOD-frame confirmation summary are retained in JSON/provenance.

## PSF and spatial diagnostics

PSF morphology and residual spatial fits remain diagnostic-only. Their measurements are preserved in `frame_psf_summary_v1` / frame photometric QC artifacts; no PSF parameter is promoted to an independent reject gate.

## Compatibility

- no database migration;
- no magnitude correction;
- no error inflation for SUSPECT epochs;
- spatial ensemble magnitude correction remains experimental and mutually exclusive with photometric frame QC;
- controlled MASTER A/B remains required before enabling the policy by default.

---

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.44.15.md`

# 0.5.44.15 — confirmed-candidate HIGH_RMS export semantics and PSF spatial-summary wiring

## Motivation

The real 0.5.44.14 MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B validated the diagnostic-only frame-QC architecture. EAST/V retained 29964 accepted science points with 17 GOOD / 6 SUSPECT / 2 BAD frames; WEST/R retained 29589 with 13 / 10 / 2. GOOD-frame confirmation reduced automatic variability membership to 5 confirmed candidates in V and 25 in R, while 36 and 33 candidates respectively were classified `SYSTEMATICS_SENSITIVE`.

The final candidate-light-curve export nevertheless reported only 4 V and 16 R accepted candidates. The missing 1 V and 9 R objects were already `GOOD_FRAME_CONFIRMED`; their light curves were rejected only because the generic science-light-curve policy treats object-QC `HIGH_RMS` as a point reject flag. This is circular for a confirmed variability candidate: high RMS is the signal being tested, and the same signal was independently re-confirmed on GOOD epochs.

The same A/B also exposed a diagnostic wiring mismatch: the dedicated `psf_frames.csv` uses real columns such as `fwhm_geom_median`, `orientation_mean_deg`, and model-specific `*_constant/plane/quadratic_spatial_peak_to_peak`, while the frame-QC normalizer expected older generic aliases. Median PSF quantities survived through aperture context, but the spatial PSF peak-to-peak fields were empty.

## Candidate export semantics

For a row satisfying both:

- `candidate_status == ACCEPTED`;
- `good_frame_confirmation_status == GOOD_FRAME_CONFIRMED`;

candidate-light-curve export removes only `HIGH_RMS` from the point-level reject set. `HIGH_RMS` remains present in `object_qc_flags` and therefore remains visible as diagnostic provenance. Every other science reject flag (`EDGE`, blend/crowding flags, saturation-like flags, `PHOTOMETRIC_FRAME_BAD`, etc.) is unchanged.

Ordinary objects and unconfirmed candidates retain the existing default `HIGH_RMS` rejection policy. The override is explicitly written to candidate products as:

```text
HIGH_RMS_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY_FOR_GOOD_FRAME_CONFIRMED
```

The fix is deliberately restricted to candidate export; it does not change ordinary science-light-curve quality semantics or the frame-QC/GOOD-frame confirmation algorithms.

The field-QC candidate-triage CSV now also persists the GOOD-frame confirmation diagnostics (status, GOOD-frame counts and GOOD-only RMS/MAD/robust metrics) instead of keeping them only in in-memory/JSON provenance.

## PSF spatial summary

`photometric_frame_qc` now understands the actual PSF-field export schema:

- `fwhm_geom_median` for geometric FWHM;
- `orientation_mean_deg` for position angle;
- `fwhm_geom_{constant,plane,quadratic}_*`;
- `ellipticity_{constant,plane,quadratic}_*`.

For FWHM and ellipticity separately, the successful constant/plane/quadratic model with minimum BIC is selected. Its model name and spatial peak-to-peak amplitude are stored in `frame_psf_summary_v1` and `photometric_frame_qc_frames.csv`. PSF remains diagnostic-only and does not become a new reject gate.

## Compatibility

- no database migration;
- no change to `post_ensemble_photometric_frame_qc_v3` thresholds or GOOD/SUSPECT/BAD classification;
- no magnitude correction and no error inflation;
- no change to GOOD-frame candidate evaluator or candidate-reference exclusion;
- existing `photqc_v3` normalized calibration semantics remain valid;
- only final confirmed-candidate export and PSF diagnostic wiring change.

The full-project overlay audit also caught a latent documentation regression from the recent patch sequence: `docs/user_manual_ru/main.tex` still references `\manualversion`, while the patch overlay had replaced `version.tex` with a differently named macro. 0.5.44.15 restores the existing `\manualversion` contract and verifies the Russian XeLaTeX manual on the full project tree. This is documentation-only and does not affect runtime behavior.

# 0.5.44.16 — diagnostic candidate axis-bin correlations

## Motivation

The real 0.5.44.15 MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B closed the confirmed-candidate export issue: EAST/V exports 5 and WEST/R 25 `GOOD_FRAME_CONFIRMED` candidates while retaining 29964/29589 accepted science points. Detailed inspection nevertheless showed that multiple confirmed WEST/R candidates change brightness synchronously on otherwise globally GOOD frames and cluster in detector X/Y regions. A new local correction or residual-map rejection layer would add substantial policy complexity.

0.5.44.16 therefore adds a narrower diagnostic: compare only already-confirmed candidate light curves that occupy the same detector-axis bins. The diagnostic does not alter photometry, frame QC, candidate status, or candidate-reference exclusion.

## Algorithm

For `ACCEPTED` candidates with `GOOD_FRAME_CONFIRMED` (and explicitly preserved accepted targets):

1. load the current calibration only on photometric-frame-QC `GOOD` frames;
2. compute the candidate median detector `(x,y)` and median-centred magnitude changes;
3. divide each detector axis independently into 16 bins;
4. also evaluate a second 16-bin partition shifted by half a bin, so nearby sources are not separated only by an arbitrary primary-bin boundary;
5. compare a pair only when it shares an X or Y bin in at least one partition;
6. require at least 8 common GOOD epochs;
7. calculate Spearman correlation of the magnitude changes;
8. set a diagnostic flag when `abs(rho) >= 0.8`.

Flags are:

- `CANDIDATE_CORRELATED_X`;
- `CANDIDATE_CORRELATED_Y`;
- both flags may be present simultaneously.

The sign of rho is preserved. Negative correlations are retained because detector/PSF/blending systematics can redistribute flux in opposite directions; the flag therefore uses absolute correlation while the exported metric remains signed.

## Outputs

`field_qc_candidate_triage.csv` and final candidate summaries gain:

- median detector X/Y;
- primary and half-shifted X/Y bin indices;
- candidate counts sharing the X/Y bin neighbourhood;
- strongest signed X/Y Spearman rho;
- corresponding object/source id;
- number of common GOOD epochs for the strongest pair;
- number of strongly correlated X/Y neighbours;
- correlation status and flags.

A dedicated diagnostic directory is also written:

```text
candidate_axis_correlation/
  candidate_axis_pairs.csv
  summary.json
```

The process summary reports candidate counts correlated in X, Y, or either axis.

## Safety semantics

This patch is diagnostic-only:

- candidate `ACCEPTED/BORDERLINE/REJECTED` membership is unchanged;
- candidate-excluded ensemble membership is unchanged;
- no magnitude correction is applied;
- no error inflation is applied;
- frame `GOOD/SUSPECT/BAD` policy is unchanged;
- `HIGH_RMS` confirmed-candidate export semantics from 0.5.44.15 are unchanged;
- no database migration is required.

## Control-dataset precheck

Running the same algorithm offline on the exported 0.5.44.15 GPX_TF17 products flags 0/5 confirmed EAST/V candidates and 17/25 confirmed WEST/R candidates. This is only a precheck of the diagnostic behaviour; the 0.5.44.16 runtime A/B remains the acceptance test for wiring/provenance.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.44.17.md`

# 0.5.44.17 — dual Spearman/Pearson candidate axis diagnostics

## Motivation

The real 0.5.44.16 MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B reproduced the offline axis-bin diagnostic exactly: EAST/V retained 5 `GOOD_FRAME_CONFIRMED` candidates with 0 axis-correlation flags, while WEST/R retained 25 with 17 flagged candidates. Science photometry and candidate acceptance were unchanged.

Inspection of the exported GOOD-epoch light curves exposed a complementary failure mode of Spearman-only diagnostics: several candidates can share one very large synchronous excursion while having otherwise unrelated epoch ordering. Such pairs can have weak Spearman rho but Pearson correlation close to unity. This is useful diagnostic information for detector/PSF/blending artefacts and should not be lost.

## Algorithm

The 0.5.44.16 geometry and safety semantics are retained unchanged:

- only `ACCEPTED` `GOOD_FRAME_CONFIRMED` candidates (plus explicitly preserved accepted targets);
- only photometric-frame-QC `GOOD` epochs;
- 16 X bins and 16 Y bins;
- primary plus half-bin-shifted partitions;
- at least 8 common GOOD epochs;
- diagnostic-only: no candidate-status, photometry, error, frame-QC, or ensemble-exclusion changes.

For every eligible pair Grandgousier now computes both signed coefficients:

```text
spearman_rho
pearson_r
```

A pair is flagged when either criterion passes:

```text
abs(spearman_rho) >= 0.8
OR
abs(pearson_r) >= 0.8
```

The pair/candidate mode is one of `NONE`, `SPEARMAN`, `PEARSON`, or `BOTH`. Negative correlations remain valid diagnostics because detector/PSF/blending effects can redistribute flux in opposite directions.

## Outputs

`candidate_axis_pairs.csv` gains Pearson metrics, per-metric pass flags, and correlation mode. Candidate triage/final summaries retain the old Spearman fields and additionally persist strongest signed Pearson and Spearman partners/common-epoch counts, per-axis/combined mode, per-metric correlated-neighbour counts, and the strongest generic triggering partner.

The process summary additionally exposes candidate counts with Spearman and Pearson evidence and correlation-mode counts.

## Offline replay on the supplied 0.5.44.16 exports

Recomputing Pearson on the exact pair geometry and GOOD epochs already exported by the supplied 0.5.44.16 project gives:

- EAST/V: Spearman flags 0/5 candidates, Pearson 2/5, union 2/5;
- WEST/R: Spearman flags 17/25 candidates, Pearson 22/25, union 23/25.

One explicit EAST/V Pearson-only pair is object 30225 vs 31378: Spearman `-0.0980`, Pearson `+0.8242` over 17 common GOOD epochs. This is an offline diagnostic replay, not a substitute for the 0.5.44.17 runtime A/B wiring test.

## Packaging audit

The user-supplied full 0.5.44.16 tree revealed a real version inconsistency: `grandgousier/__init__.py`, manual and project state reported 0.5.44.16, but `pyproject.toml` still reported 0.5.44.15. 0.5.44.17 restores a consistent package version across these markers.

## Database

No migration.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.44.2.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.44.2

## Adaptive aperture as a full Stage-2 alternate estimator

The real 0.5.44.1 MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B showed that local-PSF adaptive elliptical apertures materially reduce WEST/R false variability: median differential RMS fell from 0.06327 to 0.05454 mag, median MAD from 0.02202 to 0.01250 mag, and the detector-Y dependence weakened strongly while EAST/V remained approximately neutral. Version 0.5.44.2 therefore promotes the estimator from diagnostic CSVs into a controlled alternate Stage-2 BASE calibration generation.

### New CLI

`process-archive-path` and `run-field-pipeline` now accept:

```text
--photometry-estimator {circular,adaptive_ellipse}
```

The default is still `circular`. `adaptive_ellipse` automatically requires source detection, constructs a local PSF covariance field from bright isolated detections and measures a PSF-aligned elliptical aperture for every forced catalog source.

Adaptive tuning parameters include PSF-reference S/N/number/isolation, interpolation-neighbor count, FWHM scale, maximum axis ratio and maximum equal-area radius scale. Circular fallback is enabled by default when no reliable local PSF geometry can be formed and is explicitly recorded in measurement flags; strict A/B runs can disable the fallback.

### Scientific semantics

Adaptive measurements now use the same physical random-error model as circular forced photometry, including source Poisson, empirical/detector background, background-estimator uncertainty, optional fractional floor and scintillation terms. The scalar `measurements.aperture_radius_pix` stores the equal-area circular radius for schema compatibility, while semi-major/minor axes, orientation, local PSF shape and adaptive annulus geometry are preserved in JSON flags.

The adaptive BASE calibration is separate and immutable. Existing aperture correction, aperture ZP, ensemble calibration, object QC, candidate iterations and final science materialization operate on that BASE exactly as they do on circular photometry. This enables a scientifically meaningful end-to-end A/B without duplicating downstream algorithms.

### Compatibility and safety

- Circular photometry remains the default and retains its historical calibration-name semantics.
- No database migration is introduced.
- Existing science rows are not overwritten when a distinct calibration prefix is used for the adaptive A/B.
- Adaptive photometry does not imply automatic frame rejection for elongated PSF.
- Permanent multi-estimator columns and `primary_method` remain a later roadmap item; 0.5.44.2 uses separate immutable calibration generations only for controlled validation.

### Immediate MASTER gate

Repeat the 25 EAST/V + 25 WEST/R 2018-09-07 Stage-2 run with `--photometry-estimator adaptive_ellipse` and a distinct calibration prefix. Compare final candidate counts, accepted science points, RMS/MAD versus detector Y, common-mode structure and fallback/PSF-reference coverage against the existing circular baseline.

# 0.5.44.4 — spatially varying PSF photometry

- Added `spatial_psf` as an experimental full Stage-2 BASE photometry estimator.
- Local PSF shape is interpolated from bright isolated detections; the default flux model is an elliptical Moffat profile with fixed beta and a small forced-position centroid grid search.
- Flux uncertainty uses the matched-profile noise-equivalent area inside the existing physical Poisson/background/fractional/scintillation decomposition.
- Per-source PSF fit provenance includes local shape, centroid offsets, residual MAD, fit radius, capture fraction and noise-equivalent pixels.
- Failed source-level profile fits fall back to adaptive ellipse by default; missing PSF fields can fall back to circular aperture. Both fallbacks are explicit and configurable.
- PSF BASE remains a distinct immutable calibration generation and uses the existing profile-to-reference aperture correction, ZP, ensemble, object-QC, candidates and science materialization chain.
- Circular remains the default; no DB migration.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.44.5.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.44.5 — spatial empirical PSF A/B

## Motivation

The real 0.5.44.4 MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B showed that the first analytic spatial PSF estimator is not suitable for this instrument.  On series 76/77 it produced 17/144 final V/R candidates and only 29520/26637 accepted science points, compared with the validated adaptive-ellipse result 7/30 and 30995/29312.  WEST/R median RMS/MAD also degraded from 0.05240/0.01302 mag (adaptive) to 0.06118/0.02167 mag.  The profile-to-reference aperture correction for the analytic fit was about +0.46--0.47 mag, a direct sign that a fixed-form Moffat profile does not describe the real MASTER PSF/wings adequately.

## New estimator

0.5.44.5 adds experimental `--photometry-estimator empirical_psf` without changing the default `circular` path and without a DB migration.

For every frame the estimator:

1. selects bright, isolated, unsaturated detection references;
2. estimates a sub-pixel centroid for each reference star;
3. resamples a registered stellar stamp on a common pixel grid;
4. subtracts a local robust sky estimate;
5. normalizes every reference stamp to its flux inside a configurable reference aperture (default 5 px);
6. builds a regular spatial PSF grid (default 3x3), each node being a robust combination of the nearest reference stamps;
7. bilinearly interpolates the complete two-dimensional template between grid nodes;
8. fits only flux and a small centroid offset at each forced catalog source.

Because each template is normalized to the same reference aperture used by the downstream aperture-correction layer, the empirical PSF amplitude is a reference-aperture flux estimator rather than an analytic extrapolation to infinite radius.

## Error model and fallbacks

The matched-template noise-equivalent area `1/sum(P^2)` is propagated through the existing physical random-error model.  Source-level failures fall back to `adaptive_ellipse` by default; circular remains the last fallback when allowed.  All fallbacks are explicit in measurement flags.

## CLI

New options for `run-forced-photometry`, `run-field-pipeline` and `process-archive-path`:

- `--photometry-estimator empirical_psf`
- `--empirical-psf-grid-size` (default 3)
- `--empirical-psf-stamp-radius-pix` (default 8)
- `--empirical-psf-reference-radius-pix` (default 5.0)
- `--empirical-psf-references-per-node` (default 48)
- `--empirical-psf-min-references-per-node` (default 12)
- `--no-empirical-psf-adaptive-fallback`

Centroid search and residual clipping reuse the existing `--psf-centroid-*` and `--psf-residual-*` controls.

## Immediate validation gate

Repeat the same 25 EAST/V + 25 WEST/R MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B.  The empirical estimator should be judged against the validated adaptive baseline, not merely against circular:

- V: 7 final candidates, 30995 accepted science points;
- R: 30 final candidates, 29312 accepted science points;
- R median RMS/MAD: 0.05240/0.01302 mag.

A successful empirical PSF should at minimum avoid the 0.5.44.4 degradation and preferably reduce the residual R common-mode/spatial candidate population below the adaptive result.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.5.44.6.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.44.6 — spatial ensemble calibration

## Назначение

Экспериментальный spatial-ensemble слой после обычной ensemble calibration. Потоковый estimator не меняется; рекомендуемый MASTER A/B использует `adaptive_ellipse`.

Модель для reference residuals на каждом кадре:

`m_ij = M_i + Z_j + S_j(x_i,y_i) + eps_ij`.

Обычный ensemble по-прежнему определяет `Z_j` и reference stars. Новый слой оценивает только zero-mean spatial term `S_j`: intercept используется как nuisance-параметр при fit, но не применяется к measurements. Доступны identity, plane и quadratic модели с iterative clipping, BIC/amplitude/safety gates.

## CLI

`--enable-spatial-ensemble` включает слой. Дополнительные параметры: `--spatial-ensemble-max-order`, `--spatial-ensemble-min-ref-stars-per-frame`, `--spatial-ensemble-clip-sigma`, `--spatial-ensemble-n-iterations`, `--spatial-ensemble-min-bic-improvement`, `--spatial-ensemble-min-spatial-peak-to-peak`, `--spatial-ensemble-max-residual-mad`, `--spatial-ensemble-max-abs-spatial-deviation`, `--spatial-ensemble-min-good-frame-fraction`.

Spatial model переоценивается на каждом candidate-excluded ensemble iteration. При global quality-gate failure final calibration является identity-copy обычного ensemble. В 0.5.44.6 random-error values не меняются: model uncertainty записывается только диагностически, поэтому A/B candidate membership не может улучшиться из-за искусственного inflation `mag_err`.

## Артефакты

В series output создаются раздельные diagnostics для каждой ensemble-итерации: `spatial_ensemble/iter1/spatial_ensemble_summary.json`, `spatial_ensemble/iter1/spatial_ensemble_frames.csv`, а при candidate-excluded convergence также `iter2`, `iter3`, ... . Это предотвращает перезапись provenance между итерациями. Новая DB migration не требуется.

## MASTER acceptance gate

Сравнение с проверенным adaptive baseline: EAST/V 7 candidates и 30995 accepted points; WEST/R 30 candidates и 29312 accepted points, median RMS/MAD 0.05240/0.01302 mag. Требуется уменьшение residual detector-Y/common-mode/PCA structure без заметной деградации V.

# Grandgousier 0.5.44.9

Spatial-ensemble robust non-degradation gate.

The first complete 0.5.44.8 MASTER GPX_TF17 A/B showed a mixed result. Spatial ensemble reduced the median scatter of the main population (WEST/R RMS 0.05240 -> 0.05014 mag and MAD 0.01302 -> 0.01194 mag; EAST/V RMS 0.05477 -> 0.05266 mag and MAD 0.01450 -> 0.01376 mag), but candidate contamination did not improve: raw/triage counts changed R 217/93 -> 220/95 and V 135/54 -> 154/66. Frame diagnostics also contained BIC-selected spatial surfaces whose residual MAD was slightly worse than identity.

0.5.44.9 therefore adds a local science-safety gate after the existing BIC/amplitude/spatial-excursion checks:

- new `--spatial-ensemble-max-residual-mad-degradation`, default `0.0` mag;
- a plane/quadratic surface whose robust residual MAD exceeds identity by more than this tolerance is replaced by identity for that frame;
- this fallback does **not** invalidate the frame and therefore does not reduce `good_frame_fraction`;
- negative CLI values disable this one gate for diagnostic reproduction of the 0.5.44.8 policy;
- measurement flags and frame diagnostics now retain proposed model, selection/fallback reason, selected/proposed MAD and RMS deltas, and fractional MAD improvement;
- summary diagnostics count `frames_robust_non_degradation_fallback`;
- random-error columns remain unchanged.

Because the scientific model-selection policy changed, the algorithm provenance is now `robust_zero_mean_spatial_residual_v3` and final ensemble products use `spatial_v3`, avoiding collisions with the existing 0.5.44.8 `spatial_v2` products.

No DB migration. `--enable-spatial-ensemble` remains opt-in; adaptive ellipse remains the preferred MASTER BASE estimator while this A/B is unresolved.

# Grandgousier 0.5.45.0

Stage 3 M1--M3 read-only computational MVP.

- Adds `analyze-interseries-calibration` on top of published Stage-2 `SCIENCE` generations.
- M1 derives robust per-series representative object states from `science_measurements`: median magnitude, MAD/robust scatter, representative uncertainty and Stage-2 reference/QC provenance.
- Inter-series calibrators are restricted to the nearest final normalized ENSEMBLE reference population and vetoed by standard object-QC reject flags.
- M2 estimates pairwise offsets with iterative median/MAD clipping and exports every used/rejected calibrator.
- Fixes the Stage-3 sign convention explicitly: `delta_ab = m_b - m_a`, `z_a - z_b = delta_ab`, `m_global = m_science + z_s`.
- M3 solves connected pairwise graphs by weighted least squares with a fixed reference-series gauge and exports closure residuals, chi-square and series offsets.
- Refuses to silently choose between multiple independent compatible components; the user must narrow filter/instrument/catalog scope or set `--reference-series-id`.
- Writes diagnostics only (`series_summary.csv`, `series_object_states.csv`, `pairwise_offsets.csv`, `pairwise_calibrators.csv`, `graph_offsets.csv`, `graph_edges.csv`, `interseries_summary.json`). No Stage-3 DB rows are written yet.
- No schema migration.

# Grandgousier 0.5.45.1

Stage-2 selective-rerun and ensemble-precondition hotfix required by the first real GPX_TF17 Stage-3 seed expansion.

- Adds `process-archive-path --series-id <ID>` (repeatable). In selective mode Grandgousier does not call `build_field_series`; it only reruns requested existing series that contain frames physically discovered under `--path`. A mismatched ID stops with `FAILED_PRECONDITION_SERIES_SELECTION`.
- Adds `process-archive-path --ensemble-min-ref-stars-per-frame`. Default remains **30**, preserving previous archive-workflow science semantics; the option now makes the ordinary ensemble threshold explicit instead of being inaccessible from the one-command workflow.
- Adds an explicit ordinary-ensemble gate in `run-field-pipeline`. If the base ensemble cannot form a usable solution (`usable_reference_objects < required`, no selected frames, no frame offsets, or no calibrated measurements), the run terminates as `FAILED_PRECONDITION_ENSEMBLE` before photometric-frame-QC/Object-QC can reference a nonexistent derived generation.
- Persists base-ensemble diagnostics into failed step telemetry and, when photometric-frame-QC succeeds, into the QC step result: reference candidate count, usable references, required references/frame, selected frames, frames with offsets, calibrated measurements and base calibration version.
- `show-pipeline-steps` exposes the ensemble telemetry in table/CSV output.
- Fixes common CLI JSON rendering of PostgreSQL `datetime` values by using `json.dumps(..., default=str)`, fixing `show-pipeline-steps --format json` and `show-pipeline-log-events --format json`.
- Does **not** change the global ordinary-ensemble default from 30 to 20. The GPX_TF17 series-78 rerun should pass 20 explicitly; real dry-runs showed 22 usable references and complete 29/29 frame coverage at 20, with no improvement at 15 or 10.
- No database migration. Stage-3 M1--M3 scientific algorithms are unchanged.

# Grandgousier 0.5.45.2

Дата: 2026-09-04.

## Назначение

Узкий Stage-3 input-recovery hotfix после первого реального GPX_TF17 planner run. Алгоритмы M1--M3, их sign contract и DB schema не меняются.

Реальная диагностика field 33 показала два независимых дефекта Stage-2/Stage-3 handoff:

1. Новые photometric-frame-QC SCIENCE generations series 76--81 были опубликованы, но `science_measurements` для них оставались пустыми. В run 239 materializer вернул `status=OK`, `reconstructed_rows=0` для calibration version 991.
2. M0 planner выбирал только SCIENCE generations, уже имевшие rows, и сортировал разные logical products прежде всего по `generation_no`. Поскольку `generation_no` локален для `logical_name`, planner откатывался к старым empirical-PSF generations 816/821 вместо новейших production-like products.

## Исправления

- PostgreSQL science-materialization fast path теперь используется только когда `iteration_kind` соответствует поддерживаемому стандартному stage. Derived ENSEMBLE generations с `PHOTOMETRIC_FRAME_QC` или `SPATIAL_ENSEMBLE` автоматически используют authoritative Python normalized reconstruction вместо ошибочного поиска `ENSEMBLE_OFFSET` в их последней итерации.
- Нулевая reconstruction из непустого BASE scope больше не считается `OK`: materialization завершается ошибкой до публикации некорректного SCIENCE product.
- Добавлена команда `materialize-science-calibration` для безопасного backfill уже существующей immutable SCIENCE generation без повторной фотометрии.
- M0 planner теперь выбирает новейшую SCIENCE generation по `finalized_at`, затем `materialized_at`, `pipeline_run_id`, `calibration_version_id`; `generation_no` не сравнивается между различными logical products.
- Planner выбирает новейший SCIENCE product независимо от наличия `science_measurements`. Пустая materialization показывается как `NO_SCIENCE_ROWS`, а не скрыто заменяется старым продуктом.
- `--catalog-name` применяется внутри SCIENCE selector, поэтому несовместимые/неподготовленные series больше не исчезают из общего списка field series.
- Исправлено прокидывание base-ensemble telemetry из pipeline step в `process-archive-path` summary.

## GPX_TF17 recovery

После установки 0.5.45.2 backfill требуется для последних intended SCIENCE generations:

- series 76: calibration version 960;
- series 77: 967;
- series 78: 991;
- series 79: 981;
- series 80: 976;
- series 81: 986.

После backfill нужно повторить planner V/R с shared catalog и только затем запускать M1--M3.

DB migration отсутствует.

# Grandgousier 0.5.46.0

Date: 2026-09-04

## Purpose

0.5.46.0 introduces Stage 3 M4: an immutable, idempotent persisted inter-series calibration generation built from the already validated M1--M3 graph solution.

The release does **not** rewrite Stage-2 `science_measurements` and does not alter the M1/M2/M3 sign convention or estimators.

## Database migration

Managed migration:

`mvp5_46_0_interseries_calibration_generations`

It creates three tables:

- `interseries_calibration_generations` — generation-level immutable provenance, graph quality and exact input fingerprint;
- `interseries_calibration_series` — exact source SCIENCE generation and additive `z_s`/uncertainty for every included series;
- `interseries_calibration_edges` — M2 pairwise result, calibrator membership IDs and M3 closure diagnostics.

The earlier `interseries_calibration_offsets` table is retained untouched as a legacy compatibility layer. It is not the M4 production storage model.

## Immutable fingerprint

The SHA-256 generation fingerprint includes:

- exact `(series_id, calibration_version_id)` source SCIENCE identities;
- field/instrument/filter/catalog scope;
- M1--M3 algorithm and sign convention;
- reference series;
- `min_points_per_object`;
- `min_common_objects`;
- `clip_sigma`;
- `max_clip_iterations`.

Repeating persistence with the same inputs returns the existing generation and does not duplicate series/edge rows. A new Stage-2 SCIENCE generation or any changed scientific parameter creates a different M4 generation.

## Reliability classes

Successful connected graphs are persisted with an explicit reliability class:

- `REDUNDANT_GRAPH_OK`: graph has positive degrees of freedom and therefore an internal closure test;
- `SPARSE_GRAPH_NO_CLOSURE`: connected tree with `graph_dof=0`; persistence requires explicit `--allow-sparse-graph`.

The GPX_TF17 validation motivates this distinction: R 77/80/81 is a redundant triangle; V 76/78/79 is a scientifically reviewed sparse tree at `min_common_objects=15`.

## CLI

New commands:

- `persist-interseries-calibration`
- `show-interseries-calibration`
- `verify-interseries-calibration`

`verify-interseries-calibration` checks the generation fingerprint, exact immutable SCIENCE provenance, retained SCIENCE row counts and stored graph equations/chi-square. It does not silently select newer Stage-2 products.

## Uncertainty semantics

`offset_err_mag` is retained as a per-series zero-point uncertainty correlated by construction across all measurements of that series. M4 does not fold it into every Stage-2 point or overwrite `mag_err_random`/`mag_err_systematic`. Object-history consumption remains a later M5 step.

# Grandgousier 0.5.47.0

Date: 2026-09-04

## Purpose

0.5.47.0 implements Stage 3 M5 as a read-only global object-history exporter consuming already persisted M4 generations. It adds plotting and bounded-memory plot reduction, but does not add a database migration or materialize a new copy of photometric measurements.

## Exact M4 linkage

A row is calibrated globally only when both `series_id` and Stage-2 `science_calibration_version_id` exactly match an `interseries_calibration_series` source. A newer SCIENCE generation never inherits an older M4 offset implicitly. Ambiguous automatic generation selection is refused; repeatable `--generation-id` resolves it explicitly. Unlinked/stale current SCIENCE blocks the export unless `--allow-partial` is explicit.

## Photometry and errors

M5 exports `mag_global = mag_science + z_s`. Stage-2 random/systematic error components are retained. `mag_err_series_zp` is the M4 zero-point uncertainty correlated across the series. `mag_err_effective = sqrt(mag_err_random^2 + mag_err_series_zp^2)` is a convenience field only and is not independent point noise.

## CSV and plotting

The main CSV is streamed and never thinned by visualization settings. Plots reuse the existing headless Matplotlib infrastructure and are separate per filter. `--plot-reduction auto` draws raw accepted points when the exact linked source-row count is within `--plot-max-points` (default 5000); otherwise only the plot layer is reduced into per-series time bins. Bins retain mean magnitude, random/bin SEM and min/max envelope. An explicit `--plot-bin-minutes`, `--plot-reduction bin|none`, `--no-plots`, and PNG/PDF/SVG are supported.

## CLI

New command: `export-global-object-light-curve`. Typical outputs are the exact global CSV, JSON summary, one plot-data CSV per filter and one plot image per filter.

## Database

No migration. M4 generation/series/edge tables from 0.5.46.0 remain authoritative provenance.

The first real GPX smoke used object 29700. M5 correctly resolved 128 rows but accepted none. - CLI returns code 2 when exact linked rows exist but zero survive QC;
- plots remain accepted-only.

# Grandgousier 0.5.48.0

M8 production-orchestration milestone. No database migration and no change to the scientific semantics of Stage 2, M0--M5, QC flags, inter-series equations, or M5 error propagation.

## Added

- `process-field-archive`: resumable field-scale orchestration over processed FITS leaf batches.
- Explicit immutable Stage-3 policies via `--stage3-policy FILTER:MIN_COMMON[:REFERENCE_SERIES_ID[:INSTRUMENT_UNIT_ID]]`.
- Frozen real-data validated `stage3_scale_v1` Stage-2 recipe.
- Mandatory gates: Stage-2 success, SCIENCE materialization parity for processed series, catalog identity, M0 readiness, connected M1--M3 graph, M4 verification, optional M5 control objects.
- Resume classification: `SKIP_READY`, `RUN_NEW`, `RESUME_INCOMPLETE`, `STOP_CONFLICT`.
- Fail-closed ambiguity guards: one M8 v1 Stage-3 policy per filter and no multi-date FITS leaf batch.
- Explicit `--exclude-date` / `--include-date` controls for unsafe or deliberately out-of-scope archive blocks.
- Consolidated machine- and human-readable output: `final_report.json`, `report.html`, batch, frame-QC, M4 series/edges/offsets, and M5 control CSV summaries.

## Safety contract

M8 never lowers `min_common_objects` automatically. A disconnected graph stops the workflow. Existing READY batches are skipped under `--resume`; conflicting field ownership stops execution. Duplicate policies for one filter and leaf batches spanning multiple calendar dates are rejected before execution. The orchestration layer calls the existing Stage-2/M0--M5 implementations rather than maintaining duplicate scientific algorithms.

# Grandgousier 0.5.51.0

Productization P3 foundation: production service/job/config layer over the already validated M8 field-archive workflow.

## Service boundary

New package `grandgousier.services` provides:

- `FieldArchiveJobConfig` with deterministic source precedence: defaults < environment < YAML/JSON file < explicit overrides;
- `run_field_archive_job()` as the single server-facing wrapper around existing `run_field_archive_workflow()`;
- `check_runtime_readiness()` for package resources, processed/output roots, PostgreSQL connectivity and migration ledger readiness;
- append-only `job_events.jsonl` with scan/batch/Stage-3/M5 progress, sanitized `job_config.json`, `job_summary.json` and retained `failure.json`;
- PostgreSQL advisory locking for one `(field_id, catalog_name, processed_root)` production scope.

The existing CLI `process-field-archive` now builds the same `FieldArchiveJobConfig` and calls the same service function. Existing direct CLI flags remain valid. `--format json` preserves the legacy M8 JSON payload when M8 runs; `--format job-json` returns the full service wrapper. New `--job-config` accepts YAML/JSON; explicit CLI values override file/environment values. `--plan-only` can override a config that requests execution. `--no-preflight` exists only for controlled diagnostics/tests.

## Readiness

New CLI command `field-archive-readiness` checks:

- processed-root existence;
- bundled MASTER/RoboPhot profile resources;
- report-root writability;
- packaged CA bundle availability (`certifi`);
- PostgreSQL connection + `SELECT 1`;
- zero pending managed migrations;
- zero migration checksum drift.

The readiness command and job preflight never apply migrations automatically.

## Concurrency

Before M8 execution/plan, the service acquires a PostgreSQL session advisory lock derived from field ID, shared catalog namespace and normalized processed root. A competing job on the same scope fails as `FAILED_PRECONDITION / FieldArchiveJobLocked` rather than running a second Stage-2/M0--M5 workflow.

No DB schema migration is needed.

## Scientific contract

No Stage-2 estimator, QC, M0--M5 formula, Stage-3 threshold, M4 persistence semantics, M5 linkage/error convention or M8 batch classification was changed. The service layer delegates to the existing implementation.

## Intentionally deferred

0.5.51.0 does not add an HTTP framework, authentication, worker queue, remote scheduler, stable-frame-identity migration or storage-model refactor. Those remain separate productization tasks after real service-layer validation.

## Public distribution boundary

The public wheel/sdist excludes repository-local remote archive transport code and does not contain private MASTER endpoints, credentials, database addresses, authenticated web paths, or server storage topology. Remote discovery/fetch tooling remains repository-local only. Local FITS reduction/photometry support and instrument profiles remain public. `README_PUBLIC.md` is used as package metadata; internal historical README/context files are excluded from sdist.

# 0.5.53.0 — P4b observation-aware ingestion

Date: 2026-09-10.

This release wires the P4a physical-observation identity layer into the normal archive indexer without changing database schema or scientific processing.

- Newly indexed supported Frame products create/reuse and link the matching `Observation`.
- An exact existing legacy Frame is identity-reconciled before it is counted as `skipped_existing`.
- Copy/move and compatible product variants remain distinct Frame rows but share one Observation.
- P4a hard/soft consistency rules are shared between backfill and ingestion.
- Observation unique-key races are isolated with a SAVEPOINT and recovered only by exact post-race identity lookup.
- Missing/invalid identity persists the new Frame unlinked with an explicit warning; no path/object fallback key is synthesized.
- Hard identity/link conflicts fail safely and are not misreported as existing files.
- No migration, no `frame_uid` rewrite, no Frame merge/delete, no Stage 2/M0--M5/M8 scientific change.

Downstream field/series construction is still Frame-row based. P4c must define deterministic representative-product selection before known duplicate physical exposures are permitted into the production science workflow.

# Grandgousier 0.5.55.0

Stage-2 provenance-aware readiness for Stage 3/M8.

## What changed

- Added a shared `stage3_scale_v1` recipe contract in `grandgousier.pipeline.recipe_contracts`.
- Published SCIENCE generations can now be classified from their producing `pipeline_runs.recipe_json` as:
  - `READY_STAGE3_RECIPE`;
  - `RECIPE_MISMATCH`;
  - `MISSING_PROVENANCE`.
- `plan-interseries-calibration` accepts read-only `--required-stage2-recipe stage3_scale_v1` and excludes incompatible/unknown-provenance series from the READY graph.
- M8 always applies the selected `--stage2-recipe` readiness contract before treating an existing series as READY, and propagates the same contract through M0/M1-M4 selection.
- `--resume` never turns recipe mismatch or missing provenance into a hidden rerun. Such batches are `STOP_CONFLICT`; an existing DONE series must be rebuilt explicitly.
- M8 writes `stage2_recipe_readiness.csv` and includes the same machine-readable information in `final_report.json` / HTML.

## Compatibility semantics

The contract compares persisted scientific settings, not calibration names, paths, run ids, output files or quality-gate outcomes. `color_calibration_activated=false` is therefore not a mismatch when color calibration was requested by the recipe.

The canonical execution recipe remains `ensemble_min_ref_stars_per_frame=30`. Existing field-33 production includes real-validated series 78 produced with 20; readiness accepts exactly the real-validated values `20` and `30` and records a compatibility note when the value differs from canonical 30. New `stage3_scale_v1` runs still use 30.

This keeps production series 76--93 usable without hard-coding field/series IDs. Older incomplete provenance such as historical 74/75 is not guessed from calibration names.

## Not changed

- No DB migration.
- No Stage-2 numerical algorithm change.
- No weakening of `NO_DETECTION_SUPPORT` or other Stage-3 reference vetoes.
- No automatic rebuild of DONE series.
- No Observation/P4 semantics change.
- No M4 sign/order, covariance, M5 rejection or plotting change.
- Existing M4 generation fingerprints do not include readiness metadata, so identical source SCIENCE generations/policies continue to reuse the same M4 generation.

# 0.6.0.1 — Stage-1 ProductStore date hotfix

The first Windows/full-science validation of 0.6.0 produced a READY five-item MASTER metadata-only plan and a READY frozen `gpx_tf17_2` acceptance with no unexpected database writes. The plan also exposed a narrow ProductStore layout defect: canonical `observed_at` values were serialized with an explicit UTC offset (`+00:00`), but the legacy Astropy `isot` parsing branch used while constructing the product path did not accept that suffix, so planned products were placed under `undated/`.

0.6.0.1 accepts standard Python ISO-8601 forms, including explicit offsets and `Z`, before falling back to the existing Astropy parser. Offset-aware values are normalized to UTC; naive timestamps retain the existing Grandgousier convention of being interpreted as UTC. Regression coverage verifies the canonical `+00:00` form, non-zero offset normalization, and dated ProductStore paths.

There is no database migration and no change to observation identity, MASTER reduction mathematics, Stage-2/Stage-3 science, CLI/config schema, or asset materialization behavior.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.6.1.0.md`

# 0.6.1.0 — Canonical Stage-1 execution and ProductStore provenance

0.6.1.0 adds the first explicit execution layer behind the source-neutral Stage-1 contract that was real-validated in 0.6.0.1. It does not change the MASTER calibration formula, Stage-2/Stage-3 science, the database schema, or observation-identity rules.

The new `stage1-execute` command rebuilds and writes the exact canonical plan it will execute, then materializes only the assets required by READY items. A plan containing any BLOCKED item is refused as a whole; partial execution is not performed.

Supported execution paths in this release are deliberately narrow:

- `IMPORT_PROCESSED`: byte-preserving copy from a filesystem/FITS source into the configured filesystem ProductStore;
- `REDUCE_RAW` for MASTER: delegates to the existing `MASTER_DARK_FLAT_V1` reducer and therefore preserves the accepted `(raw-SDARK)/SFLAT`, separate processing-header, WCS, DQ and validation semantics.

Each successful product receives a `*.provenance.json` sidecar containing stable source/native observation identity, exact asset refs, SHA-256 checksums, recipe parameters, a deterministic input/recipe fingerprint and product checksum. Repeated execution with the same inputs validates the sidecar and product checksum and returns `SKIPPED_EXISTING`. Changed inputs or a mismatched existing product are refused unless the operator explicitly uses `--overwrite`. Existing MASTER outputs without the canonical sidecar are not adopted automatically: legacy FITS provenance cards identify source paths but cannot prove the exact input bytes, so canonical execution requires an explicit `--overwrite` rebuild before stamping checksum provenance. Byte-identical processed imports can be adopted safely because source and destination bytes can be compared directly.

Execution writes products and sidecars only. It does not write Grandgousier DB state and does not automatically invoke Stage 2 in this release. The next integration gate is a small real MASTER execute smoke followed by a second idempotency run and the frozen `gpx_tf17_2` acceptance check.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.6.1.1.md`

# 0.6.1.1 — MASTER partial-cache materialization hotfix

0.6.1.1 fixes the first real Windows `stage1-execute` failure from 0.6.1.0. The canonical plan was READY, but `MasterCacheAssetProvider` treated the configured cache as complete and failed immediately when a science raw had previously been pruned from disk.

MASTER storage is intentionally a partial cache: science raw files may be deleted after a validated processed product exists, while processing headers and shared SDARK/SFLAT products are retained. Explicit Stage-1 execution must therefore materialize only the selected missing assets instead of requiring a complete mirror of the remote archive.

Changes:

- MASTER metadata and asset cache roots are independent. `metadata.cache_root` is used for metadata/header enrichment; `assets.cache_root` is the primary materialization/write cache.
- `assets.search_roots` may list additional read-only/local cache roots. The metadata cache root is also searched automatically.
- `stage1-execute` reuses any matching local asset from those roots before network access.
- If a selected MASTER asset is absent and `assets.fetch_missing` is true (default), the full repository checkout lazily imports the existing `internal_tools.master_remote` transport and downloads only that missing ref into `assets.cache_root`.
- One authenticated HTTP session is reused for all missing assets in the command and closed after execution.
- `stage1-plan` is unchanged and remains metadata-only/offline with respect to asset materialization.
- Public wheel/sdist still do not contain private MASTER transport code or endpoints. If repository-local transport is unavailable, execution gives an explicit precondition error and users may prefetch with `master-archive-fetch`.

No calibration formula, Observation identity rule, DB schema, Stage-2/Stage-3 science semantics, or product-fingerprint format changes.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.6.2.0.md`

# 0.6.2.0 — Exact Stage-1 -> Stage-2 handoff

0.6.2.0 connects the REAL-VALIDATED Stage-1 ProductStore execution layer to the existing Observation-aware Stage-2 ingestion without scanning unrelated ProductStore content.

The new `stage1-handoff` command consumes one canonical Stage-1 execution report. Before any DB write it verifies each named product and provenance sidecar, recomputes the product SHA-256, reads the FITS physical observation identity, and runs the existing P4 science-input planner.

Key safety behavior:

- only FITS products explicitly named by the execution report are eligible;
- report and provenance must agree on product store/backend/locator as well as checksum, fingerprint and observation identity;
- no ProductStore directory scan, copy, hardlink or temporary FITS staging is used;
- the real ProductStore path remains the `Frame.raw_path`/file-product identity input;
- `ALREADY_REPRESENTED` observations are retained as audit context and are not indexed as alternate Frame representatives;
- ambiguous products, identity conflicts, missing identities and historical multiple representatives block the whole handoff before DB writes;
- execution delegates selected exact paths to the existing `process_archive_path` implementation through a list-based input boundary; Stage-2 scientific defaults/algorithms are not replaced;
- the default command mode is read-only preflight; `--execute` is required for DB/Stage-2 work;
- an exception from the nested Stage-2 call is preserved as a `FAILED` handoff report instead of losing the handoff audit record.

There is no DB migration and no change to `MASTER_DARK_FLAT_V1`, P4 identity rules, Stage-2 photometry, Stage-3 or M5.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.6.2.1.md`

# 0.6.2.1 — Historical multiple-representative handoff no-op

0.6.2.1 is a narrow hotfix over 0.6.2.0. The first real P0 handoff exposed a frozen historical P4 condition for MASTER observation `204_15814`: two existing Frame products are already present in `field_series_frames` via series 74 and 76.

The general P4 selector intentionally continues to report `EXISTING_MULTIPLE_REPRESENTATIVES`; no historical row is deleted, reassigned, merged or otherwise repaired. At the Stage-1 handoff boundary, however, that condition is now retained as a safe no-op instead of blocking the whole handoff. Multiple existing representatives prove that the physical observation is already represented, so the ProductStore FITS must not be indexed as a third Frame and Stage 2 must not run for it.

The handoff report preserves `p4_action=EXISTING_MULTIPLE_REPRESENTATIVES`, `selected_frame_id=null`, and the existing series ids for audit. Its handoff `status` is `ALREADY_REPRESENTED`; `selected_for_stage2=0`, `blocked=0`, and `stage2_invoked=false`.

No migration, reduction, P4 identity rule, Stage-2/Stage-3/M5 scientific algorithm, or frozen historical database state changes.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.6.3.0.md`

# 0.6.3.0 — Python science-flag storage compaction

0.6.3.0 is a storage-only optimization for the retained `science_measurements`
layer. It does not change photometric scalar equations, normalized calibration
terms, Stage-2/Stage-3 selection policy, P4 observation identity, or Stage-1
handoff behavior.

## Motivation from the real production database

A read-only audit of the Windows production database found about 72 GB total
storage with 10,151,494 retained `science_measurements`. The rows split into:

- 5,723,538 `RECONSTRUCTED_NORMALIZED` rows produced by the Python fallback;
- 4,427,956 `POSTGRESQL_SERVER_RECONSTRUCTION_V7_MAP` rows produced by the
  PostgreSQL compact fast path.

Sampled `flags` size was about 3.2 kB/row for the Python fallback versus roughly
1.1 kB/row for the server path. The audit also showed that many large provenance
keys are constant inside `(calibration_version_id, frame_id)`, while object-level
keys make the complete JSON payload unique per measurement.

The server path has already stored compact science-only flags since the 0.5.40.x
storage work. The remaining asymmetry was the Python compatibility path, whose
row writer still copied the complete accumulated effective flag mapping into the
science table.

## New fallback storage contract

Python reconstruction now keeps one immutable in-memory reference to the BASE
flag mapping and stores only the top-level SCIENCE delta:

`compact = {k: effective[k] | k not in BASE or effective[k] != BASE[k]}`

The public flag contract is unchanged because readers already expose
`BASE || SCIENCE`, with SCIENCE taking precedence. Exact duplicate BASE keys are
therefore redundant in the stored science row.

The compact fallback also records normalized science provenance identifiers:

- `science_provenance_normalized=true`;
- `science_base_calibration_version_id`;
- `science_calibration_version_id`.

The result telemetry marker for the Python path is now
`science_flags_strategy=BASE_DELTA_EFFECTIVE_FLAGS_V1`.

## Memory safety

The reconstruction state does not copy the large BASE JSON twice. `flags` and
`_base_flags` initially reference the same immutable dictionary; calibration
stages replace `flags` with a copied mapping on first mutation, leaving the BASE
snapshot available for final delta calculation.

## Existing databases

No migration and no automatic rewrite are performed. Existing historical science
rows remain readable exactly as before. The patch prevents future Python fallback
materializations from repeating unchanged BASE provenance.

Re-materializing an existing immutable SCIENCE generation under 0.6.3.0 will
rewrite that generation using the compact fallback contract when the Python path
is required. This changes storage representation only; scalar science parity must
still be checked with the existing verification commands.

Reclaiming filesystem space from already rewritten/deleted PostgreSQL tuples is a
separate maintenance operation and is deliberately not performed by this patch.

## Validation

Regression coverage verifies that:

- compacting exact BASE duplicates preserves the effective `BASE || SCIENCE`
  mapping;
- changed values, new keys, nested values and explicit nulls remain in SCIENCE;
- the Python row writer no longer copies legacy-target flags or unchanged BASE
  flags;
- source measurement identity and scalar reconstruction remain unchanged;
- the PostgreSQL V7 compact fast path is untouched.

# Grandgousier 0.6.3.1

Narrow safety hotfix over 0.6.3.0.

- Legacy target measurements remain the preferred shadow baseline when present.
- Otherwise the existing immutable `science_measurements` product is used as the scalar baseline, matching `verify-science-materialization`.
- If neither baseline exists, the command refuses before deleting any SCIENCE rows.
- Adds `shadow_comparison_source` and `shadow_baseline_rows` to materialization diagnostics.
- No schema migration; no photometric/science changes; no change to BASE-delta flag storage.

## Архивный источник: `docs/releases/0.6.3.2.md`

# Grandgousier 0.6.3.2

## Historical science flag-preservation hotfix

The first real 0.6.3.1 storage compaction of calibration 1094 proved scalar photometric parity but exposed that historical effective `science_measurements.flags` are not guaranteed to equal flags reconstructed today from normalized terms. The write succeeded and reduced average stored SCIENCE flags from 3214 to 1976 bytes per row, but the aggregate effective JSONB hash changed.

0.6.3.2 therefore makes shadow-checked historical rematerialization use the exact shadow baseline effective flag mapping as the compaction source. Legacy target `measurements.flags` are used directly when legacy rows exist. When the baseline is an existing SCIENCE product, its public effective view is reconstructed as immutable BASE flags overlaid by the existing SCIENCE flags. The stored row is then the exact top-level BASE delta of that baseline. No new provenance keys are synthesized during an exact historical shadow rewrite.

Scalar reconstruction remains authoritative for photometric values and is still checked before any delete. BASE measurement identity is also required to match when an existing SCIENCE product is the shadow baseline. New/non-shadow materializations retain the 0.6.3.0 normalized provenance keys.

No schema migration or scientific calibration formula changes are included.
