## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_38_2_OBJECT_QC_PERFORMANCE_MASTER_BV_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.38.2 — Object-QC performance and MASTER B/V calibration

Patch поверх 0.5.38.1. Миграция БД не требуется.

## Причина

Контрольные MASTER-серии `TIC13533330_01` показали время 30–40 минут на 66 кадров. Manifest timings локализовали основной расход в `compute_object_qc`: два прохода занимали около 20 минут. Старый алгоритм строил neighbor statistics полным Python-перебором всех Gaia-источников поля: примерно `18 916 × 18 916` угловых расстояний на каждый QC-проход, хотя science measurements имелись только для 819–827 объектов.

## Оптимизация Object QC

- neighbor geometry вычисляется только для реально измеренных `source_id` против полного каталога;
- pair calculation выполняется точным векторизованным haversine-алгоритмом блоками NumPy;
- статическая геометрия кэшируется между повторными QC-проходами одного pipeline process;
- nearest-neighbor distance и counts в радиусах 3/5/10 arcsec сохраняют прежнюю семантику;
- в step result добавлены algorithm/provenance и детальные `timings_sec`.

Synthetic benchmark, соответствующий контрольному полю MASTER:

- catalog sources: 18 916;
- measured objects: 827;
- old work scale: 357 815 056 Python pair evaluations per pass;
- new work scale: 15 643 532 vectorized pair evaluations;
- first geometry pass: около 1.2 s в упаковочной среде;
- cached repeat: около 0.004 s.

Это не означает, что весь pipeline будет занимать 1.2 s: остаются catalog matching, forced photometry, aperture correction, calibration, field report и database I/O. По реальным timings ожидается сокращение серии порядка 30 минут до нескольких минут; точное значение необходимо проверить на той же `WEST_R` серии.

## Target-resolution fast path

При отрицательном `target_max_sep_arcsec` и отсутствии explicit target IDs resolver теперь возвращает `DISABLED_UNRESOLVED` до запросов calibration/frame-centre/nearest-object. Это устраняет 15–16 s лишней работы в массовом режиме без target map.

## MASTER B/V

Pan-STARRS rows теперь дополнительно содержат synthetic Johnson B/V для stellar calibrators по Tonry et al. (2012), Table 6:

- `B - gP1 = 0.212 + 0.556(g-r) + 0.034(g-r)^2`;
- `V - rP1 = 0.005 + 0.462(g-r) + 0.013(g-r)^2`.

Transformation scatter (`0.032 mag` для B, `0.012 mag` для V) включается в propagated reference error. В reference provenance сохраняется `synthetic_bv_transform=tonry2012_table6_stellar_vega`.

`configs/master.yaml` включает B/V color calibration с `g-r`. Это калибровка через stellar color equations, а не synthetic photometry произвольного SED; для не-звёздных объектов и strongly structured spectra абсолютная привязка требует отдельной проверки.

## Совместимость

- science formulas forced photometry/aperture correction/ensemble не меняются;
- object flags должны быть идентичны legacy result с точностью spherical-distance calculation;
- R/I policy сохраняется;
- existing Pan-STARRS scoped catalogs без `mag_b/mag_v` будут автоматически дополнены при первом B/V run;
- миграция БД не требуется.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_38_3_CALIBRATION_ANALYSIS_SNAPSHOT_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.38.3 — calibration-analysis snapshot and database access optimization

Patch поверх 0.5.38.2. Требуется одна миграция БД.

## Причина

После устранения квадратичного neighbor search контрольная серия из 159 кадров заняла около 1013 s, из них сам pipeline — около 719 s. Численная обработка измерений уже занимала доли секунды, но одни и те же примерно 75 тысяч строк `measurements` многократно читались через PostgreSQL и гидратировались как полные ORM-объекты.

Два `compute_object_qc` прохода тратили примерно:

- `load_object_scatter_rows`: 29.4 + 28.2 s;
- `load_measurement_geometry`: 25.4 + 28.7 s;
- собственно object loop: около 0.014 s суммарно.

Кроме того, каждый `field_qc_report` повторно загружал scatter rows, а `build_candidate_triage()` делал ещё одну такую загрузку внутри отчёта. Random-error validation снова читала тот же calibration layer.

## Изменения

### 1. Calibration-analysis snapshot

Добавлен `CalibrationAnalysisSnapshot`:

- measurements загружаются скалярным SQL-запросом без создания десятков тысяч ORM `Measurement`/`Frame`/`Object` экземпляров;
- frame JSON загружается и декодируется один раз на кадр, а не один раз на measurement;
- object metadata загружается один раз на реально измеренный объект;
- из одного снимка строятся object scatter и measurement geometry;
- тот же снимок используется Object QC, candidate triage, field report и random-error validation.

Pipeline хранит LRU-кэш максимум из двух снимков. Это позволяет одновременно держать текущую science calibration и её source layer, но не накапливать все итерационные calibration layers в памяти.

### 2. Устранена двойная загрузка внутри field report

`build_field_qc_report()` передаёт уже вычисленные `object_rows` в `build_candidate_triage()`. Внутренняя повторная загрузка measurement layer больше не выполняется.

### 3. Индекс measurements с calibration-first access path

Добавлена миграция:

```text
scripts/migrate_mvp5_38_3_measurement_calibration_index.sql
```

Она создаёт индекс:

```sql
CREATE INDEX ix_measurements_calibration_object_frame
ON measurements (calibration_version_id, object_id, frame_id);
```

Legacy unique index `(object_id, frame_id, calibration_version_id)` не заменяет этот индекс: почти все тяжёлые QC-запросы начинают фильтрацию с `calibration_version_id`.

### 4. Более крупные безопасные bulk batches

Default bulk batch size увеличен с 1000 до 3000 строк. Фактический размер по-прежнему ограничивается функцией `safe_bulk_insert_batch_size()` по пределу bind parameters PostgreSQL, поэтому широкие rows автоматически разбиваются на меньшие пакеты.

`COPY`/temporary table/`INSERT ... SELECT ... ON CONFLICT` в этот patch не включены. Это остаётся следующим уровнем оптимизации калибровочных записей после измерения эффекта snapshot и индекса.

## Применение миграции

Из корня проекта:

```powershell
psql -U grandgousier -d grandgousier -h localhost `
  -f scripts\migrate_mvp5_38_3_measurement_calibration_index.sql
```

Либо выполнить cumulative migration:

```powershell
psql -U grandgousier -d grandgousier -h localhost `
  -f scripts\migrate_all.sql
```

## Проверка

```powershell
python -m compileall grandgousier
python -m pytest -q
```

Упаковочная проверка: `125 passed, 8 skipped`.

В новом manifest проверить:

- `compute_object_qc.result.analysis_snapshot_algorithm`;
- `analysis_snapshot_cache_hit`;
- `analysis_snapshot_measurements`;
- `timings_sec.analysis_snapshot_db_load`;
- `field_qc_report.result` и `field_qc_report_color_calibrated.result`;
- `validate_random_error_model.result.analysis_snapshot_cache_hit`;
- времена `aperture_zp_calibrate`, `apply_aperture_correction`, `ensemble_calibrate`, `apply_color_calibration` после увеличения batch size.

Реалистичная цель для той же 159-frame серии — 7–10 минут для первого объекта и 4–7 минут для следующих фильтров того же объекта. Это целевой диапазон, а не подтверждённый benchmark: фактическое время зависит от диска, PostgreSQL cache state и внешних catalog operations.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_38_4_CANDIDATE_REFERENCE_NOOP_GUARD_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.38.4 — candidate reference no-op guard

## Проблема

Candidate-excluded ensemble pass запускался по факту наличия accepted candidate IDs. Он не проверял, входят ли эти objects в текущий reference ensemble. Поэтому при `requested_excluded_reference_objects > 0` и `actually_excluded_reference_objects = 0` создавался идентичный calibration layer и повторно выполнялись Object QC и field report.

## Исправление

Первичный ensemble pass возвращает `reference_object_ids`. Перед каждой candidate iteration pipeline вычисляет:

```text
requested_excluded_object_ids ∩ current_reference_object_ids
```

Пустое пересечение означает, что recalibration математически не может изменить ensemble offsets. Branch завершается без записи нового слоя.

## Provenance

Selection step добавляет:

```text
reference_precheck_available
input_reference_objects
effective_reference_exclusion_object_ids
effective_reference_exclusion_objects
will_run_iteration
stop_reason
```

Terminal convergence:

```text
stop_status = NO_USABLE_REFERENCE_EXCLUSIONS
stop_reason = no_usable_reference_exclusions
no_op_iteration_skipped = true
iterations_executed = 0
```

Миграция БД не требуется.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_39_1_SCHEMA_MIGRATION_LEDGER_PATCH.md`

# MVP5.39.1 — managed schema migration ledger

Патч применяется поверх **0.5.39.0** и не меняет фотометрические алгоритмы или научные результаты.

## Что добавлено

- таблица `schema_migrations` в SQLAlchemy schema contract;
- детерминированный manifest всех миграций до текущей версии;
- SHA-256 контроль SQL migration files;
- безопасное принятие (`BASELINED`) истории существующей pre-ledger БД только после structural validation;
- managed runner для новых миграций;
- команды `schema-status` и `migrate-db`;
- свежие `init-db`/`reset-db` автоматически получают baseline ledger;
- исторические SQL migration scripts никогда автоматически не переисполняются managed runner'ом.

## Обновление существующей БД 0.5.38.3+

Один раз выполнить:

```powershell
python -m grandgousier.cli migrate-db --adopt-legacy
python -m grandgousier.cli schema-status
```

`--adopt-legacy` не запускает старые миграции повторно. Перед записью истории проверяются ключевые таблицы, колонки, индекс `ix_measurements_calibration_object_frame` и unique constraint detection idempotency.

Ожидаемый итог:

```text
schema migrations: total=17, applied=1, baselined=16, pending=0, checksum_drift=0
```

## Проверка без изменений БД

```powershell
python -m grandgousier.cli migrate-db --adopt-legacy --dry-run
```

Для уже принятой БД:

```powershell
python -m grandgousier.cli migrate-db --dry-run
```

## Важное правило для следующих патчей

Новые managed migration scripts не должны содержать psql meta-commands (`\\ir`, `\\set` и т.п.). Runner выполняет каждый новый SQL script и запись его ledger row в одной транзакции PostgreSQL.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_39_5_IMMUTABLE_CALIBRATION_GENERATIONS_PATCH.md`

Идентичное содержимое также было в: `docs/releases/0.5.39.5.md`.

# MVP5.39.5 — Immutable calibration generations and stable heads

Patch over Grandgousier 0.5.39.4.

This patch completes B1b of the data-model refactor without yet removing the
legacy full `measurements` materializations.

## What changes

- `calibration_versions` gains `logical_name`, `generation_no`, and `finalized_at`.
- New `calibration_product_aliases` table stores the explicit logical head.
- The recorded main field pipeline opts into immutable generation semantics for
  forced photometry, aperture correction, aperture ZP, ensemble passes and color
  calibration.
- A completed head is never selected as a write target. Recalculation allocates
  a pending generation, materializes into its new `calibration_version_id`, then
  atomically publishes it as the logical head.
- The previous head is renamed once to a deterministic archival physical name,
  marked `SUPERSEDED_IMMUTABLE`, and remains addressable by primary key.
- `CalibrationVersion.name` remains the current publication/head name for
  backward compatibility with existing readers. This compatibility behavior is
  temporary; `calibration_product_aliases` is the future authoritative resolver.
- Forced-photometry reuse only reuses an immutable base layer if every requested
  catalog link is already materialized. A partial immutable layer causes a new
  generation rather than in-place repair.
- Standalone legacy materializers now refuse to rewrite a completed immutable
  target instead of silently mutating it.
- `product_role` is treated as publication metadata rather than scientific
  content, so an already finalized ensemble can later be promoted from
  `INTERMEDIATE` to `SCIENCE` without changing its content fingerprint.

## Migration

```powershell
python -m grandgousier.cli migrate-db
python -m grandgousier.cli schema-status
```

Expected newest migration:

`mvp5_39_5_calibration_immutable_generations`

No measurement rows are copied by the migration itself. Existing calibration
rows are backfilled as generation 1 and registered as compatibility heads.

## Compatibility note

This patch intentionally still stores one full measurement layer for each
calibration stage. It prevents destructive overwrite and establishes immutable
provenance. Removal of intermediate materialization remains Phase C/D work.

# MVP5.40.1 calibration reconstruction parity patch

This patch completes the second dual-write gate before intermediate measurement-layer removal.

New behavior:

- reconstructs calibration products from the immutable base-photometry layer plus normalized calibration terms;
- verifies scalar photometric parity against the compatibility materialization;
- compares row membership, flux/flux error, instrumental/calibrated magnitude, random/systematic errors, local ZP, centroid and aperture/background state;
- persists the ensemble input-magnitude preference explicitly;
- stores one color-application object term for every science object, including the exact applied color/pivot and correlated systematic error;
- deliberately does not reconstruct legacy measurement JSON flags, because those flags are one of the duplicated structures scheduled for removal.

After a new recompute, verify the final science calibration with:

```powershell
python -m grandgousier.cli verify-calibration-reconstruction --calibration-version-id <ID>
```

A successful result must report `status=OK`, `missing_rows=0`, `extra_rows=0`, and `scalar_mismatches=0` before the materialization cutover is enabled.

No database migration is required; the patch enriches the existing normalized tables introduced in 0.5.40.0.

# MVP5 0.5.47.1 — M5 rejection diagnostics hotfix

The first real M5 smoke used GPX object 29700 and returned 128 exact M4-linked source rows but zero accepted rows. Cross-checking the archived M1-M3 `series_object_states.csv` shows the object is rejected scientifically in all six seed series (saturation/high RMS/catalog residual/proper-motion mismatch plus detection support diagnostics).

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_47_2_M5_PLOT_BUDGET_TIME_BREAKS_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.47.2 - M5 strict plot budget and compressed time axis

0.5.47.2 is a visualization-only M5 patch over 0.5.47.1.

## Strict plot-point budget

`--plot-max-points N` is now a hard per-filter ceiling for automatic/forced binned plots. The previous implementation allocated exactly N bins across series but a measurement exactly at a series `mjd_max` could create bin index N because of the inclusive upper endpoint. 0.5.47.2 stores the allocated `max_bins` for every series and clamps the endpoint into the final allocated bin.

The budget is distributed with a largest-remainder allocation while reserving at least one bin for every non-empty series. If `N` is smaller than the number of non-empty series, M5 refuses the plot instead of silently dropping whole series. Explicit `--plot-bin-minutes` is treated as a minimum bin width and may be made coarser to honor the hard cap.

The exact M5 scientific CSV is unchanged and is never downsampled by plot policy.

## Compressed/broken time axis

New CLI option:

```text
--plot-time-axis auto|continuous|compressed
```

Default `auto` preserves real time differences inside each observing block but shortens large empty gaps between non-overlapping series. The plot marks every shortened gap with `//`; tick labels show the original MJD and, for small series counts, the series id. `continuous` restores ordinary physical MJD spacing. `compressed` requests gap compression whenever a positive gap is large enough to benefit from it.

The transform is display-only. Main CSV and `*_plot.csv` keep the original MJD values.

For up to 12 series the plot keeps the detailed per-series style and legend. Above 12 series it automatically switches to an archive-overview style: one visual style inside the filter and no per-series legend, while time breaks and MJD labels carry the observing-block structure.

## Real GPX motivation

The 0.5.47.1 positive smoke on object 29786 produced 121 accepted rows (R=60, V=61). With `--plot-max-points 20`, the old plot layer emitted 21 points in each filter because the final endpoint opened an extra bin. 0.5.47.2 fixes that off-by-one and makes the multi-night overview readable by compressing the large gaps between series 76/78/79 and 77/80/81.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_47_3_M5_EPOCH_SATURATION_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.47.3 - M5 epoch-level saturation rejection

0.5.47.3 is a narrow M5 scientific-selection hotfix over 0.5.47.2. There is no database migration.

## Real failure that motivated the patch

After adding the full 2018-09-11 GPX_TF17 night, immutable M4 generations 5 (R) and 6 (V) linked 548 exact SCIENCE rows for object 29786. M5 accepted only 121 and rejected 420 new rows as `SATURATED_LIKE`.

The rejection debug product showed that `SATURATED_LIKE` was an object/series-level flag on all 210 V rows and all 210 R rows, but the measurement-level `SATURATED_OR_NEAR_SATURATED` flag was active only on 11 V epochs and 8 R epochs. The old M5 default therefore converted "the object had at least one saturated epoch" into "reject every epoch in the series".

A clean scale-control object 30112 independently verified the M4->M5 linkage: 548 source rows, 538 accepted, 10 `NO_VALID_MAG` rejects.

## New M5 policy

The M5 algorithm provenance is now `global_object_lightcurve_v2`.

Default M5 row rejection:

- keeps object-level `SATURATED_LIKE` in `quality_flags` as diagnostic provenance;
- does not reject a row solely because `SATURATED_LIKE` is active;
- rejects the specific row when measurement-level `SATURATED_OR_NEAR_SATURATED` is active;
- leaves all other generic reject flags unchanged.

Users can deliberately restore the strict object-level behavior with:

```text
--extra-reject-flags SATURATED_LIKE
```

The generic `DEFAULT_REJECT_FLAGS` tuple is not changed. Therefore Stage-2 Object-QC, candidate triage, ensemble-reference selection, M1/M2 reference eligibility, M3/M4 graph products, stored SCIENCE values and database schema are unchanged.

## Expected real replay

For object 29786 with field 33 and M4 generations 5+6:

```text
source_rows = 548
accepted    = 519
rejected    = 29
SATURATED_OR_NEAR_SATURATED = 19
NO_VALID_MAG                 = 10
```

For object 30112 the result should remain 538/548 accepted with 10 `NO_VALID_MAG` rejects.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_48_0_M8_FIELD_ARCHIVE_ORCHESTRATION_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.48.0 — M8 field-archive orchestration

This patch turns the validated manual Stage-3 scale workflow into one resumable native Grandgousier command while keeping all scientific stages unchanged.

The new `process-field-archive` command scans FITS leaf directories under a processed root, classifies each batch against the current DB, skips already READY data when resuming, processes only new/incomplete batches with the frozen `stage3_scale_v1` recipe, verifies newly selected SCIENCE products, checks shared catalog identity, executes explicit Stage-3 policies, persists/verifies immutable M4 generations, runs optional M5 controls, and writes one consolidated report bundle.

The command deliberately requires explicit Stage-3 policy values. It will not change `min_common_objects` to force graph connectivity. This preserves the GPX_TF17 validation decision where V uses 15 because series 78 has only 16 eligible reference objects, while R remains at 20.

No schema migration is required.

M8 v1 is deliberately fail-closed for ambiguous configuration: exactly one Stage-3 policy may be supplied per filter, and one FITS leaf directory may not span multiple observing calendar dates. Such cases must be resolved explicitly instead of being guessed by orchestration.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_48_1_M8_TOO_SMALL_BATCH_HOTFIX.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.48.1 — M8 too-small batch hotfix

0.5.48.1 is a narrow orchestration hotfix over 0.5.48.0. The first real `process-field-archive` plan correctly found all leaf dates, but classified 2018-09-08 (6 FITS total) and 2018-10-02 (3 FITS total) as `RUN_NEW` even though the frozen Stage-2 production recipe requires `min_frames_per_series=10`.

The hotfix computes a conservative series-like group size from scanner identity `(profile, instrument, site, tube, camera, filter, object)`. For NEW/INCOMPLETE batches where no such group reaches 10 frames, M8 now reports `SKIP_TOO_SMALL` with reason `NO_SERIES_GROUP_MEETS_MIN_FRAMES_PER_SERIES`. The batch is not sent to Stage 2. READY batches retain `SKIP_READY`; excluded dates retain `SKIP_EXCLUDED`; scientific Stage 2 and M0-M5 algorithms are unchanged. No DB migration.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_49_0_PACKAGE_RESOURCES_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.49.0 — package resources / installability foundation

This patch is the first productization implementation after the Stage-2/M0-M5 production-v1 freeze.

The 0.5.48.1 audit proved that wheel/sdist contained Python modules but omitted runtime `configs/*.yaml` and `scripts/*.sql`, while default profile discovery and the migration runner resolved those files relative to the repository root. Therefore an installed wheel was structurally incomplete.

0.5.49.0 moves the runtime contract to installed package resources under `grandgousier/resources/` and explicitly packages them. Root-level `configs/` and `scripts/` are retained for compatibility and developer workflows; source-tree tests require byte-identical copies.

Scientific photometry, Stage-3 formulas, M4/M5 provenance, M8 recipe/policies, frame identity and database schema are unchanged.

Идентичное содержимое также было в: `docs/releases/0.5.52.0.md`.

# Grandgousier 0.5.52.0 — P4a physical observation identity foundation

P4a is an additive, non-destructive schema and maintenance layer over 0.5.51.0. Scientific Stage 2, Stage 3 M0--M5 and M8 are unchanged.

## Added

- `observations` table representing one physical exposure independently of file products;
- nullable `frames.observation_id` FK (`ON DELETE SET NULL`);
- deterministic observation identities:
  - MASTER: `master_uniqnum_v1` from FITS `UNIQNUM`;
  - RoboPhot: `robophot_sernum_dateobs_v1` from FITS `SERNUM + DATE-OBS`; RoboPhot `DATE-OBS` is already UTC and is never shifted from KAO local time;
- `grandgousier.identity` pure identity builders and safe backfill planner;
- `backfill-observation-identity` CLI, plan-only unless `--execute` is supplied;
- reports `summary.json`, `observation_groups.csv`, `frame_identity_issues.csv`;
- managed migration `mvp5_52_0_observation_identity`.

## Safety semantics

- legacy `frames.frame_id` and `frames.frame_uid` are preserved;
- no frame merge/delete/reindex;
- path, file size and mtime never enter physical observation identity;
- `COPY_LIKE` and `PRODUCT_VARIANT` groups may map multiple frame rows to one observation;
- hard metadata conflicts, invalid identities, mismatched existing observations or conflicting links block execution;
- missing native identity metadata is reported and remains unlinked rather than guessed;
- Stage-2 derived reset preserves `observations`.

## Audit basis

The design follows read-only audits of the current database: MASTER 6685 frames with complete `UNIQNUM` coverage -> 6644 expected observations (36 copy-like groups, 5 product variants); RoboPhot 364 frames with complete `SERNUM`/`DATE-OBS` coverage -> 364 observations. Expected combined first backfill if the database is unchanged: 7049 frames -> 7008 observations.

## Deliberately deferred

The archive indexer still uses the legacy file-level `frame_uid` behavior and does not auto-link new frames to observations. That is P4b after the real backfill is validated.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_53_0_OBSERVATION_AWARE_INGESTION_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.53.0 — P4b observation-aware ingestion

P4b connects the real-validated P4a physical-observation model to normal FITS ingestion. It is deliberately a file/identity integrity patch, not a scientific Stage 2/Stage 3 deduplication patch.

## Added/changed

- `index_archive_paths()` now creates or reuses the P4a `Observation` for newly indexed MASTER/RoboPhot Frame products and writes `frames.observation_id` in the same per-file transaction;
- exact legacy `frame_uid` re-index no longer skips before identity reconciliation, so an existing unlinked frame can be repaired without creating another Frame;
- copied/moved FITS and compatible alternate processed products may create a second Frame while reusing the same Observation;
- P4a hard/soft compatibility semantics are factored into a shared helper and reused by backfill and ingestion;
- observation creation uses a nested transaction/savepoint. An Observation unique-key race is recovered only when the exact identity can be re-read and validated;
- the old broad `IntegrityError -> skipped_existing` behavior is narrowed: only a concurrently created exact legacy Frame retains `skipped_existing`; unrelated integrity failures are reported as failures;
- missing/invalid stable identity remains backward-compatible: a new Frame is persisted with `observation_id=NULL` and a `WARNING` ProcessingEvent; no fallback identity is guessed;
- hard physical identity/link conflicts fail the file ingestion and are recorded as an error event.

## Frozen contracts

- no DB migration in 0.5.53.0;
- legacy `frame_id` and `frame_uid=hash(path,size,mtime)` remain unchanged;
- one Observation may have multiple Frame products;
- MASTER identity remains `master_uniqnum_v1` / FITS `UNIQNUM`;
- RoboPhot identity remains `robophot_sernum_dateobs_v1` / FITS `SERNUM + DATE-OBS`, where `DATE-OBS` is already UTC;
- product/file size, path and mtime do not enter physical identity;
- Stage 2, M0--M5 and M8 scientific semantics are unchanged;
- no representative Frame/product is selected per observation in P4b.

## Remaining gate

Real Windows/PostgreSQL validation must first use a controlled copy/move/product test, not the known additional 2018-09-07 GPX_TF17 block. Downstream observation-aware representative-product selection is P4c and remains required before that block can be admitted to science processing.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP5_54_0_OBSERVATION_SCIENCE_INPUT_GUARD_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.54.0 — P4c observation-aware science input guard

P4c closes the next data-integrity gap after the real-validated P4b ingestion layer. It prevents multiple Frame/file products of one physical Observation from being admitted automatically as multiple Stage-2 epochs while deliberately avoiding any heuristic "best product" ranking.

## Behavior

- `build_field_series()` now applies a read-only physical-observation guard before creating `field_series_frames` membership.
- If one Frame product of an Observation is already in `field_series_frames`, it remains the representative and alternate products are classified `ALREADY_REPRESENTED`.
- If an unrepresented Observation has multiple Frame products, all automatic candidates for that Observation are blocked as `AMBIGUOUS_MULTIPLE_PRODUCTS`; no `MIN(frame_id)`, newest-file, largest-file, path, mtime or size heuristic is used.
- If historical data already contain more than one representative Frame for the same Observation, P4c reports `EXISTING_MULTIPLE_REPRESENTATIVES` and does not repair/reassign the history automatically.
- MASTER/RoboPhot Frames with `observation_id=NULL` are blocked from new automatic science-series membership. Instruments without a P4 identity scheme retain legacy behavior.
- Distinct Observations remain distinct even when timestamps coincide, preserving the RoboPhot simultaneous-camera contract.

## `process-archive-path`

Planning now derives the existing P4 physical identity while each FITS header is already being scanned and produces a read-only projected science-input decision before `--execute`.

Execution applies the persisted Frame guard after indexing and before new series membership. A directory containing only alternate products of already represented/ambiguous Observations stops before catalog/network/Stage-2 work and returns safely with diagnostics.

When `--manifest-out` is supplied, the manifest contains `observation_selection_results` and a sibling `*_observation_selection.csv` with per-file action/reason, physical identity, current products and existing series IDs.

## Frozen contracts

- no DB migration in 0.5.54.0;
- P4a/P4b Observation identity and ingestion semantics are unchanged;
- `frame_uid` remains legacy file identity;
- multiple Frames per Observation remain allowed in the archive DB;
- no existing `field_series_frames` membership is deleted or reassigned;
- Stage-2 photometry/calibration/QC and Stage-3 M0--M5/M8 numerical semantics are unchanged;
- P4c is a membership guard, not an automatic processing-product quality selector.

## P4b real-validation baseline incorporated

Before P4c development, 0.5.53.0 was real-validated on Windows/PostgreSQL: 108 targeted tests passed, schema remained 26 migrations with zero pending/drift, controlled MASTER copy created Frame 7050 reusing Observation 401, controlled RoboPhot copy created Frame 7051 reusing Observation 19, and exact re-index of both copies produced `inserted=0, skipped_existing=1`.

## Next gate

Real-validate 0.5.54.0 first on Frames 7050/7051 using plan-only `process-archive-path`; both should be `ALREADY_REPRESENTED` if their original Frames are already series members. Then run plan-only diagnostics on the additional 2018-09-07 GPX_TF17 block. Do not remove the production exclusion until that audit shows deterministic safe behavior and any genuinely new physical observations are understood.

## Local release validation

After the final P4c compatibility/concurrency changes, the source tree passed:

```text

152 passed, 10 skipped # expanded frozen public API + Stage-3/M5 + identity/P4c set
```

# Grandgousier 0.5.54.1 — P4c process-archive replay NOOP hotfix

This is a narrow orchestration hotfix over the real-validated P4c science-input guard in 0.5.54.0.

## Cause

`process-archive-path` correctly selected only new physical Observations, but then merged `created_series_ids` with every pre-existing series reached through any input path. On the GPX_TF17 2018-09-07 replay this resurrected historical series 74/75 and reran them together with the new series 92/93. Series 74/75 are only 3/2 frames and fail the ensemble precondition, causing the whole replay to report `FAILED` even though P4c had selected no new science input.

## Fix

- ordinary process-by-path mode now queues only series created/rebuilt from Frames selected by the P4c guard in the current invocation;
- if P4c returns zero selected Frames, execution stops before catalog/network/Stage-2 work;
- pre-existing series found only through blocked `ALREADY_REPRESENTED` / `EXISTING_MULTIPLE_REPRESENTATIVES` inputs are audit context, not implicit rerun requests;
- intentional rerun of an existing series remains available through explicit `--series-id`;
- no DB migration and no Stage-2/Stage-3 numerical change.

## Real baseline motivating the hotfix

P4c real validation on GPX_TF17 2018-09-07 produced 272 Frame products -> 222 new Observations -> two new series 92/93 with 111 unique Observations each and zero overlap with old series. `multiple_existing_representatives` remained at the historical baseline 41. Post-ingest identity audit: 7323 Frames, 7230 Observations, missing/invalid/collision/unlinked/link-conflict all zero.

## Local release validation

```text

source expanded:       161 passed, 9 skipped
fresh 0.5.54.0 overlay targeted: 102 passed, 4 skipped
fresh 0.5.54.0 overlay expanded: 161 passed, 9 skipped

wheel + sdist: OK
public artifact privacy scan: 0 forbidden MASTER hits
```

# Grandgousier 0.5.54.2 — M4 canonical edge persistence hotfix

Narrow hotfix over 0.5.54.1. The real GPX_TF17 V graph contains a valid planner-oriented edge `(92,78)`, while the immutable M4 table has the long-standing check `left_series_id < right_series_id`. M1--M3 accepts either orientation, but persistence previously copied it verbatim and PostgreSQL rejected the row.

The fix canonicalizes every persisted edge to `(min(series_id), max(series_id))`. If orientation changes, the signs of `measured_delta_mag`, `predicted_delta_mag`, `closure_residual_mag` and `standardized_residual` are reversed together. `measured_err_mag`, scatter, counts and calibrator object sets are orientation-invariant and are copied unchanged.

No migration. M1--M3 analysis/output, global offsets, SCIENCE source mapping, generation fingerprint and reliability classification are unchanged. The CLI transaction remains atomic; a failed insert leaves no partial generation, although PostgreSQL sequence numbers may have gaps.

## Local validation

- exact reconstructed base: full 0.5.52.0 + official 0.5.53.0 + 0.5.54.0 + 0.5.54.1 overlays;
- source targeted/frozen set: 142 passed, 8 skipped;
- exact fresh 0.5.54.1 -> 0.5.54.2 overlay: 142 passed, 8 skipped;

- wheel build via `pip wheel --no-build-isolation`: passed;

# Grandgousier 0.5.54.3 — M8 observation-aware resume hotfix

## Problem

After P4c correctly prevented duplicate physical observations from entering new science series, M8 still judged archive completeness by direct Frame membership. GPX_TF17 2018-09-07 therefore appeared `INCOMPLETE / RESUME_INCOMPLETE`: alternate Frame products were unassigned even though their physical Observations already had science representatives. Historical tiny series 74/75 could also poison readiness despite READY representatives 76/77 for the same Observations.

## Fix

`_inspect_batch_db_state()` now resolves P4-linked inputs by `observation_id` in the requested field. A physical Observation is complete when it has a representative series; READY representatives are preferred over non-READY historical duplicates, with deterministic ranking by science-frame coverage and series id. Legacy NULL identities keep the old frame-level guard.

## Safety

No migration, no deletion/reassignment, no P4c selection change, no Stage-2/M0--M5 numerical change. Truly unrepresented Observations and direct cross-field conflicts remain blocking.

# 0.5.58.1 release install-smoke isolation hotfix

Narrow operational hotfix over 0.5.58.0. No database schema, photometry, Stage-2, Stage-3, M5, acceptance baseline or scientific semantics change.

## Problem

When `tools/release_check.py` was executed from a full-science venv that already contained Grandgousier 0.5.57.0, the temporary wheel install succeeded but `wheel_install_smoke` ended in a bare `AssertionError`. The old smoke added the temporary target to `sys.path`, but still executed under the active environment and did not prove the imported package/resource actually came from that target.

## Fix

- `pip install --target` now also uses `--ignore-installed`;
- smoke subprocess runs with `python -I -S`;
- the temporary wheel target is explicitly prepended to `sys.path`;
- imported `grandgousier.__file__` must resolve under the temporary target;
- bundled `master.yaml` must exist and resolve under the same target;
- package version must equal the wheel version;
- failures report concrete origin/resource/version details instead of a bare assertion.

This is release tooling only. The 0.5.58.0 frozen science acceptance contract is unchanged.

Operational/self-service milestone built on the fully REAL-VALIDATED 0.5.58.1 full-science release.

## Scope

No database migration and no scientific algorithm change. Stage 2, Stage 3/M0–M5, observation identity, acceptance baselines and calibration semantics are unchanged.

## Changes

- Every `process-field-archive` service job now writes a self-contained run bundle under `<out_root>/_jobs/<job_id>/`.
- New `run_manifest.json` records Grandgousier version, Python/platform runtime, plan/execute mode, secret-safe resolved config and the existing private config fingerprint.
- New `diagnosis.json` stores a stable recovery code, severity, summary and recommended actions for READY, plan-only and failure outcomes.
- New bootstrap-safe command:
  `grandgousier diagnose-run <job-dir-or-job_summary.json>`.
- `diagnose-run` also understands legacy pre-0.5.59 job directories and reports which modern bundle artifacts are missing.
- Recovery guidance covers runtime readiness failures, advisory-lock conflicts, Stage-2 provenance/recipe conflicts, missing detection support, catalog preconditions, disconnected Stage-3 graphs, interruptions and unexpected exceptions.
- CLI now prints run-bundle, manifest and diagnosis paths after `process-field-archive`.
- Database URLs remain redacted from bundle configuration/manifest artifacts; only the existing SHA-256 config fingerprint can depend on the private URL.

A normal 0.5.59+ job directory contains:

- `run_manifest.json`
- `job_config.json`
- `job_events.jsonl`

- `diagnosis.json`
- `failure.json` only for failures

M8 `final_report.json`/`report.html` remain in the normal report root and are referenced from the job summary.

The patch is expected to preserve the 0.5.58.1 full-science acceptance baseline exactly. Real validation should check the new bundle on a plan-only field-33 job and run `diagnose-run` on that bundle; write-capable science processing is not required because no science path changed.

# Grandgousier 0.5.59.1 — clean release-build staging hotfix

This is a narrow release-tooling hotfix over 0.5.59.0.

## Real failure

On Windows, `tools/release_check.py` built wheel metadata for 0.5.59.0 but the isolated wheel smoke imported `grandgousier.__version__ == 0.5.58.1`. The wheel was installed from the temporary target correctly; the stale version had already been copied into the wheel from an old local `build/lib` tree. Overlay ZIPs preserve source mtimes, so setuptools could consider the old staged module newer than the newly overlaid source.

## Fix

Before each clean release build, `tools/release_check.py` now removes:

- `dist/`;
- `build/`;
- root-level `*.egg-info`.

The build backend therefore always stages Python modules from the current source tree. The 0.5.58.1 wheel-import isolation (`--ignore-installed`, `python -I -S`, origin/resource checks) remains unchanged.

## Scope

No database migration, science algorithm, acceptance baseline, run-bundle format or CLI workflow changed.

## Regression

A regression test seeds a future-dated stale `build/lib/grandgousier/__init__.py` with version 0.5.58.1 and verifies that release build cleanup removes it before invoking the backend.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP6_0_0_STAGE1_ARCHIVE_SOURCE_CONTRACT_PATCH.md`

# Grandgousier 0.6.0 — Stage 1 archive-source contract foundation

Base: **0.5.59.1** (fully REAL-VALIDATED on the user's Windows/full-science environment).

Status of this patch: **prepared and locally/container validated only**. It is not REAL-VALIDATED until the Windows/full-science acceptance gate is repeated.

## Scope

0.6.0 introduces a generic Stage-1 boundary without changing Stage-2/Stage-3 scientific semantics:

- canonical `ArchiveRequest`, `ArchiveSourceDescriptor`, `ObservationRecord`, `AssetRef`, `CalibrationGroup`, `CalibrationPlan`, `ProductRef`;
- separate `MetadataProvider`, `AssetProvider` and `ProductStore` responsibilities;
- `fits-filesystem` and `master-manifest` adapters;
- metadata-only `stage1-plan` command and JSON/CSV manifests;
- a filesystem ProductStore independent of the source archive;
- path-independent source provenance based on `archive_source_id + native_observation_id`;
- integration with the existing P4 observation identity rules rather than a second identity system;
- secret-safe serialization of archive/product configuration.

No database migration is added. Existing MASTER reduction code, `process-archive-path`, Stage 2 recipes, Stage 3 calibration and acceptance semantics are unchanged.

## Identity rules

- MASTER native physical identity remains `UNIQNUM`.
- RoboPhot remains `SERNUM + DATE-OBS`; `DATE-OBS` is already UTC and no `+05:00` correction is applied.
- Absolute/relative storage paths and legacy `raw_id` are not accepted as replacement physical observation identity.
- Existing path-sensitive `frame_uid` remains a downstream file-product identifier and is not repurposed as Stage-1 observation identity.

The historical MASTER inventory schema does not guarantee `UNIQNUM`. `master-manifest` therefore accepts an authoritative `uniqnum` column or an already cached processing-header FITS containing `UNIQNUM`; otherwise the canonical plan is explicitly `BLOCKED`. This is intentional and prevents silent identity corruption.

## Plan-only semantics

`stage1-plan` performs discovery/header metadata work, canonical normalization, calibration-ref association and ProductStore target planning. It does not call `AssetProvider.materialize`, does not write calibrated FITS, does not invoke Stage 2 and does not mutate the Grandgousier database.

## Validation boundary

Container validation covers unit/regression tests, compilation, manual build and release packaging. Environment-specific full-science checks still belong to the user's Windows/CPython 3.11 environment: strict doctor, a small real MASTER metadata-only plan, frozen `gpx_tf17_2` acceptance with no DB writes, and release check against the validated dependency snapshot/constraints.

## Архивный источник: `README_MVP6_0_1_STAGE1_PRODUCT_DATE_HOTFIX.md`

# Grandgousier 0.6.0.1 — Stage-1 ProductStore date hotfix

Base: **0.6.0** Stage-1 archive-source contract foundation.

The first real Windows MASTER `stage1-plan` was scientifically/architecturally successful (`READY`, 5/5 items, no materialization, no DB writes), but exposed one narrow ProductStore layout defect: canonical `ObservationRecord.observed_at` values such as `2018-09-07T17:04:22+00:00` were serialized correctly, then rejected by the legacy `astropy.time.Time(..., format="isot")` parsing path when ProductStore derived its date directory. Products were therefore planned under `undated/` despite a valid observation time.

0.6.0.1 fixes only that parser/layout defect:

- `parse_datetime()` now accepts standard ISO-8601 offset-aware strings (including `Z`) before the existing Astropy fallback;
- parsed offset-aware times are normalized to UTC;
- naive ISO inputs keep the historical Grandgousier rule of being interpreted as UTC;
- Stage-1 ProductStore now plans dated paths such as `.../2018/09/07/...` for canonical records carrying `observed_at`;
- regression tests cover canonical `+00:00`, non-zero offset normalization, and the dated ProductStore locator.

No database migration, observation identity rule, MASTER reduction math, Stage-2 recipe, Stage-3 calibration, CLI/config schema, or materialization behavior changes.

The 0.6.0 real validation already established `doctor=READY`, Stage-1 plan `READY` with 5/5 MASTER items, and frozen `gpx_tf17_2` acceptance `READY` with `no_unexpected_db_writes=OK`. 0.6.0.1 must repeat the small Stage-1 plan and frozen acceptance before being called REAL-VALIDATED.

The first real 0.6.1.0 Windows execution gate reached a READY canonical MASTER plan but failed on materialization because the selected science raw was not present under the configured local cache. That is a valid MASTER lifecycle state: raw files can be pruned after successful reduction while processing headers and shared calibration assets remain local.

0.6.1.1 makes MASTER materialization cache-aware instead of cache-complete:

- metadata and asset cache roots are separated;
- multiple local cache roots are searched before any transfer;

- the HTTP session is shared within the command and closed after execution;
- `stage1-plan` remains metadata-only and performs no asset downloads;
- public package artifacts continue to exclude the repository-local MASTER transport.

There are no DB migrations and no changes to `MASTER_DARK_FLAT_V1`, P4 identity, Stage 2, Stage 3, or M5.

# Grandgousier 0.6.3.0 — science flag storage compaction

Base: 0.6.2.1.

This patch closes a storage asymmetry between the PostgreSQL server science
materializer and the Python reconstruction fallback. The server path was already
compact; the fallback still copied the complete accumulated flag JSON into every
`science_measurements` row.

0.6.3.0 stores only keys that differ from immutable BASE flags and relies on the
existing backward-compatible `BASE || SCIENCE` reader contract. No schema
migration, photometric formula change, Stage-3 change, observation-identity
change or Stage-1 handoff change is included.

The production audit motivating the patch found 5,723,538 Python-fallback science
rows with sampled flags around 3.2 kB/row. Existing rows are not automatically
rewritten. Re-materialization can be performed later under the existing immutable
SCIENCE workflow after an explicit storage-maintenance plan is reviewed.

## Архивный источник: `README_S1B_PHYSICAL_STORAGE_PROBE.md`

# Grandgousier 0.6.3.2 — S1b transient physical storage probe

This is a development/audit overlay, not a runtime release and does not change the Grandgousier version.

Purpose: resolve the nonlinear PostgreSQL heap/TOAST question left by the read-only S1 audit.

The earlier S1 logical BASE result is valid (`FRAME_CONTEXT || OBJECT_REMAINDER == OLD_FLAGS`), but its projected bytes are logical JSONB bytes. The earlier Science V2 `ROW(...)` aggregate must not be interpreted as physical table size because transient composite construction can detoast large historical JSONB values.

`tools/audit_storage_refactor_s1b_physical.py` therefore measures temporary relations produced by PostgreSQL itself.

Safety boundary:

- only `CREATE TEMP TABLE`, TEMP `INSERT/CTAS`, and TEMP indexes are used;
- no public-schema table is inserted/updated/deleted/altered;
- the complete transaction is explicitly rolled back;
- TEMP relations also disappear when the DB session closes;
- this is non-destructive, but unlike S1 it does perform transient writes to PostgreSQL temporary storage and therefore needs temporary disk space.

The BASE probe compares the same full measurement rows with:

1. current flags;
2. exact object-specific remainder flags plus one frame-context row per `(calibration_version_id, frame_id)`.

It verifies exact merge parity before reporting the physical table saving.

The SCIENCE probe compares, on the exact same sampled rows and with the existing flags unchanged:

1. V1 row;
2. V2 compatibility row without `x`, `y`, `aperture_radius_pix`, `local_background`, `centroid_dx_pix`, `centroid_dy_pix`;
3. V2 core row additionally without `source_measurement_id`.

Equivalent PK/UNIQUE/calibration-frame indexes are built on all three temporary SCIENCE tables, so the reported total includes the prototype indexes. This deliberately isolates only the physical value of narrow scalar storage; science-flag normalization is a separate later decision.

Run from repository root after the successful S1 report:

```powershell
python .\tools\audit_storage_refactor_s1b_physical.py `
  --s1-report-root "reports\storage_refactor_s1_0632_real" `
  --out-root "reports\storage_refactor_s1b_physical_0632_real" `
  --base-frames 32 `
  --science-sample-rows 20000
```

Outputs:

- `summary.json`
- `summary.md`
- `physical_relation_sizes.csv`
- `selected_base_frames.csv`

Do not use this probe as authorization for production migration or cleanup. Structural storage changes remain additive until real parity/acceptance gates are complete.

## Архивный источник: `README_S1C_HOTFIX1_SQLALCHEMY_BIND_CAST.md`

# S1c hotfix 1 — SQLAlchemy bind cast

Fixes the read-only/TEMP storage probe failure caused by PostgreSQL receiving the literal token `:cv::bigint`.
SQLAlchemy `text()` does not reliably recognize a bind parameter immediately followed by PostgreSQL's `::` cast syntax.

Changed only:

```sql
:cv::bigint
```

to:

```sql
CAST(:cv AS bigint)
```

No storage semantics, sample selection, exact effective-flag parity rule, TEMP-table schema, or production data are changed.
Runtime project version remains 0.6.3.2.

Read-only with respect to the public/production schema. The helper creates session-local PostgreSQL TEMP tables, measures them, drops candidates sequentially, and rolls the transaction back.

## 3. Permanent domain rules

## 6. 0.6.3.0 -> 0.6.3.2 science-flag compaction findings

### 6.1. Root defect

Public science flags already have the semantic contract:

```text
EFFECTIVE_FLAGS = BASE.flags || SCIENCE.flags
```

but the Python fallback historically copied the whole accumulated effective flag mapping into `science_measurements.flags`.

0.6.3.0 introduced `BASE_DELTA_EFFECTIVE_FLAGS_V1`: store only top-level keys whose values differ from BASE.

### 6.2. CV 1094 caution

Controlled candidate 1094 (series 92, 222,000 rows) was deliberately chosen because it is `SUPERSEDED_IMMUTABLE` and outside current alias/M4/event/downstream/publication dependencies.

0.6.3.1 successfully rematerialized it with zero scalar mismatches and reduced stored flags:

- avg `3214 -> 1976` bytes/row (~38.5% smaller)
- total logical flag bytes `713,533,186 -> 438,586,308`

However its effective flags hash changed:

- before `4fcd679132acd03231a4d321da775061`
- after `d7a55f41ad2a6d808cf0999cca769ab5`

Cause: today's normalized reconstruction is scalar-equivalent but does not necessarily reproduce every historical diagnostic/provenance flag exactly. The old effective payload cannot be restored from an aggregate MD5 alone. CV 1094 is superseded and outside current Stage-3 dependencies; do not attempt speculative reconstruction of its pre-0.6.3.1 historical flags.

### 6.3. 0.6.3.2 exact preservation gate on untouched CV 1101

0.6.3.2 changed shadow compaction source to the **exact shadow-baseline effective flags**, not reconstructed effective flags.

Untouched CV 1101 real gate:

Before:

- rows 222,000
- distinct BASE rows 222,000
- missing BASE rows 0
- source `RECONSTRUCTED_NORMALIZED`
- avg stored flags 3214 bytes
- total stored flags 713,441,615 bytes
- effective hash `c7d1b19c4b2f7fd203fcb68f0bd3557e`

Materialization:

- status OK
- reconstructed 222,000
- inserted 222,000
- deleted stale 222,000
- shadow source `EXISTING_SCIENCE_MEASUREMENTS`
- shadow rows 222,000
- scalar mismatches 0
- mismatches 0
- write strategy `POSTGRESQL_COPY_STAGING`
- flags strategy `BASE_DELTA_EFFECTIVE_FLAGS_V1`
- flags source `SHADOW_BASELINE_EFFECTIVE_FLAGS`

After:

- rows 222,000
- distinct BASE rows 222,000
- missing BASE rows 0
- source `RECONSTRUCTED_NORMALIZED_SHADOW`
- avg stored flags 1905 bytes
- total stored flags 422,888,021 bytes
- **effective hash unchanged exactly**: `c7d1b19c4b2f7fd203fcb68f0bd3557e`

Logical flag payload reduction for this generation = **40.73%**, ~290.6 MB decimal / ~277 MiB.

Post-write `verify-science-materialization` = OK / zero scalar mismatches; frozen field-33 acceptance after CV1101 = READY.

Therefore 0.6.3.2 is user-real-validated for **lossless historical effective-flag-preserving science compaction**.

Do not spend time bulk-compacting all old SCIENCE generations merely to save ~7–8 GB; the current priority is a larger structural storage refactor.

## 7. New storage-model conclusion — conservative scientific retention

The user explicitly prefers the **conservative scientific-retention model**: final scientific photometry must remain in PostgreSQL as a durable, queryable dataset because it will be reused for future research. The goal is not to turn all science products into transient/reconstructed artifacts.

New target:

```text
one heavy immutable BASE row per object/frame
+
one narrow durable SCIENCE row per final science product/object/frame
+
normalized frame/calibration context
+
lossless archived verbose diagnostics where appropriate
```

The old target “BASE + full SCIENCE <= 2N heavy rows” is now considered too wasteful.

### 7.1. What SCIENCE really duplicates

A full-frame-independent sample of 52,051 science rows joined to BASE showed:

- `x` identical: 100.000%
- `y` identical: 100.000%
- `aperture_radius_pix`: 100.000%
- `local_background`: 100.000%
- `centroid_dx_pix`: 100.000%
- `centroid_dy_pix`: 100.000%

These are strong candidates to remove from physical SCIENCE storage and recover through `base_measurement_id`.

But these values are **not** duplicates and must remain part of the durable science result or be otherwise explicitly represented:

- `flux`: only 1.401% identical to BASE
- `flux_err`: 1.401%
- `mag_inst`: 1.401%
- `mag_err_random`: 59.930%
- `mag_err_systematic`: 75.430%
- `local_zp_correction`: 0.000%
- `mag_cal`/`mag_err` are inherently science-layer outputs and remain required.

Therefore do **not** replace durable science photometry with BASE-only reconstruction. Design a narrow `ScienceMeasurement V2` instead.

### 7.2. Candidate narrow science row

At minimum retain:

- calibration version id
- base measurement id
- object id (deliberately duplicated for fast object queries)
- frame id (deliberately duplicated for fast frame queries)
- science `flux`
- science `flux_err`
- science `mag_inst`
- `mag_cal`
- `mag_err`
- `mag_err_random`
- `mag_err_systematic`
- `local_zp_correction`
- compact object-level QC/flags
- materialization/provenance identity as needed

Do not blindly remove `object_id`/`frame_id` just because they can be reached through BASE; they are useful intentional denormalization for high-volume light-curve queries.

### 7.3. BASE `measurements` composition

Exact current rows by calibration product class:

- BASE_PHOTOMETRY / BASE / COMPLETE_IMMUTABLE: **10,088,095** rows, 115 versions
- ENSEMBLE / INTERMEDIATE / SUPERSEDED_IMMUTABLE: **900,000** rows, 18 versions
- ENSEMBLE / INTERMEDIATE / COMPLETE_IMMUTABLE: **600,000** rows, 12 versions
- LEGACY_UNCLASSIFIED / INTERMEDIATE / MATERIALIZING: **200,000** rows, 4 versions
- ENSEMBLE / SCIENCE / COMPLETE_IMMUTABLE: **100,000** rows, 2 versions

Thus **1.8 million / 15.14%** of `measurements` are not immutable BASE photometry. They are a future cleanup target, but only after a direct-reader/dependency audit and successful cutover to `CalibrationPhotometryView`/new storage.

### 7.4. BASE flags are likely another major saving

Earlier exact/sampled key audits show many `Measurement.flags` keys are constant inside `(calibration_version_id, frame_id)`, e.g. algorithm names, exposure/gain/read-noise settings, annulus parameters, zero-point/frame terms, error-model semantics. The average BASE flags payload was previously measured around 1.68 kB/row.

Preferred approach is **lossless factoring**, not deleting information:

```text
frame_context.flags = all keys whose value is identical for the whole calibration/frame
measurement.flags   = genuinely object-specific remainder
reader effective     = frame_context.flags || measurement.flags
```

Before implementation, run a full-row audit on 50–100 complete BASE frames rather than TABLESAMPLE-only inference, and quantify projected logical/physical savings.

Check whether existing normalized homes are already sufficient (`calibration_frame_terms.details`, calibration iterations/version metadata, frame QC fields). Do not introduce a new frame-context table until existing schema has been evaluated semantically and for read performance.

### 7.5. Detection/catalog-link data must be retained conservatively

Exact current counts:

- `source_detections = 6,925,992`
- `detection_catalog_matches = 5,573,857`
- `frame_catalog_links = 8,486,095`
- event-linked source detections = **0**

These tables are large (~14 GB combined), but they must **not** be deleted now.

Reasons:

1. The project goal includes future searches for unusual variables/transients; source detections may be scientifically valuable raw derived data.
2. Current code still reads `frame_catalog_links` from:
   - `grandgousier/catalogs/frame_match.py`
   - `grandgousier/catalogs/reference_photometry.py`
   - `grandgousier/interseries/catalog_identity.py`
   - `grandgousier/photometry/forced_aperture.py`
   - `grandgousier/photometry/adaptive_aperture.py`
   - `grandgousier/db/catalog_link_io.py`
   - pipeline/CLI/reset paths.

Long-term direction: archive/reorganize high-volume detection/link arrays into a compact lossless columnar artifact layer (e.g. Parquet+Zstd) **only after** readers and research use-cases have an explicit access contract. Keep searchable summaries/candidates/provenance in PostgreSQL. This is later than the ScienceMeasurement/Base-flags work.

## 8. Current implementation boundaries to inspect before next patch

Read these files physically before designing schema/code:

Core storage/model:

- `grandgousier/db/models.py`
- `grandgousier/db/schema_contract.py`
- `grandgousier/db/migrations.py`
- `grandgousier/resources/migrations/migrate_mvp5_40_2_science_measurements.sql`
- `grandgousier/resources/migrations/migrate_mvp5_40_13_science_measurement_index_cleanup.sql`

Science abstraction/materialization:

- `grandgousier/photometry/calibration_view.py`
- `grandgousier/photometry/science_flags.py`
- `grandgousier/photometry/science_materialization.py`
- `grandgousier/calibration/reconstruction.py`

Downstream readers:

- `grandgousier/interseries/planning.py`
- `grandgousier/interseries/analysis.py`
- `grandgousier/interseries/persistence.py`
- `grandgousier/lightcurves/global_object.py`
- `grandgousier/lightcurves/product.py`
- `grandgousier/lightcurves/target.py`
- `grandgousier/pipeline/runner.py`

BASE/detection/catalog paths:

- `grandgousier/photometry/forced_aperture.py`
- `grandgousier/photometry/adaptive_aperture.py`
- `grandgousier/photometry/source_detection.py`
- `grandgousier/catalogs/frame_match.py`
- `grandgousier/catalogs/reference_photometry.py`
- `grandgousier/db/catalog_link_io.py`
- `grandgousier/interseries/catalog_identity.py`

Tests:

- `tests/test_science_materialization.py`
- `tests/test_calibration_reconstruction.py`
- `tests/test_spatial_ensemble_normalized_reconstruction.py`
- Stage-3 planner/analysis/persistence tests
- M5/global-lightcurve tests
- schema/migration tests
- archive/Stage-1 tests as regression guard, although storage refactor must not change Stage 1.

## 9. Next engineering plan

### S0 — freeze and quantify before coding

1. Treat 0.6.3.2 + READY field-33 acceptance as the current safety baseline.
2. Do not bulk-compact old science generations yet.
3. Do not run `VACUUM FULL`, `CLUSTER`, bulk deletes, or `pg_repack` yet.
4. Build an exact storage projection using complete-frame samples and `pg_column_size`, not just theoretical column widths.

### S1 — full-frame BASE flag factoring audit

On 50–100 complete BASE `(calibration_version_id, frame_id)` groups:

- enumerate every flag key;
- classify exact constant-per-frame vs object-varying;
- calculate current payload bytes;
- calculate payload after exact frame factoring;
- calculate projected reduction percentage;
- identify whether each constant key already has a normalized authoritative home.

No writes.

### S2 — ScienceMeasurement V2 design

Prepare an evidence-based schema proposal for a **narrow durable science table**, preserving all values required for future scientific reuse.

Must answer:

- exact columns retained vs inherited from BASE;
- effective flag/QC representation;
- required indexes for object/frame/calibration access;
- whether old table is altered in place or a new additive table is introduced;
- how `CalibrationPhotometryView` presents the same public row regardless of v1/v2 storage;
- how migrations/backfill/parity are performed without destructive cutover.

Prefer additive migration + dual/read fallback rather than an in-place destructive ALTER as the first patch.

### S3 — prototype/additive implementation

Likely first structural patch after audit:

- introduce V2 storage or equivalent additive columns/table;
- support dual materialization for a controlled calibration;
- update `CalibrationPhotometryView` to read V2 first with v1/legacy/reconstruction fallback;
- add exact scalar + effective-QC parity tests;
- no deletion of old science table yet.

### S4 — real parity gate

Use a superseded/non-current calibration first, then frozen field-33 current products:

- row counts;
- exact/scalar equality;
- effective flags/QC equality;
- M5 lightcurve output equality;
- Stage-3 planning/graph unchanged;
- acceptance READY;
- physical/logical storage measurements.

### S5 — BASE flags factoring

After Science V2 is stable:

- decide authoritative frame-context storage using existing normalized schema where possible;
- factor constant BASE flag payload losslessly;
- preserve public `Measurement.flags`/view semantics through merge logic during compatibility period;
- audit all direct readers before cutover.

### S6 — legacy `measurements` cleanup

Only after reader cutover/parity:

- identify dependencies on the 1.8M non-BASE rows;
- verify none are authoritative/current;
- export/retain provenance if needed;
- remove only approved intermediate/legacy layers.

### S7 — detection/catalog archival architecture

Later and separately:

- define lossless columnar artifact schema and reader API;
- keep source detections scientifically accessible;
- replace live dependencies on `frame_catalog_links` before removing them from PostgreSQL;
- do not equate `event_linked_detections=0` with “safe to delete”.

### S8 — physical PostgreSQL reclamation

Only after all logical changes are complete and accepted:

- measure dead/free space and available disk headroom;
- choose `VACUUM FULL`, `pg_repack`, partition/table rewrite or other reviewed method;
- expect rewrite operations to need additional temporary disk and/or locks;
- perform one planned reclaim rather than repeatedly rewriting 25–30 GB tables during development.

## 10. Main traps

1. Do not confuse scalar reconstruction parity with exact historical flag parity; CV1094 proved they differ.
2. Do not infer that a value belongs in BASE simply because it is numerically equal in one sample; use semantic ownership plus full-frame statistics.
3. Do not remove science `flux/flux_err/mag_inst`: they are changed in ~98.6% of sampled rows.
4. Do not remove `local_zp_correction`: it differs from BASE in 100% of sampled rows.
5. Do not delete detection/link tables merely because they are large or have zero event links.
6. Do not make `science_measurements` fully reconstruct-on-demand; user explicitly wants durable science data for later research.
7. Do not make object/frame joins unnecessarily expensive by over-normalizing IDs out of the narrow science row.
8. Do not run physical reclaim before logical storage migration is complete.
9. Do not mutate frozen Stage-3 generation 20/21 semantics while changing storage.
10. Do not use path identity or alter RoboPhot UTC rule as part of storage work.
11. Keep old readers/legacy fallback for at least one compatibility release before dropping old rows/columns.
12. Any destructive cleanup requires explicit user agreement and a backup/maintenance plan.

## 11. Next-chat entry point

The next chat should begin by reading:

1. `CONTEXT.md`
2. `docs/context/CURRENT_STATE.md`
3. `docs/context/NEXT_TASKS.md`
4. `docs/context/NEXT_WORK_CHECKLIST.md`
5. `docs/context/HANDOFF_NEXT_CHAT_0_6_3_2_STORAGE_REFACTOR_RU.md`
6. `docs/architecture/DATA_MODEL_REFACTOR_TZ.md` — amended storage target at top
7. `context/project_state.yaml`

Then inspect the actual source files listed in section 8 before proposing the first structural patch.

## Архивный источник до консолидации: `docs/CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE.md`

# Grandgousier 0.5.58.0 — full-science acceptance layer

The science algorithms and database schema remain unchanged from 0.5.57.0. 0.5.58.0 adds a read-only acceptance layer above the real PostgreSQL science products.

`grandgousier.services.acceptance` loads a packaged dataset specification, requires a strict full-science doctor result, snapshots frozen database counters, uses the existing operational field-status contract for Stage 2/3, exports M5 controls into a temporary local directory, then snapshots database counters again. No persist/materialize/process command is called.

The first golden dataset is `grandgousier/resources/acceptance/gpx_tf17_2.json`. Release inspection requires this resource in wheel and `tools/acceptance_check.py` in sdist.

## Архивный источник до консолидации: `docs/README.md`

# Документация Grandgousier

## Для пользователя

- [`user_manual_ru/`](user_manual_ru/) — основной русскоязычный LaTeX-manual. Он начинается с быстрого старта и далее содержит полное описание программы.
- [`user_manual_ru/README.md`](user_manual_ru/README.md) — сборка manual и правила сопровождения.

## Для продолжения разработки

- `../CONTEXT.md` — входная точка для нового чата в этом архивном снимке; файл не входит в текущий source.
- [`context/CURRENT_STATE.md`](context/CURRENT_STATE.md) — текущее подтверждённое состояние.
- [`context/NEXT_TASKS.md`](context/NEXT_TASKS.md) — ближайшие задачи.
- [`context/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`](context/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) — известные проблемы.
- [`context/TEST_DATASETS.md`](context/TEST_DATASETS.md) — контрольные данные.
- [`context/COMMANDS.md`](context/COMMANDS.md) — рабочие команды.

## Архитектура и решения

- [`CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE.md`](CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) — фактическая архитектура кода.
- [`architecture/STAGE3_MULTI_SERIES_PLAN_RU.md`](architecture/STAGE3_MULTI_SERIES_PLAN_RU.md) — инженерная карта Stage 3: inter-series calibration и object history.
- [`decisions/`](decisions/) — ADR: причины решений, которые неочевидны из кода.

## История версий

Новые release notes хранятся в [`releases/`](releases/). Старые `README_MVP*.md` пока оставлены в корне для сохранения истории и ссылок; новые файлы такого формата создавать не следует.

## Правило обновления

При каждом патче отдельно проверяется влияние на пользовательский контракт. Если меняются CLI, параметры, workflow, migrations, продукты или интерпретация результатов, соответствующие файлы `docs/user_manual_ru/*.tex`/`chapters/*.tex` обновляются и включаются в тот же patch-only архив. Внутренняя оптимизация без изменения пользовательского поведения может не менять manual.

При завершении значимого патча нужно обновить:

1. версию в `pyproject.toml` и `grandgousier/__init__.py`;
2. `docs/context/CURRENT_STATE.md`;
3. `docs/context/NEXT_TASKS.md` и `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, если изменились;
4. `context/project_state.yaml`;
5. release note в `docs/releases/<version>.md`;
6. regression tests;
7. переносной bundle командой `python scripts/build_context_bundle.py`.

  status: implemented_pending_real_windows_rerun
  trigger: 0.5.44.10 reached spatial + candidate-excluded Object QC but failed downstream with ReconstructionStateError
  root_cause: spatial_v3 was FULL_MEASUREMENTS-only and had no CalibrationIteration/frame terms, while immutable reconstruction
    requires every derived chain stage to have normalized state
  behavior:
  - spatial materialization remains FULL_MEASUREMENTS for the controlled A/B
  - the same spatial model is dual-written as iteration_kind=SPATIAL_ENSEMBLE
  - linear coefficients use generic frame-term columns; quadratic coefficients and detector bounds use existing JSON details/parameters
  - reconstruction dispatches SPATIAL_ENSEMBLE before generic ENSEMBLE semantics and applies mag_out = mag_source - spatial_correction
  - mag_err/random/systematic values are preserved
  schema_migration: false
  scientific_model_changed: false
  validation: 84 targeted tests passed, 1 skipped
  next: rerun identical MASTER series 76/77 spatial_v3 A/B; no DB cleanup

## 2026-09-17 — 0.6.4.0 prepared: reconstructable SCIENCE cache cutover foundation

S2 production audit covered all 104 SCIENCE products / 10,151,494 rows. Sampled complete-frame scalar reconstruction matched stored SCIENCE for every product; all rows have valid BASE identity and `mag_err == mag_err_random` globally. Physical projection showed ~90% reduction when wide reconstructable state/JSON is omitted. 0.6.4.0 therefore adds `science_photometry_cache(calibration_version_id, base_measurement_id, mag_cal, mag_err_random)` as an explicitly rebuildable Stage-3 cache. Stage-3 readers prefer only complete cache generations and otherwise fall back to V1. No V1 deletion is part of this patch.

## 2026-09-17 — 0.6.4.0 real gate / 0.6.4.1 cache+reconstruction reader cutover prepared

0.6.4.0 migration applied cleanly on production (27 managed migrations, pending=0, checksum drift=0). Field 33 backfill created exactly 6,323,538 `science_photometry_cache` rows for 32 materialized SCIENCE products with zero scalar mismatches; 14 products without V1 rows remained `NO_V1_SCIENCE_ROWS`. Frozen `gpx_tf17_2` acceptance stayed `READY`, including exact Stage-3 generations and M5 controls. 0.6.4.1 then prepared a reversible read cutover: M5/global-object and current alias-head lightcurves can read complete cache plus normalized reconstruction, while missing/partial/historical-ineligible cache falls back to V1. No schema change or V1 deletion is included.



## 2026-09-17 — 0.6.4.1 real gate / 0.6.4.2 compact SCIENCE writer cutover prepared

0.6.4.1 was real-validated on production field 33. Both M5 controls read through `SCIENCE_CACHE_RECONSTRUCTED`: object 29786 remained 2640 source / 2578 accepted / 62 rejected with 22 `NO_VALID_MAG` + 40 `SATURATED_OR_NEAR_SATURATED`; object 30112 remained 2640 / 2618 / 22 with 22 `NO_VALID_MAG`. Frozen `gpx_tf17_2` acceptance remained `READY`.

0.6.4.2 prepares the write-side cutover. Normal SCIENCE finalization now materializes only `science_photometry_cache(calibration_version_id, base_measurement_id, mag_cal, mag_err_random)` directly from authoritative BASE + normalized calibration terms. Wide `science_measurements` is no longer written by default and becomes an explicit compatibility/debug output under the existing `--materialize-intermediate-calibrations` option. Historical V1 rows are retained; no destructive cleanup or physical reclaim is part of this patch. MASTER processed-prune recognizes either compact cache or legacy V1 as retained science evidence.


## 2026-09-17 — 0.6.4.2 real writer gate and 0.6.4.3 historical flag-override foundation

0.6.4.2 was real-validated by rebuilding superseded CV1094 directly from normalized provenance into 222,000 `science_photometry_cache` rows while leaving its 222,000 legacy V1 rows unchanged; frozen field-33 acceptance remained READY. S3 then sampled 215,997 rows across 36 field-33 SCIENCE calibrations: scalar/identity parity was exact, lossless top-level historical flag patches had zero failures, and a naive sparse patch projection used 151.1 MiB versus 609.5 MiB for sampled V1 rows (75.2% saving). Because most differences repeat per calibration, 0.6.4.3 was designed with a calibration-common patch manifest plus sparse per-BASE residuals rather than a full patch on every row.


## 2026-09-18 — 0.6.4.3 real all-row override gate and 0.6.4.4 retirement preparation

Production field 33 completed exact historical override backfill and verification for all 36 materialized SCIENCE products / 7,211,538 V1 rows. Every product returned zero scalar, identity and flag mismatches; manifest residual counts matched actual storage. The compatibility layer contained 36 manifests and 426,349 residual rows (~76 MiB) while compact cache was ~575 MiB and retained wide `science_measurements` remained ~31 GiB. Frozen acceptance remained READY. 0.6.4.4 therefore introduced fail-closed calibration-scoped retirement: complete cache, exact manifest, fresh all-row verification and no inbound FK references are mandatory before V1 DELETE; successful retirement preserves exact historical flags under `RETIRED_EXACT`.

## 0.6.4.5 — global materialized SCIENCE retirement scope (prepared 2026-09-18)

After user-real validation of 0.6.4.4, field 33 had all 7,211,538 legacy wide `science_measurements` rows retired with 36 `RETIRED_EXACT` manifests and frozen acceptance still READY. The database retained 2,939,956 V1 rows outside field 33. Version 0.6.4.5 adds an explicit `--all-materialized` scope to compact-cache backfill, historical flag override backfill/verification, and controlled retirement. The scope is mutually exclusive with field or explicit calibration selection, includes only immutable SCIENCE products that still physically own V1 rows, and never implies execution; destructive deletion still requires `--execute`.

## 2026-09-18 — 0.6.4.5.1 global-scope PostgreSQL bind hotfix

The first production launch of 0.6.4.5 `backfill-science-photometry-cache --all-materialized` failed before any writes with PostgreSQL/psycopg `AmbiguousParameter`: the selector used `(:field_id IS NULL OR cv.field_id = :field_id)` while binding `field_id=None`, so PostgreSQL could not infer the NULL parameter type. 0.6.4.5.1 removes nullable scope binds entirely: global materialized scope and field scope now use separate SQL statements. The same fix is applied proactively to the historical flag-override selector. No schema, science formulas, cache semantics, override semantics, or retirement safety gates changed.
## 2026-10-11 — A2/B .8 SOURCE-ONLY (P2-07 OPEN/PARTIAL)

At unchanged HEAD `8a370d65cad383337d2a55d8ec72aecf0ddb18e3` new managed source .8 brings manifest to **37 / 21 managed**; existing .4/.5/.6/.7 SQL and earlier user changes remain untouched. New deferred reference→membership and immediate SCIENCE-CV field/pair+triple FKs with two immediate CV parent uniques join unchanged A1 five edge FKs, reference RESTRICT, member generation CASCADE/series-only SET NULL and ID-only CV RESTRICT. Triple MATCH SIMPLE skips nullable membership series, pair still validates field. No role/lifecycle freeze or scientific formula/selection change. Source/runtime now expects .7/.8 while last independently observed TEST remained ledger 35 with .4/.5/.6 APPLIED, .7/.8 absent and old three edge FKs; no new DB observation. Ordinary `migrate-db` may commit .7 before .8 and leave PARTIAL on .8 failure. Five ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks plus ledger SHARE, two index builds, 5s lock/30s statement timeouts are not a total bound. No DB connection/query/SQL execution or Git commit here, no verified backup/PITR, physical-byte parity, live PostgreSQL parser/application or new DB-write approval. P2-07 OPEN/PARTIAL; `READY_FOR_DB_WRITE=NO`, `READY_FOR_EXECUTE=NO`, `READY_FOR_MIGRATION_APPLICATION=NO`.
